fields.setting: $Y$ is projective with Gorenstein canonical singularities.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $\dim Y\le4$ and ${E_{\mathrm{st}}}(Y;u,v)$ is polynomial.
fields.statement: $$\term{stringy-hodge}{h_{\mathrm{st}}^{p,q}}(Y)\ge0\qquad\text{for all }p,q.$$
fields.proof: The cases of dimension at most three are known. In dimension four, Olano's inequality ${h_{\mathrm{st}}^{p,1}}(Y)\ge0$, symmetry, and duality leave only [[str-thm-1-2|Theorem 1.2]].

fields.setting: $Y$ is a complex projective Gorenstein canonical fourfold.
fields.proof: On a crepant terminal model, [[str-prop-4-6|Proposition 4.6]] gives the middle coefficient as $\term{intersection-middle}{I_Y}+\term{discrepancy-count}{n}+\term{total-cokernel}{\epsilon}-\sum_\alpha\term{delta}{\delta_\alpha}$. The bound in [[str-prop-5-1|Proposition 5.1]] makes this at least $\term{intersection-middle}{I_Y}+\term{total-cokernel}{\epsilon}\ge0$.

notations.intersection-middle: The dimension of an intersection cohomology term.
notations.discrepancy-count: The number of discrepancy-one exceptional divisors.
notations.total-cokernel: The sum of the certain cokernel dimensions over the point fibers.
notations.delta: The number of independent defect classes fixed by monodromy.

fields.setting:
$Y$ is a complex projective Gorenstein terminal fourfold, with adapted resolution $f:X\to Y$ as in [[str-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1]].

Write $D=\bigcup_iD_i$ and $K_{X/Y}=\sum_i {a_i}D_i$. Let ${B}$ be the omitted curve points, ${S}$ the isolated singular points, and ${E_q}=f^{-1}(q)_{\mathrm{red}}$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
{I_Y}&={h^{2,2}}({\operatorname{IH}}^4(Y,\mathbb Q)),\\
{n}&=\#\{i:{a_i}=1\},\\
{\delta_\alpha}&=\dim\card{str-def-4-2}{\Delta_{\alpha,x}}^{\term{monodromy}{G_\alpha}},\\
{\epsilon}&=\sum_{q\in {B}\cup {S}}\dim\operatorname{coker}\!\left(H^4(\term{point-components}{E_q^{[1]}})\longrightarrow H^4(\term{point-intersections}{E_q^{[2]}})\right).
\end{aligned}
$$
fields.statement: $$[u^2v^2]\term{stringy-e}{E_{\mathrm{st}}}(Y)={I_Y}+{n}+{\epsilon}-\sum_\alpha{\delta_\alpha}.$$
fields.proof: Combine the resolution and exceptional-stratum cohomology formulas. [[str-lemma-4-4|Lemma 4.4]] turns the monodromy contribution into $\sum_\alpha\delta_\alpha$, and [[str-lemma-4-7|Lemma 4.7]] cancels the boundary terms.

notations.monodromy: The finite group recording monodromy action.
notations.point-components: The disjoint union of the components of the exceptional point fiber.
notations.point-intersections: The disjoint union of pairwise intersections of exceptional point-fiber components.

fields.setting:
$Y$ is a complex projective Gorenstein terminal fourfold, with $f:X\to Y$ as in [[str-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1]].

Write 
$$K_{X/Y}=\sum_i {a_i}D_i,\qquad {\delta_\alpha}=\dim\card{str-def-4-2}{\Delta_{\alpha,x}}^{\term{monodromy}{G_\alpha}},\qquad {I_\alpha}=\{i:f({D_i})={C_\alpha}\}.$$
fields.statement:
For each curve ${C_\alpha}$,
$${\delta_\alpha}\le {n_\alpha},\qquad {n_\alpha}=\#\{i\in {I_\alpha}:{a_i}=1\}.$$
fields.proof: [[str-lemma-5-5|Lemma 5.5]] and [[str-lemma-5-6|Lemma 5.6]] identify $\delta_\alpha$ with the rational class-group rank of $\term{completed-ring}{\widehat{\mathcal O}_\alpha}$. Using [[str-lemma-5-3|Lemma 5.3]], a small $\mathbb Q$-factorialization bounds this rank by its contracted curves; blowing up each curve gives a distinct discrepancy-one divisor counted by $n_\alpha$.

notations.monodromy: The finite group recording monodromy action.
notations.completed-ring: The completed transverse local ring at the generic point of the singular curve.

fields.setting: $Y$ is a complex projective Gorenstein terminal fourfold with singular curve locus $C=\bigcup_\alpha C_\alpha$.
fields.statement:
There exist a projective log resolution $f:X\to Y$ and pairwise disjoint connected smooth dense opens ${U_\alpha}\subset {C_\alpha}$ with the following properties. Write ${C}=\bigcup_\alpha {C_\alpha}$, ${U}=\coprod_\alpha {U_\alpha}$, and ${B}={C}\setminus {U}$; horizontal exceptional divisors dominate curves, and vertical ones map to points.

1. $f^{-1}({U})$ lies in the horizontal exceptional divisors. Horizontal single, double, and triple strata restrict to smooth proper maps over the ${U_\alpha}$.
2. No horizontal double or triple stratum maps to a point; no horizontal quadruple stratum meets $f^{-1}({U})$.
3. A general hyperplane through $x\in {U_\alpha}$ gives a terminal threefold ${Z_x}$ with isolated singularities, and snc exceptional surface
$${E_x}=f^{-1}(x)_{\mathrm{red}}.$$
4. For $d\in {B}$, ${E_d}$ is precisely the vertical exceptional divisors above $d$.
fields.proof: Generic smoothness and Bertini give the good curve opens and transverse slices. Principalizing the bad-point ideals with snc centers makes their fibers divisorial; dimension counts then exclude horizontal strata collapsing to points.

fields.setting:
$Y$ is a complex projective Gorenstein terminal fourfold, with $f:X\to Y$ as in [[str-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1]].

Choose a point $x\in {U_\alpha}$. Let ${E_x}=\bigcup_jE_{x,j}$ be the exceptional surface, and ${L_x}$ its link.
fields.statement:
The following sequences are exact:

$$0\longrightarrow H^2({E_x})\xrightarrow{{\rho_x}}H^2(\term{slice-components}{E_x^{[1]}})\xrightarrow{{\partial_x}}H^2(\term{slice-intersections}{E_x^{[2]}})\longrightarrow0,$$

$$0\longrightarrow H_4({E_x})(-3)\xrightarrow{{\kappa_x}}H^2({E_x})\longrightarrow H^2({L_x})\longrightarrow0.$$

All terms have pure Hodge type $(1,1)$. The first maps are restriction and alternating restriction, and

$${\kappa_x}([{E_{x,j}}])=c_1\!\left(\mathcal O_{{\widetilde Z_x}}({E_{x,j}})|_{{E_x}}\right).$$
fields.proof: Friedman–Laza's local cohomology sequences and duality give exactness. Compatibility with restriction and Gysin maps, together with the Hodge types of the curve and link terms, gives purity.

notations.slice-components: The disjoint union of the exceptional surface components.
notations.slice-intersections: The disjoint union of pairwise intersections of the exceptional surface components.

fields.setting:
$Y$ is a complex projective Gorenstein terminal fourfold, with $f:X\to Y$ as in [[str-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1]]. Let ${f_\alpha^\circ}:{D_\alpha^\circ}\to {U_\alpha}$ be the exceptional family. Set
$$
\begin{aligned}
{\mathcal V_\alpha^2}&=R^2({f_\alpha^\circ})_*\mathbb Q,&
{\mathcal V_\alpha^{21}}&=R^2(({f_\alpha^\circ})^{[1]})_*\mathbb Q,\\
{\mathcal V_\alpha^{22}}&=R^2(({f_\alpha^\circ})^{[2]})_*\mathbb Q,&
{\mathcal V_\alpha^{01}}&=(({f_\alpha^\circ})^{[1]})_*{\mathbb Q(-1)}.
\end{aligned}
$$
fields.statement:
On ${U_\alpha}^{\mathrm{an}}$ there are exact sequences of local systems

$$0\to{\mathcal V_\alpha^{2,\mathrm{an}}}\to{\mathcal V_\alpha^{21,\mathrm{an}}}\to{\mathcal V_\alpha^{22,\mathrm{an}}}\to0,$$

$$0\to{\mathcal V_\alpha^{01,\mathrm{an}}}\xrightarrow{\term{family-gysin}{\boldsymbol\kappa_\alpha}}{\mathcal V_\alpha^{2,\mathrm{an}}}\to{\mathcal D_\alpha^{\mathrm{an}}}\to0,\qquad ({\mathcal D_\alpha^{\mathrm{an}}})_x\cong\card{str-def-4-2}{\Delta_{\alpha,x}}.$$
fields.proof: Smooth proper strata from [[str-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1]] produce local systems. Proper base change identifies their stalk maps with [[str-lemma-4-1|Lemma 4.1]], so exactness holds throughout the family.

notations.family-gysin: The family of maps assigning cohomology classes to exceptional divisors.

fields.setting:
$Y$ is a complex projective Gorenstein terminal fourfold, with $f:X\to Y$ as in [[str-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1]].
Let
$${m_\alpha}=\dim H^0({U_\alpha}^{\mathrm{an}},\term{component-system}{\mathcal V_\alpha^{21,\mathrm{an}}}),\qquad {c_{h,\alpha}}=|{I_\alpha}|,$$ and ${c_{hh,\alpha}}$ counts connected horizontal double strata.
fields.statement:
The monodromy image ${G_\alpha}$ of $\term{component-system}{\mathcal V_\alpha^{21,\mathrm{an}}}$ is finite, and the other systems in Lemma 4.3 factor through it. Moreover,

$${\delta_\alpha}=\dim H^0({U_\alpha}^{\mathrm{an}},\term{defect-system}{\mathcal D_\alpha^{\mathrm{an}}})=\dim\card{str-def-4-2}{\Delta_{\alpha,x}}^{{G_\alpha}},$$

$${m_\alpha}={c_{h,\alpha}}+{c_{hh,\alpha}}+{\delta_\alpha},\qquad {m}={c_h}+{c_{hh}}+\sum_\alpha{\delta_\alpha}.$$

The invariant spaces $H^0({U_\alpha}^{\mathrm{an}},R^2(f_i^\circ)_*\mathbb Q)$ have type $(1,1)$.
fields.proof: The purity in [[str-lemma-4-1|Lemma 4.1]] makes the polarized integral lattice definite, hence its monodromy finite. Taking invariants in [[str-lemma-4-3|Lemma 4.3]] is exact over $\mathbb Q$; counting the connected strata gives the identities.

notations.component-system: Second cohomology of the individual exceptional surface components.
notations.defect-system: The family of local defect spaces along $U_\alpha$.

fields.setting:
$Y$ is a complex projective Gorenstein terminal fourfold, with $f:X\to Y$ as in [[str-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1]].

${c_{hv}}$ counts connected horizontal–vertical double strata, and
$$
{r_B}=\sum_{d\in {B}}\sum_{\widetilde d\in{\nu}^{-1}(d)}\dim H^4(E_{x_{\widetilde d}})^{{T_{\widetilde d}}},\qquad
{\kappa_B}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{hor}}}\sum_{\widetilde d\in{\nu}^{-1}({B})}\dim {K^{-1}_{\widetilde d,i}}.
$$

The map ${\nu}$ normalizes ${C}$, $x_{\widetilde d}$ is a nearby good point on that branch, and ${T_{\widetilde d}}$ is its local monodromy. Each ${K^{-1}_{\widetilde d,i}}$ is the point-supported summand of ${}^pH^{-1}(R\widetilde f_{i*}\mathbb Q_{{D_i}}[3])$ for the map ${\widetilde f_i}$ to the normalized curve.

Cohomology has rational coefficients.
fields.statement:
$${c_{hv}}={r_B}+{\kappa_B}.$$

Each ${K^{-1}_{\widetilde d,i}}$ has pure type $(1,1)$.
fields.proof: The decomposition theorem splits the top cohomology of each special fiber into monodromy invariants and a point-supported term. Relative hard Lefschetz identifies the latter correction, and counting the fiber components gives $c_{hv}=r_B+\kappa_B$.

fields.setting:
$Y$ is a complex projective Gorenstein terminal fourfold, with $f:X\to Y$ as in [[str-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1]].

$${\eta_\alpha}\in {C_\alpha},\quad {K_\alpha}=\mathbb C({C_\alpha}),\quad{\mathcal O_\alpha}=\mathcal O_{Y,{\eta_\alpha}},\quad{\widehat S_\alpha}=\operatorname{Spec}{\widehat{\mathcal O}_\alpha},$$

where ${\eta_\alpha}$ is the generic point, and ${D_{\alpha,i}}$ is the generic fiber of ${D_i}\to {C_\alpha}$.
fields.statement:
The completed ring is a three-dimensional complete excellent normal Gorenstein terminal domain with regular punctured spectrum. Base change gives a projective log resolution $\widehat g_\alpha:{\widehat X_\alpha}\to{\widehat S_\alpha}$, preserving the closed fiber. Its exceptional divisors are exactly

$${\widehat D_{\alpha,i}}\cong {D_{\alpha,i}}\quad(i\in {I_\alpha}),\qquad a({\widehat D_{\alpha,i}},{\widehat S_\alpha})={a_i}.$$
fields.proof: Localization and excellent completion give regular base changes; completion preserves the residue field and hence the closed fiber and its prime divisors. [[str-lemma-5-4|Lemma 5.4]] preserves discrepancies.

fields.setting: Consider a Cartesian square of Noetherian schemes $Z'=Z\times_W W'$, with projections $\psi':Z'\to Z$, $\varphi':Z'\to W'$.
fields.hypotheses:
Suppose $\varphi:Z\to W$ is proper, $\psi:W'\to W$ is flat, and

$$\term{duality-pullback}{\varphi^!}\mathcal O_W\cong\mathcal O_Z(K_{Z/W})$$

for a relative canonical Cartier divisor $K_{Z/W}$.
fields.statement:
A relative canonical Cartier divisor for $\varphi'$ is

$$K_{Z'/W'}=(\psi')^*K_{Z/W}.$$
fields.proof: Flatness makes the square Tor-independent. Proper duality base change identifies $(\varphi')^!\mathcal O_{W'}$ with the pullback of $\term{duality-pullback}{\varphi^!}\mathcal O_W$, giving the claimed divisor.

notations.duality-pullback: The duality pullback that carries relative canonical information.

cards.title: Lemma 5.5 (Defect and the geometric class group)

fields.setting:
$Y$ is a complex projective Gorenstein terminal fourfold, with $f:X\to Y$ as in [[str-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1]].

Take ${\mathcal O_\alpha}=\mathcal O_{Y,{\eta_\alpha}}$, and a separable closure ${\overline K_\alpha}$ of ${K_\alpha}=\mathbb{C}(C_\alpha)$. Let ${\mathcal O_\alpha^{\mathrm{sh}}}$ be the strict henselization and ${G_{K_\alpha}}=\operatorname{Gal}({\overline K_\alpha}/{K_\alpha})$.

On ${U_\alpha}^{\mathrm{\acute et}}$, let ${\mathcal D_\alpha^{\mathrm{\acute et}}}$ be the cokernel of the map sending exceptional divisors to their line bundles in the relative Picard sheaf.
fields.statement:
$$({\mathcal D_\alpha^{\mathrm{\acute et}}})_{{\overline\eta_\alpha}}\cong{\operatorname{Cl}}({\mathcal O_\alpha^{\mathrm{sh}}})\otimes\mathbb Q$$

naturally and ${G_{K_\alpha}}$-equivariantly. Consequently,

$$\card{str-def-4-2}{\Delta_{\alpha,x}}^{{G_\alpha}}\cong\left({\operatorname{Cl}}({\mathcal O_\alpha^{\mathrm{sh}}})\otimes\mathbb Q\right)^{{G_{K_\alpha}}}.$$
fields.proof: The relative Picard–class-group sequence identifies the étale cokernel with the geometric class group. Rationality, the exponential sequence, and [[str-lemma-4-1|Lemma 4.1]] identify its analytic fiber with the local defect; finite-cover comparison then identifies the invariant spaces.

fields.setting:
$Y$ is a complex projective Gorenstein terminal fourfold, with $f:X\to Y$ as in [[str-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1]].

Use the completed and strictly henselian generic local rings ${\widehat{\mathcal O}_\alpha}$ and ${\mathcal O_\alpha^{\mathrm{sh}}}$.
fields.statement: $${\operatorname{Cl}}({\widehat{\mathcal O}_\alpha})\otimes\mathbb Q\cong\left({\operatorname{Cl}}({\mathcal O_\alpha^{\mathrm{sh}}})\otimes\mathbb Q\right)^{{G_{K_\alpha}}}.$$
fields.proof: The henselian and completed class groups agree. [[str-lemma-5-3|Lemma 5.3]] gives regular punctured spectra, where class groups are Picard groups; Galois descent obstructions disappear after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$.

fields.setting:
Let ${q_0},{q_1}\in\mathbb C[x_0,\ldots,x_3]$ be quadrics and ${c}$ a cubic. Set ${C}=V({q_0},{q_1})\subset\mathbb P^3$ and
$${Y}=V(sq_0(x)+tq_1(x)+{c}(x))\subset\mathbb P^5,\qquad {X_n}={Y}\times(\mathbb P^1)^{{n}}.$$
fields.hypotheses: Suppose the forms are general, ${C}$ is smooth, and ${n}\ge1$.
fields.statement:
${X_n}$ is a complex projective Gorenstein terminal variety of dimension ${n}+4$, with polynomial $\term{stringy-e}{E_{\mathrm{st}}}$ and

$$\term{stringy-hodge}{h_{\mathrm{st}}^{2,3}}({X_n})=-1.$$
fields.proof: A direct computation of a log resolution by blow-up and the stringy $E$-function yields the negative stringy Hodge number. The construction is inspired by the 7-dimensional counterexample of Satriano-Usatine.

fields.setting: Fix the adapted resolution of [[str-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1]], a component ${C_\alpha}$, and $x\in {U_\alpha}$. Let ${E_x}$ be the exceptional surface over ${Z_x}$, with link ${L_x}$.
fields.definition:
$$\Delta_{\alpha,x}:=\operatorname{coker}({\kappa_x})\cong H^2({L_x},\mathbb Q),$$

where

$${\kappa_x}:H_4({E_x},\mathbb Q)(-3)\longrightarrow H^2({E_x},\mathbb Q),\qquad [{E_{x,j}}]\longmapsto c_1\!\left(\mathcal O_{{\widetilde Z_x}}({E_{x,j}})|_{{E_x}}\right).$$

This records exceptional-fiber cohomology not accounted for by exceptional divisor classes.

fields.setting: $f=h+F:(\mathbb C^n,0)\to(\mathbb C,0)$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. $${\mathcal X_m}=\{\gamma\in{\mathcal L_m(\mathbb C^n)}:\gamma(0)=0,\ f(\gamma(t))\equiv t^m\pmod{t^{m+1}}\}.$$ $\phi$ is the Milnor monodromy.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $2\le d<n/2$ or $d>2n-2$.
fields.statement: $$H_c^{j+(n-1)(2m+1)}(\mathcal X_m;\mathbb Z)\cong\term{floer}{\operatorname{HF}^{j}}(\phi^{m},+;\mathbb Z)\qquad(j\in\mathbb Z).$$
fields.proof: Apply [[cl-thm-4-2|Theorem 4.2]]: in these degree ranges, the two numerical conditions hold for every $m$, so the corresponding compactly supported and Floer cohomology groups agree.

notations.floer: Floer cohomology of the iterated Milnor monodromy.

fields.setting: $f=h+F:(\mathbb C^n,0)\to(\mathbb C,0)$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. The [[cl-def-5-2|dlt, contact, and essential $m$-valuations]] belong to the triple $(\mathbb C^n,\operatorname{div}(f),\{0\})$.
fields.statement: $$\begin{array}{c|ccc}&\mathrm{dlt}&\mathrm{contact}&\mathrm{essential}\\\hline d<n&0&\mathbf1_{m\ge d}&\lfloor m/d\rfloor\\ d\ge n&\lfloor m/d\rfloor&\lfloor m/d\rfloor&\lfloor m/d\rfloor\end{array}$$ In the second row the three sets coincide. Contact valuations correspond to irreducible components of the {{unrestricted|unrestricted contact locus}}.
fields.proof: [[cl-prop-5-4|Proposition 5.4]] identifies the contact valuations, [[cl-prop-5-11|Proposition 5.11]] identifies the dlt valuations, and [[cl-cor-5-13|Corollary 5.13]] identifies the essential valuations.

notations.unrestricted: Contact locus with arbitrary nonzero leading coefficient.

fields.setting: $f:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C$ is homogeneous of degree $d\ge2$, with an isolated singularity at $0$, where $n\ge3$, $m\ge1$. $${\mathcal X_m}=\{\gamma\in{\mathcal L_m(\mathbb C^n)}:\gamma(0)=0,\ f(\gamma(t))\equiv t^m\pmod{t^{m+1}}\}.$$
fields.hypotheses:
For every integer $1\le k<m/d$,

$$2k(d-n)+1\notin\{\pm1,\pm(n-1),\pm(n-2),\pm(2n-3)\}.$$

$$2k(d-n)\notin\{0,\pm(n-2),\pm(n-1)\}.$$
fields.statement: $$H_c^{j+(n-1)(2m+1)}(\mathcal X_m;\mathbb Z)\cong{\operatorname{HF}^{j}}({\phi}^{m},+;\mathbb Z)\quad(j\in\mathbb Z).$$
fields.proof: Use [[cl-prop-4-1|Proposition 4.1]] together with the divisor indexing and degree shifts from [[cl-thm-2-11|Theorem 2.11]]. [[cl-cor-2-9|Corollary 2.9]] lists the possible homology degrees; two columns in the same total degree would violate the second numerical condition. Each filtration therefore has at most one nonzero layer per degree, eliminating extension ambiguity.

fields.setting: $f$ is homogeneous of degree $d\ge2$ with an isolated singularity at $0\in\mathbb C^n$, where $n\ge3$, $m\ge1$. $F$ is the order filtration on the restricted contact locus, and $A$ is the action filtration on Floer cohomology.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $$2k(d-n)+1\notin\{\pm1,\pm(n-1),\pm(n-2),\pm(2n-3)\}\quad(1\le k<m/d,\ k\in\mathbb Z).$$
fields.statement: $${\operatorname{gr}_F}H_c^{j+(n-1)(2m+1)}({\mathcal X_m};\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{gr}_A{\operatorname{HF}^{j}}(\term{phi}{\phi}^{m},+;\mathbb Z)\qquad(j\in\mathbb Z).$$
fields.proof: The two first pages agree after reindexing and the degree shift. [[cl-thm-2-11|Theorem 2.11]] and [[cl-thm-3-6|Theorem 3.6]] make both sequences degenerate, giving the same associated graded groups.

fields.setting: $f=h+F$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ on $\mathbb C^n$, of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. Blow up the origin, then repeatedly blow up divisor intersections whose multiplicities sum to at most $m$. The resulting chain resolution has $S=\{h=0\}\subset\mathbb P^{n-1}$ and exceptional divisors ${E_{(\kappa,r)}}$. Label the first exceptional divisor $(0,1)$ and the strict transform $(1,0)$; each later label is the sum of its two parents.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $$2k(d-n)+1\notin\{\pm1,\pm(n-1),\pm(n-2),\pm(2n-3)\}\quad(1\le k<m/d,\ k\in\mathbb Z).$$
fields.statement: The McLean spectral sequence for this resolution degenerates at $E_1$. Its first page is $$E_1^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{\substack{E\text{ exceptional},\ N_E\mid m\\mb_E/N_E=p}}H_{n-1-(p+q)-2m(\nu_E/N_E-1)}(\term{cover}{\widetilde E^\circ};\mathbb Z),$$ where ${N_E}$, ${\nu_E}$ and ${b_E}$ are the multiplicities, log discrepancies and ample-divisor coefficients. It converges to ${\operatorname{HF}^{*}}({\phi}^{m},+)$.
fields.proof: [[cl-lemma-2-10|Lemma 2.10]] orders the columns along the chain, and [[cl-cor-2-9|Corollary 2.9]] lists their possible homology degrees. A nonzero differential between columns $i<j$ would force $2(j-i)(d-n)+1$ into the excluded set.

notations.cover: The Denef–Loeser cyclic cover of the divisor stratum.

fields.setting: $f=h+F$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ on $\mathbb C^n$, of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. Blow up the origin, then repeatedly blow up divisor intersections whose multiplicities sum to at most $m$. The resulting chain resolution has $S=\{h=0\}\subset\mathbb P^{n-1}$ and exceptional divisors ${E_{(\kappa,r)}}$. ${b}=\operatorname{rank}H^{n-2}(S;\mathbb Z)$ and ${\mu(h)}=(d-1)^n$. Label the first exceptional divisor $(0,1)$ and the strict transform $(1,0)$; each later label is the sum of its two parents.
fields.statement: For the first exceptional divisor, $$H_a(\term{cover}{\widetilde E_{(0,1)}^\circ};\mathbb Z)=\begin{cases}\mathbb Z&a=0,\\\mathbb Z^{\mu(h)}&a=n-1,\\0&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$ For every other exceptional divisor the only nonzero integral homology groups are $$\begin{array}{c|cc}a&n\text{ odd}&n\text{ even}\\\hline0&\mathbb Z&\mathbb Z\\n-2&\mathbb Z^b\oplus\mathbb Z/d&\mathbb Z^{b-1}\\n-1&\mathbb Z^b&\mathbb Z^{b-1}\\2n-3&\mathbb Z&\mathbb Z\end{array}$$ Here $$b=(-1)^{n-1}2\left\lceil\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rceil+\sum_{a=0}^{n-2}(-1)^a\binom na d^{n-1-a}.$$
fields.proof: [[cl-prop-2-4|Proposition 2.4]] identifies the first cover with the Milnor fiber, a bouquet of $(n-1)$-spheres. For the others, [[cl-prop-2-7|Proposition 2.7]] gives the Euler class for the Thom–Gysin sequence; [[cl-lemma-2-8|Lemma 2.8]] controls its middle-degree map, and Poincaré duality gives the displayed homology.

notations.cover: The Denef–Loeser cyclic cover of the divisor stratum.

fields.setting: $f=h+F$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ on $\mathbb C^n$, of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. Set $S=\{h=0\}\subset\mathbb P^{n-1}$, and let $E_{(0,1)}$ be the first exceptional divisor.
fields.statement: The degree-$d$ Denef–Loeser cover of $E_{(0,1)}^\circ\cong\mathbb P^{n-1}\setminus S$ is homeomorphic to $${M_h}=\{x\in\mathbb C^n:h(x)=1\}.$$
fields.proof: On every line through a point $[a]\in\mathbb P^{n-1}\setminus S$, the equation $t^dh(a)=1$ has exactly $d$ solutions. These local root covers are exactly the covers glued in the Denef–Loeser construction.

fields.setting: $f=h+F$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ on $\mathbb C^n$, of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. Blow up the origin, then repeatedly blow up divisor intersections whose multiplicities sum to at most $m$. The resulting chain resolution has $S=\{h=0\}\subset\mathbb P^{n-1}$ and exceptional divisors ${E_{(\kappa,r)}}$. Label the first exceptional divisor $(0,1)$ and the strict transform $(1,0)$; each later label is the sum of its two parents. Write $\eta=c_1(\mathcal O_S(1))$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $(\kappa,r)\ne(0,1),(1,0)$.
fields.statement: The map $$\widetilde\pi:\term{cover}{\widetilde E_{(\kappa,r)}^\circ}\longrightarrow S$$ is a $\mathbb C^\times$-bundle with Euler class $\pm{\eta}$, according to orientation.
fields.proof: [[cl-prop-2-5|Proposition 2.5]] supplies the punctured line bundle before covering. The coprime-multiplicity monodromy of [[cl-lemma-2-6|Lemma 2.6]] makes the degree-$N$ cover connected on each fiber; dividing its Euler class $\pm N\eta$ by the fiber-cover degree gives $\pm\eta$.

notations.cover: The Denef–Loeser cyclic cover of the divisor stratum.

fields.setting: $f=h+F$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ on $\mathbb C^n$, of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. Blow up the origin, then repeatedly blow up divisor intersections whose multiplicities sum to at most $m$. The resulting chain resolution has $S=\{h=0\}\subset\mathbb P^{n-1}$ and exceptional divisors ${E_{(\kappa,r)}}$. Label the first exceptional divisor $(0,1)$ and the strict transform $(1,0)$; each later label is the sum of its two parents.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $(\kappa,r)\ne(0,1),(1,0)$.
fields.statement: $E_{(\kappa,r)}\to S$ is a $\mathbb P^1$-bundle with two disjoint sections supplied by its adjacent divisors. Removing one section gives a line bundle with Euler class $$\pm(\kappa+rd){\eta}.$$ Removing both gives its punctured line bundle.
fields.proof: At a blow-up center the two normal lines are $\mathcal O_S(\kappa^{\prime}+r^{\prime}d)$ and $\mathcal O_S(-\kappa^{\prime\prime}-r^{\prime\prime}d)$. Projectivizing their sum and tensoring by either inverse identifies the complement of a section with $\mathcal O_S(\pm(\kappa+rd))$; induction starts from $\mathcal O_S(d)$ and $\mathcal O_S(-1)$.

fields.setting: $E_{(\kappa,r)}$ is an intermediate exceptional divisor of the chain resolution.
fields.statement: The cyclic cover $\widetilde E_{(\kappa,r)}^\circ$ is path connected.
fields.proof: Adjacent multiplicities remain coprime throughout the blow-ups. A small loop about an adjacent divisor acts on the $N$ sheets by a coprime rotation, so its iterates join every sheet; paths in the base then connect the entire cover.

fields.setting: $S\subset\mathbb P^{n-1}$ is a smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface, $n\ge3$, with ${\eta}=c_1(\mathcal O_S(1))$.
fields.statement: $$H^{n-2}(S;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\smile\eta}H^n(S;\mathbb Z)$$ is surjective.
fields.proof: For odd $n$ the target vanishes. For even $n$, deform to a Fermat hypersurface containing a linear subspace of dimension $(n-2)/2$; its Poincaré-dual class pairs to $1$ with the appropriate hyperplane power and produces a generator of the target.

fields.setting: In the chain resolution, $N_E$ is the multiplicity of $f$ along $E$, and $E_{(0,1)}$ is the first exceptional divisor.
fields.statement: There is an ample divisor $H=\sum_E{b_E}E$ with integral $b_E\le0$ such that $$\frac{b_E}{N_E}<\frac{b_{E^{\prime}}}{N_{E^{\prime}}}$$ whenever $E$ lies closer to $E_{(0,1)}$ than $E^{\prime}$ along the chain.
fields.proof: Start with minus the first exceptional divisor. After blowing up an adjacent intersection, take a sufficiently large multiple of the pullback of the old ample divisor minus the new exceptional divisor; its new ratio lies strictly between the two old neighboring ratios.

fields.setting: $f=h+F:(\mathbb C^n,0)\to(\mathbb C,0)$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. $${\mathcal X_m}=\{\gamma\in{\mathcal L_m(\mathbb C^n)}:\gamma(0)=0,\ f(\gamma(t))\equiv t^m\pmod{t^{m+1}}\}.$$ The order filtration is ${F_p\mathcal X_m}=\{\gamma\in\mathcal X_m:\operatorname{ord}_t\gamma\ge-p\}$, with ${F_{(p)}\mathcal X_m}=F_p\mathcal X_m\setminus F_{p-1}\mathcal X_m$. Set $\rho=-p$.
fields.statement: The piece is empty unless $1\le\rho\le\lfloor m/d\rfloor$. Otherwise: (i) $\gamma_0,\ldots,\gamma_{\rho-1}=0$; (ii) the leading coefficient lies in $$\begin{cases}{CS^\circ}=\{h=0\}\setminus\{0\},&d\rho<m,\\{M_h}=\{h=1\},&d\rho=m;\end{cases}$$ (iii) each $\gamma_a$, $\rho<a\le m-(d-1)\rho$, is constrained to an affine hyperplane modeled on the tangent space of that leading-coefficient variety; (iv) $\gamma_{m-(d-1)\rho+1},\ldots,\gamma_m$ are free. The successive affine bundles depend holomorphically on the lower coefficients.
fields.proof: Expand $f(\gamma(t))$: its first coefficient is $h(\gamma_\rho)$, and each later relevant equation is linear in its newest coefficient with linear part $Dh(\gamma_\rho)$. Smoothness away from the vertex makes that linear form nonzero, yielding the affine bundles and free final coefficients.

fields.setting: $f=h+F$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ on $\mathbb C^n$, of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. $${\mathcal X_m}=\{\gamma\in{\mathcal L_m(\mathbb C^n)}:\gamma(0)=0,\ f(\gamma(t))\equiv t^m\pmod{t^{m+1}}\}.$$ The order filtration is ${F_p\mathcal X_m}=\{\gamma\in\mathcal X_m:\operatorname{ord}_t\gamma\ge-p\}$, with ${F_{(p)}\mathcal X_m}=F_p\mathcal X_m\setminus F_{p-1}\mathcal X_m$. Blow up the origin, then repeatedly blow up divisor intersections whose multiplicities sum to at most $m$. The resulting chain resolution has $S=\{h=0\}\subset\mathbb P^{n-1}$ and exceptional divisors ${E_{(\kappa,r)}}$. For the ample coefficients from [[cl-lemma-2-10|Lemma 2.10]], put $$G_a\mathcal X_m=\bigsqcup_{\substack{E\text{ exceptional},\ N_E\mid m\\mb_E/N_E\le a}}\mathcal X_{m,E},$$ where $\mathcal X_{m,E}$ consists of jets whose lifted arcs meet $E^\circ$. Label the first exceptional divisor $(0,1)$ and the strict transform $(1,0)$; each later label is the sum of its two parents.
fields.statement: There is an increasing reindexing $\iota:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$ with $F_p\mathcal X_m=G_{\iota(p)}\mathcal X_m$. In particular, $\mathcal X_{m,E_i}$ consists precisely of jets of order $-i$.
fields.proof: The indexing in the proof of [[cl-thm-2-11|Theorem 2.11]] orders the divisor columns. Intersecting a lifted arc with a general hyperplane gives $\operatorname{ord}_t\gamma=mr_E/N_E=-i$ on $E_i$, so the divisor pieces and order pieces coincide.

fields.setting: $f=h+F:(\mathbb C^n,0)\to(\mathbb C,0)$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. $${\mathcal X_m}=\{\gamma\in{\mathcal L_m(\mathbb C^n)}:\gamma(0)=0,\ f(\gamma(t))\equiv t^m\pmod{t^{m+1}}\}.$$ The order filtration is ${F_p\mathcal X_m}=\{\gamma\in\mathcal X_m:\operatorname{ord}_t\gamma\ge-p\}$, with ${F_{(p)}\mathcal X_m}=F_p\mathcal X_m\setminus F_{p-1}\mathcal X_m$.
fields.statement: The integral compact-support spectral sequence $$E_1^{p,q}=H_c^{p+q}(F_{(p)}\mathcal X_m;\mathbb Z)\Longrightarrow H_c^{p+q}(\mathcal X_m;\mathbb Z)$$ degenerates at $E_1$.
fields.proof: [[cl-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1]] bounds the nonempty columns. [[cl-lemma-3-3|Lemma 3.3]] makes an auxiliary-space comparison the identity on a differential’s source, while [[cl-lemma-3-4|Lemma 3.4]] identifies its target map with a bundle inclusion. [[cl-lemma-3-5|Lemma 3.5]] turns that map into multiplication by the normal Euler class, which vanishes because the punctured cone is a smooth principal hypersurface.

fields.setting: Set $\rho=-p$, $k=m-(d-1)(\rho-\ell)$, and $${Z}=(\term{pi}{\pi^m_{k-1}})^{-1}(\pi^m_{k-1}(\mathcal X_m)),\qquad F_rZ=Z\cap F_r\mathcal L_m.$$
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $\ell\ge1$ with $F_{(p)}\mathcal X_m$ and $F_{(p+\ell)}\mathcal X_m$ nonempty.
fields.statement: $$F_{(r)}Z=F_{(r)}\mathcal X_m\qquad(r<p+\ell).$$
fields.proof: [[cl-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1(ii)]] makes every coefficient beyond $m-(d-1)(-r)$ free on the earlier piece. Since this cutoff is below $k$, freeing coefficients from $k$ onward changes none of those pieces.

fields.setting: Set $\rho=-p$, $k=m-(d-1)(\rho-\ell)$, and $${Z}=(\term{pi}{\pi^m_{k-1}})^{-1}(\pi^m_{k-1}(\mathcal X_m)),\qquad F_rZ=Z\cap F_r\mathcal L_m.$$ Here $CS^\circ=\{h=0\}\setminus\{0\}$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $\ell\ge1$ with $F_{(p)}\mathcal X_m$ and $F_{(p+\ell)}\mathcal X_m$ nonempty.
fields.statement: On the piece $F_{(p+\ell)}$, the coordinates $\gamma_{k+1},\ldots,\gamma_m$ form a common free factor $\mathbb C^{n(m-k)}$. After removing it, the inclusion $$\pi_k^m(F_{(p+\ell)}\mathcal X_m)\hookrightarrow\pi_k^m(F_{(p+\ell)}Z)$$ is, after choosing an affine-bundle origin, the pullback of $$T_{{CS^\circ}}\hookrightarrow T_{\mathbb C^n}|_{CS^\circ}$$ by the leading-coefficient map to $CS^\circ$.
fields.proof: As in [[cl-lemma-3-3|Lemma 3.3]], the higher coefficients form a common free factor. [[cl-prop-3-1|Proposition 3.1]] identifies the final constrained coefficient with an affine tangent hyperplane, while in $Z$ it ranges through all of $\mathbb C^n$; these are the two pullback bundles.

fields.setting: $0\to V^{\prime}\xrightarrow{i}V\to V^{\prime\prime}\to0$ is an exact sequence of compatibly oriented real vector bundles of ranks $r^{\prime},r,r^{\prime\prime}$ on a paracompact base $B$, with compact-support Thom isomorphisms.
fields.statement: Under these isomorphisms, $$i^*:H_c^j(V)\longrightarrow H_c^j(V^{\prime})$$ is $$H_c^{j-r}(B)\xrightarrow{\smile{e(V^{\prime\prime})}}H_c^{j-r^{\prime}}(B).$$
fields.proof: Split the sequence using a bundle metric. Multiplicativity of Thom classes and restriction along the zero section replace the quotient bundle’s Thom class by its Euler class.

fields.setting: $f=h+F$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ on $\mathbb C^n$, of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. Blow up the origin, then repeatedly blow up divisor intersections whose multiplicities sum to at most $m$. The resulting chain resolution has $S=\{h=0\}\subset\mathbb P^{n-1}$ and exceptional divisors ${E_{(\kappa,r)}}$. For $-\lfloor m/d\rfloor\le i\le-1$, let $$\mathcal X_{m,i}^{\infty}=\{\gamma\in{\mathcal X_m^\infty}:\operatorname{ord}_t\gamma=-i\}.$$ Label the first exceptional divisor $(0,1)$ and the strict transform $(1,0)$; each later label is the sum of its two parents.
fields.statement: If $d<n$, only $E_{-1}$ gives a [[cl-def-5-2|contact $m$-valuation]] when $m\ge d$; none exists when $m<d$. If $d\ge n$, every exceptional $m$-divisor $E_i$ gives one.
fields.proof: [[cl-prop-3-2|Proposition 3.2]] identifies the order pieces with divisor pieces. The recalled codimension theorem (Proposition 5.1) gives $\operatorname{codim}\mathcal X_{m,i}^{\infty}=m+i(d-n)$; semicontinuity excludes containment in one direction, and these codimensions or the $m-d+n$ defining equations decide the other.

fields.setting: $f=h+F$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ on $\mathbb C^n$, of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. Blow up the origin, then repeatedly blow up divisor intersections whose multiplicities sum to at most $m$. The resulting chain resolution has $S=\{h=0\}\subset\mathbb P^{n-1}$ and exceptional divisors ${E_{(\kappa,r)}}$. Label the first exceptional divisor $(0,1)$ and the strict transform $(1,0)$; each later label is the sum of its two parents.
fields.statement: If $d<n$, the triple has no [[cl-def-5-2|dlt $m$-valuations]]. If $d\ge n$, all exceptional $m$-divisors $E_i$ of the chain resolution give dlt $m$-valuations.
fields.proof: The discrepancy formula excludes dlt valuations when $d<n$. For $d\ge n$, [[cl-prop-2-5|Proposition 2.5]] describes the ruled divisors, [[cl-lemma-5-7|Lemma 5.7]] reduces relative nefness to their fibers and curves on the first divisor, and [[cl-lemma-5-9|Lemma 5.9]] computes the required intersections. The relative canonical divisor is nef, so the dlt-modification criterion applies.

fields.setting: $f=h+F$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ on $\mathbb C^n$, of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. Blow up the origin, then repeatedly blow up divisor intersections whose multiplicities sum to at most $m$. The resulting chain resolution has $S=\{h=0\}\subset\mathbb P^{n-1}$ and exceptional divisors ${E_{(\kappa,r)}}$. Label the first exceptional divisor $(0,1)$ and the strict transform $(1,0)$; each later label is the sum of its two parents.
fields.statement: The [[cl-def-5-2|essential $m$-valuations]] are exactly the valuations of the exceptional $m$-divisors $$E_i,\qquad-\lfloor m/d\rfloor\le i\le-1.$$
fields.proof: [[cl-prop-5-12|Proposition 5.12]] forces every $m$-separating resolution to dominate this one. Each of its exceptional $m$-divisors therefore remains divisorial on every such resolution, and essential valuations must already occur on this resolution itself.

fields.setting: $f=h+F$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ on $\mathbb C^n$, of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. The chain resolution blows up the origin, then repeatedly blows up divisor intersections whose multiplicities sum to at most $m$.
fields.statement: The chain resolution $\mu:X\to\mathbb C^n$ is minimal among {{separating|$m$-separating log resolutions}} of $(\mathbb C^n,\operatorname{div}(f),\{0\})$: every other such resolution factors through $\mu$.
fields.proof: The normal-crossing divisorial inverse image of the origin forces factorization through the first blow-up. At each subsequent adjacent intersection with multiplicity sum at most $m$, the separating condition forces the next blow-up as well; the universal property of blowing up supplies the successive factorizations.

notations.separating: Divisors with multiplicity sum at most $m$ are disjoint.

fields.setting: $\pi:\mathbb P(\mathcal F)\to W$ is the projective bundle of a rank-two vector bundle, and $\sigma$ is a section.
fields.statement: For a curve $C$ mapping onto a curve in $W$, $$[C]=\deg(\pi|_C)[\sigma(\pi(C))]+\pi^*\alpha_0$$ in rational Chow groups, for some $\alpha_0\in A_0(W)_{\mathbb Q}$. A curve contained in a fiber contributes only a fiber class.
fields.proof: The projective-bundle formula writes every curve class as a section contribution plus a pullback of a zero-cycle. Pushing forward by $\pi$ fixes the section coefficient to be the degree of the map on $C$.

fields.setting: $W$ is smooth, $D\subset W$ is a smooth divisor, and $Z\subset D$ is a smooth center. The blow-up $\beta:\operatorname{Bl}_Z W\to W$ has exceptional divisor $E$ and strict transform $\widetilde D$.
fields.statement: $${\mathcal N_{\widetilde D/\operatorname{Bl}_Z W}}\cong(\beta|_{\widetilde D})^*\mathcal N_{D/W}\otimes\mathcal O_{\widetilde D}(-E|_{\widetilde D}).$$
fields.proof: The total-transform equality $\beta^*D=\widetilde D+E$ gives the corresponding line-bundle identity. Restrict to $\widetilde D$ and identify the divisor line bundles with the normal bundles.

fields.setting: $f=h+F$ is a holomorphic [[cl-def-2-3|semihomogeneous]] germ on $\mathbb C^n$, of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$ and $m\ge1$. Blow up the origin, then repeatedly blow up divisor intersections whose multiplicities sum to at most $m$. The resulting chain resolution has $S=\{h=0\}\subset\mathbb P^{n-1}$ and exceptional divisors ${E_{(\kappa,r)}}$. $E=E_{(\kappa,r)}$ is intermediate, born from parents $(\kappa^{\prime},r^{\prime})$ and $(\kappa^{\prime\prime},r^{\prime\prime})$ in left-to-right order. Put $a=\kappa^{\prime}+r^{\prime}d$, $b=\kappa^{\prime\prime}+r^{\prime\prime}d$, so $E=\mathbb P(\mathcal O_S(a)\oplus\mathcal O_S(-b))$. Label the first exceptional divisor $(0,1)$ and the strict transform $(1,0)$; each later label is the sum of its two parents.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose its intersections on the left and right are subsequently blown up $s$ and $t$ times.
fields.statement: $$\begin{aligned}\mathcal N_{E/X}\cong{}&\mathcal O_E(-1)\\&\otimes(\mathcal O_E(1)\otimes\pi^*\mathcal O_S(-b))^{-s}\\&\otimes(\mathcal O_E(1)\otimes\pi^*\mathcal O_S(a))^{-t}.\end{aligned}$$ Its degree on a ruling fiber is $-1-s-t$. The final neighbor labels are $(\kappa^{\prime},r^{\prime})+s(\kappa,r)$ and $(\kappa^{\prime\prime},r^{\prime\prime})+t(\kappa,r)$.
fields.proof: The normal bundle starts as $\mathcal O_E(-1)$. Compute the line bundles of the two sections from the tautological inclusion, then apply [[cl-lemma-5-8|Lemma 5.8]] at each later blow-up meeting a section; label addition counts the two exponents.

fields.setting: $f\in\mathbb C\llbracket x_1,\ldots,x_n\rrbracket$ is a formal power series.
fields.definition: $f$ is **semihomogeneous of degree $d$** if $$f=h+F,$$ where $h$ is homogeneous of degree $d$, has an isolated critical point at $0$, and $\operatorname{ord}_0F>d$. For Milnor monodromy and Floer cohomology, $f$ is a convergent holomorphic germ.

fields.setting: $Y$ is a smooth complex variety, $D$ is a nonzero effective divisor, $\varnothing\ne\Sigma\subset D_{\mathrm{red}}$ is closed, and $m\ge1$.
fields.definition:
An **$m$-valuation** is $v=\operatorname{ord}_E$ for a prime divisor on an $m$-separating log resolution of $(Y,D,\Sigma)$ with $N_E\mid m$.

For reduced $D$, a **dlt $m$-valuation** is an $m$-valuation represented by a divisor over $\Sigma$ on a dlt modification of $(Y,D)$.

A **contact $m$-valuation** is an $m$-valuation for which the closure of the arcs lifting to $E^\circ$ is an irreducible component of the unrestricted contact locus.

An **essential $m$-valuation** is an $m$-valuation whose center on every $m$-separating log resolution is a prime divisor over $\Sigma$.

There exist universal series $A_{\mu,
