[[esv-cor-3-7|Corollary 3.7]]
[[esv-cor-1-13|Corollary 1.13]]
fields.proof: Toric localization and [[esv-lemma-3-6|Lemma 3.6]] eliminate higher poles in the logarithm of the auxiliary genus; [[esv-lemma-4-1|Lemma 4.1]] eliminates the insertion-independent remainder. Extract the obstruction factor $c_1(S)$, take the limits in [[esv-lemma-3-3|Lemma 3.3]], and exponentiate; polynomial dependence on rank extends the formulas to K-theory classes.

fields.setting: $S=\mathbb C^2$, $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_S\langle y_j\rangle$, and $\alpha\in K_{\mathsf T}(S)$ has rank $r$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $N>0$ and $\lambda_1=\lambda$, $\lambda_2=-\lambda$. Use the {{esv-red|reduced obstruction theory}}.
fields.statement:
For the universal series of [[esv-thm-3-5|Theorem 3.5]],

$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal S^{\mathrm{red}}(E,\alpha;q)&=\sum_{\mu,\nu,\xi}\log A_{\mu,\nu,\xi}(q)\,J_{\mu,\nu,\xi},\\
\mathcal V^{\mathrm{red}}(E,\alpha;q)&=\sum_{\mu,\nu,\xi}\log B_{\mu,\nu,\xi}(q)\,J_{\mu,\nu,\xi},\\
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{red}}(E,\alpha;q)&=\sum_{\mu,\nu,\xi}\log C_{\mu,\nu,\xi}(q)\,J_{\mu,\nu,\xi},\\
J_{\mu,\nu,\xi}&=\left.\int_S\term{esv-cmu}{c_\mu(\alpha)}c_\nu(S)c_\xi(E)\right|_{\lambda_2=-\lambda_1}.
\end{aligned}$$

The constant terms are zero.

[[esv-cor-1-15|Corollary 1.15]]
[[esv-cor-1-16|Corollary 1.16]]
[[esv-conj-1-17|Conjecture 1.17]]
fields.proof: [[esv-cor-3-10|Corollary 3.10]] removes one factor of $\lambda_1+\lambda_2$ before specialization. Expanding the exponential in [[esv-thm-3-5|Theorem 3.5]], only its linear term survives this operation.

notations.esv-red: Remove one trivial obstruction direction; the series starts at $n=1$.

fields.setting:
$S=\mathbb C^2$, $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_S\langle y_j\rangle$, and $\alpha\in K_{\mathsf T}(S)$ has rank $r$.

For the series in [[esv-thm-3-5|Theorem 3.5]], set

$$\begin{aligned}
L_A^{k_1,k_2}&=k_1!k_2!\sum_{|\mu|=k_1,|\xi|=k_2}\term{esv-binpart}{\binom r\mu}\binom N\xi\log A_{\mu,(0),\xi}(q),\\
L_C^{k_1,k_2}&=k_1!k_2!\sum_{|\mu|=k_1,|\xi|=k_2}\binom r\mu\binom N\xi\log C_{\mu,(0),\xi}(q),\\
L_B^{k_1,k_2}&=k_1!k_2!r^{k_1}\sum_{|\xi|=k_2}\binom N\xi\log B_{\term{esv-ones}{(1)_{k_1}},(0),\xi}(q).
\end{aligned}$$
fields.statement:
For $k\ge1$,

$$\begin{aligned}
L_A^{k_1,k_2}&=-r\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\term{esv-falling}{(-n(r+N))_{(k-1)}}}{n}\binom{-nr-1}{nN-1}q^n,\\
L_B^{k_1,k_2}&=-r^k\sum_{n\ge1}n^{k-2}\binom{-nr-1}{nN-1}((-1)^Nq)^n,\\
L_C^{k_1,k_2}&=r\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(n(r-N))_{(k-1)}}n\binom{nr-1}{nN-1}q^n.
\end{aligned}$$

Binomial coefficients use their polynomial extension for negative upper arguments. For $k=0$,

$$\begin{aligned}
\log A_{(0),(0),(0)}^{N,r}(q)&=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac1{n^2}\binom{-nr}{nN-1}q^n,\\
\log C_{(0),(0),(0)}^{N,r}(q)&=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac1{n^2}\binom{nr}{nN-1}q^n,\\
\log B_{(0),(0),(0)}^{N,r}(q)&=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(-1)^{nN-1}}{n^2}\binom{-nr-1}{nN-1}q^n.
\end{aligned}$$

[[esv-cor-4-4|Corollary 4.4]]
fields.proof: Apply [[esv-lemma-4-1|Lemma 4.1]] to the compact Quot coefficient formula, then take the Chern and Verlinde limits of [[esv-lemma-3-3|Lemma 3.3]]. Extracting coefficients gives the binomial expressions; integration gives the $k=0$ case, and polynomial dependence on rank determines its integration constant.

notations.esv-ones: The partition of $k$ into ones; empty for $k=0$.

fields.setting:
$L_A,L_B$ are the universal logarithmic coefficients in [[esv-thm-4-3|Theorem 4.3]].

Set

$$\varphi(t)=\log(1+t),\qquad\psi(t)=\frac Nt+\frac r{1+t},\qquad D_\psi=\psi(t)^{-1}\frac d{dt}.$$

For the $N$ {{esv-puiseux|Newton–Puiseux solutions}} $H_i^N=q(1+H_i)^{-r}$, put

$$D_{\mathcal S}^{(k)}=\bigl(-(r+N)D_\psi\bigr)_{(k-1)},\qquad D_{\mathcal V}^{(k)}=r^{k-1}D_\psi^{k-1}.$$

The operator falling factorial uses commuting shifts.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $N,r>0$, $k_1,k_2\ge0$, and $k=k_1+k_2\ge1$.
fields.statement:
$$\begin{aligned}
L_A^{k_1,k_2}(q)&=-r\sum_{i=1}^N(D_{\mathcal S}^{(k)}\varphi)(H_i),\\
L_B^{k_1,k_2}((-1)^Nq)&=-r\sum_{i=1}^N(D_{\mathcal V}^{(k)}\varphi)(H_i).
\end{aligned}$$

For $k=0$, use the zero-constant-term antiderivative convention; $D_\psi^{-1}h=\int_0^t\psi(u)h(u)\,du$. For degree $-1$, see [[esv-thm-4-3|Theorem 4.3]]; continue in rank at $r=0$.
fields.proof: Lagrange inversion converts the coefficient sums in [[esv-thm-4-3|Theorem 4.3]] into sums of $\varphi(H_i)$. Differentiating $H_i^N=q(1+H_i)^{-r}$ gives $q\,dH_i/dq=1/\psi(H_i)$, so each $q\,d/dq$ becomes $D_\psi$ after composition.

notations.esv-puiseux: The $N$ formal roots tending to zero, expanded in powers of $q^{1/N}$.

fields.setting: $X=\mathbb C^4$ and $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_X\langle y_j\rangle$.
fields.hypotheses: $N>0$. The torus satisfies $t_1t_2t_3t_4=1$.
fields.statement:
For any orientation and twisted virtual structure sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}^{\mathrm{vir}}$,

$$\mathsf E=\det\bigl((E^\vee)^{[n]}\bigr),\qquad\mathcal O^{\mathrm{vir}}=\widehat{\mathcal O}^{\mathrm{vir}}\otimes\mathsf E^{1/2}.$$

$$\mathcal O^{\mathrm{vir}}\in K_0\bigl(\operatorname{Quot}_X(E,n),\mathbb Z\bigr).$$

It defines the [[esv-def-5-4|fourfold Verlinde series]].
fields.proof: In the isotropic-section presentation of the Quot scheme, the square-root determinant of the isotropic bundle is integral. The remaining factor in $\widehat{\mathcal O}^{\mathrm{vir}}$ is $\det((E^\vee)^{[n]})^{-1/2}$, which the specified twist cancels.

cards.title: Corollary 1.4 (The Chern series of a line bundle)

fields.setting: $S=\mathbb C^2$, $L=\mathcal O_S\langle v\rangle$ is an equivariant line bundle, and $w=c_1(L)$.
fields.statement:
The [[esv-def-3-2|virtual Chern series]] is

$$\mathcal C_S(\mathcal O_S,L;q)=(1-q)^{-\int_S c(L)c_1(S)}=(1-q)^{-\frac{(1+w)(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)}{\lambda_1\lambda_2}},$$

[[esv-cor-4-2|Corollary 4.2]]
fields.proof: Compute the rank-two nonvirtual Chern series using [[esv-lemma-4-1|Lemma 4.1]], then specialize one summand to have Chern root $c_1(K_S)-1$ and replace $q$ by $-q$. Its Chern factor becomes the Hilbert-scheme obstruction Euler class, giving the virtual series.

fields.setting: $S=\mathbb C^2$.
fields.statement: $$1+\sum_{n\ge1}q^n\int_{[\operatorname{Hilb}^n(S)]^{\mathrm{vir}}}1=\exp\!\left(q\frac{\lambda_1+\lambda_2}{\lambda_1\lambda_2}\right).$$
fields.proof: Take the lowest weight-degree part of each $q^n$ coefficient in [[esv-cor-1-4|Corollary 1.4]]. Only the product of $n$ copies of the linear $q$ term contributes to degree $-n$.

fields.setting: $S=\mathbb C^2$, $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_S\langle y_j\rangle$, and $\alpha\in K_{\mathsf T}(S)$ has rank $r$.
fields.statement:
For [[esv-thm-3-5|the universal series]],

$$A_{\mu,\nu,\xi}(q)=B_{\mu,\nu,\xi}((-1)^Nq)\qquad\text{if }|\mu|+|\nu|+|\xi|=1.$$

For the [[esv-def-1-3|degree-zero parts]] of the full series,

$$\mathcal S_{S,0}(E,\alpha;q)-\mathcal V_{S,0}(E,\alpha;(-1)^Nq)=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{f_n}{(\lambda_1\lambda_2)^{n-2}}\left(\int_S c_1(S)\right)^2q^n,$$

$f_n$ is homogeneous of weight degree $2n-2$, depending on the rank and Chern classes of $\alpha$.
fields.proof: Toric localization identifies the degree-zero factors of [[esv-thm-3-5|Theorem 3.5]] with the compact Segre–Verlinde correspondence [Boj21a, Theorem 1.7](https://arxiv.org/html/2303.14266v2#bib.bibx4). After exponentiating, every remaining term in the difference contains at least two factors of $c_1(S)$.

fields.setting: $S=\mathbb C^2$, $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_S\langle y_j\rangle$, and $V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathcal O_S\langle v_i\rangle$.
fields.statement:
For the [[esv-thm-3-5|universal series]] indexed by ranks $N,r$,

$$A^{N,r}_{\mu,\nu,\xi}((-1)^Nq)=A^{r,N}_{\xi,\nu,\mu}((-1)^rq)\quad\text{if }|\mu|+|\nu|+|\xi|=1.$$

$$\mathcal S_{S,0}(E,V;(-1)^Nq)-\mathcal S_{S,0}(V,E;(-1)^rq)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{g_n}{(\lambda_1\lambda_2)^{n-2}}\left(\int_S c_1(S)\right)^2q^n,$$

with $g_n$ homogeneous of weight degree $2n-2$.
fields.proof: Toric localization identifies the degree-zero factors of [[esv-thm-3-5|Theorem 3.5]] with the compact Segre symmetry [Boj21a, Theorem 1.6](https://arxiv.org/html/2303.14266v2#bib.bibx4). Every remaining term after exponentiating contains at least two factors of $c_1(S)$.

fields.setting: $S=\mathbb C^2$, $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_S\langle y_j\rangle$, and $\alpha\in K_{\mathsf T}(S)$ has rank $r$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $N>0$ and $\lambda_1+\lambda_2=0$.
fields.statement:
For the [[esv-def-1-3|degree −1 parts]],

$$\mathcal S^{\mathrm{red}}_{-1}(E,\alpha;q)=\mathcal V^{\mathrm{red}}_{-1}(E,\alpha;(-1)^Nq).$$

If $\alpha=V$ is a rank-$r>0$ equivariant vector bundle, then also

$$\mathcal S^{\mathrm{red}}_{-1}(E,V;(-1)^Nq)=\mathcal S^{\mathrm{red}}_{-1}(V,E;(-1)^rq).$$
fields.proof: [[esv-thm-3-11|Theorem 3.11]] expresses the reduced series linearly in the same logarithmic factors, with degree lowered by one. Apply [[esv-cor-3-7|Corollary 3.7]] to the correspondence and [[esv-cor-1-13|Corollary 1.13]] to the symmetry.

fields.setting: $A_{\mu,\xi}=A_{\mu,(0),\xi}(q)$ and $B_{\mu,\xi}=B_{\mu,(0),\xi}((-1)^Nq)$ are the universal series in [[esv-thm-3-5|Theorem 3.5]].
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $N>0$ and $r\ge0$.
fields.proof: In [[esv-thm-4-3|Theorem 4.3]], set $(k_1,k_2)=(2,0),(1,1),(0,2)$ and compare the Segre and sign-adjusted Verlinde coefficient sums. Exponentiation gives the three identities.

fields.setting: $S=\mathbb C^2$, $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_S\langle y_j\rangle$, and $\alpha\in K_{\mathsf T}(S)$ has rank $r$. Write $c_1(\alpha)=a\lambda$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $N,r>0$, $\lambda_1=\lambda=-\lambda_2$, and all framing weights $m_j=0$.
fields.statement:
In the degree-zero part,

$$\left.\mathcal V^{\mathrm{red}}_0(E,\alpha;q)\right|_{m_j=0}=B_1(q)a^2+B_0(q).$$

For every $n>0$,

$$[q^n]B_1(q)=-\frac12\binom{n(N+r)-1}{nr}.$$
fields.proof: [[esv-thm-3-11|Theorem 3.11]] identifies $B_1=-\log B_{(1,1),(0),(0)}$. Setting $(k_1,k_2)=(2,0)$ in [[esv-thm-4-3|Theorem 4.3]] and simplifying the negative binomial coefficient gives the formula.

fields.setting: $F(\vec x,\vec y)\in\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_m]$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $m>0$ and $F$ is symmetric separately in $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ and $y_1,\ldots,y_m$.
fields.statement: $F$ is a polynomial in symmetric polynomials of $\{y_j\}$ and $\{x_i+y_j\}_{i,j}$.
fields.proof: Expand in the elementary symmetric basis in $\vec y$ and induct on degree. It remains to recover generators in $\vec x$; expanding power sums of $\{x_i+y_j\}$ gives $m\,p_k(\vec x)$ plus terms already determined by lower degrees, so division by $m$ completes the induction.

fields.setting: $H(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ is a formal series, possibly with additional formal parameters.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $r\ge0$ and $H$ is symmetric in $z_1,\ldots,z_r$.
fields.statement:
Write

$$H(ze^{x_1},\ldots,ze^{x_r})=\sum_\mu H_\mu(z)e_\mu(x_1,\ldots,x_r).$$

For every $k\ge0$,

$$\left(z\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\right)^kH_{(0)}(z)=k!\sum_{|\mu|=k}\term{esv-binpart}{\binom r\mu}H_\mu(z),\qquad e_\mu=\prod_j e_{\mu_j}.$$
fields.proof: The identity is preserved by addition and multiplication, so it suffices to check power sums. For $H=p_n$, the left side is $rn^kz^n$; expanding $p_k(\vec x)$ in elementary symmetric functions and evaluating at $x_1=\cdots=x_r=1$ gives the same value on the right.

fields.setting: $S=\mathbb C^2$, $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_S\langle y_j\rangle$, and $V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathcal O_S\langle v_i\rangle$.
fields.statement:
The equivariant auxiliary genus is

$$\mathcal N_S(E,V;q,z)=\sum_{n\ge0}q^n\chi^{\mathrm{vir}}\!\left(\operatorname{Quot}_S(E,n),\Lambda_{-z}V^{[n]}\right).$$

$\rho_\varepsilon$ replaces each additive weight $\lambda_i,m_j,w_i$ by its negative $-\varepsilon$ multiple. Then

$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal C_S(E,V;q)&=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\rho_\varepsilon\mathcal N_S\!\left(E,V;(-1)^Nq\varepsilon^{N-r}(1+\varepsilon)^r,(1+\varepsilon)^{-1}\right),\\
\mathcal V_S(E,V;q)&=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\mathcal N_S\!\left(E,V;(-1)^rq\varepsilon^r,\varepsilon^{-1}\right).
\end{aligned}$$
fields.proof: At each fixed point, $1-e^{-\varepsilon x}/(1+\varepsilon)=\varepsilon(1+x)+O(\varepsilon^2)$ turns the numerator into Chern factors; the denominator contributes $(-\varepsilon)^{Nn}e(T_Z^{\mathrm{vir}})$. In the other limit, the highest exterior-power term is the determinant, and the stated rescaling cancels its power of $\varepsilon$.

fields.setting: $S=\mathbb C^2$, $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_S\langle y_j\rangle$, and $V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathcal O_S\langle v_i\rangle$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $N>0$ and $n>0$.
fields.statement:
$\mathcal N^{\mathrm{red}}$ uses the reduced virtual tangent class. Then

$$\begin{aligned}
[q^n]\mathcal N^{\mathrm{red}}(E,V;q,z)&=\lim_{\lambda_2\to-\lambda_1}\frac{[q^n]\mathcal N_S(E,V;q,z)}{1-e^{-(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)}}\\
&=\lim_{\lambda_2\to-\lambda_1}\frac{[q^n]\mathcal N_S(E,V;q,z)}{\lambda_1+\lambda_2}.
\end{aligned}$$
fields.proof: The reduced obstruction theory removes one copy of $K_S^\vee$ before restriction to the volume-preserving torus, so localization divides out its K-theory Euler factor. Since $1-e^{-x}=x+O(x^2)$ and the numerator vanishes at $x=0$, both limits agree.

fields.setting:
$\pi$ is a {{esv-solid|solid partition}} with character

$$Q_\pi=\sum_{(a,b,c,d)\in\pi}t_1^{-a}t_2^{-b}t_3^{-c}t_4^{-d},\qquad P_{1234}=\prod_{i=1}^4(1-t_i^{-1}).$$
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $\pi$ is nonempty and $t_1t_2=t_3t_4=1$.
fields.statement:
The character

$$Q_\pi+t_1t_2t_3t_4\overline Q_\pi-t_1t_2t_3t_4P_{1234}\overline Q_\pi Q_\pi$$

has strictly negative constant term.
fields.proof: Write the specialized $Q_\pi$ as $P=\sum p_{a,b}x^ay^b$. The constant term of $P\overline P(1-x)(1-x^{-1})(1-y)(1-y^{-1})$ is the sum of four quadrant sums of squared mixed differences; monotonicity of solid-partition slices and two finite-support inductions bound each by $p_{0,0}$. Thus the full character's constant term is at most $2p_{0,0}-4p_{0,0}<0$.

notations.esv-solid: A finite set of lattice boxes in $\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^4$ closed under decreasing coordinates.

fields.setting: $S=\mathbb C^2$, $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_S\langle y_j\rangle$, and $V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathcal O_S\langle v_i\rangle$.
fields.statement: $$\mathcal S_S(E,V;(-1)^Nq)=\mathcal S_S(V,E;(-1)^rq).$$
fields.evidence: [[esv-cor-1-13|Corollary 1.13]] proves the degree-zero logarithmic symmetry, and [[esv-thm-4-3|Theorem 4.3]] proves matching weighted coefficient identities. Finite localization checks appear in §4.4.

fields.setting: $S=\mathbb C^2$ and $\alpha$ has rank $r\in\mathbb Z$, with $c_1(\alpha)=a\lambda$ and $c_2(\alpha)=b\lambda^2$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $N=1$, the framing weight is zero, and $\lambda_1=\lambda=-\lambda_2$.
fields.statement:
Write the degree-zero series as

$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal S^{\mathrm{red}}_0(E,\alpha;q)&=A_2(q)b+A_1(q)a^2+A_0(q),\\
\mathcal V^{\mathrm{red}}_0(E,\alpha;q)&=B_1(q)a^2+B_0(q).
\end{aligned}$$

For $r\in\mathbb Z$, $n>0$,

$$[q^n]B_0=\frac16\left(\binom{r+1}2(n-1)-1\right)[q^n]B_1.$$

For $r<-1$, $n>1$,

$$[q^n]A_0=\frac1{12}r(nr+n+2)[q^n]A_1.$$
fields.evidence: Checked through $n=20$ for the tested ranks below $5$. [[esv-thm-3-11|Theorem 3.11]] supplies the reduced expansion, and [[esv-cor-1-16|Corollary 1.16]] computes $B_1$ for positive rank.

fields.setting: $X=\mathbb C^4$ and $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_X\langle y_j\rangle$. $V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathcal O_X\langle v_i\rangle$ and $\alpha\in K_{\mathsf T}(X)$.
fields.hypotheses: $N,r>0$. The torus satisfies $t_1t_2t_3t_4=1$.
fields.statement:
For suitable {{esv-orientation|orientation signs}}, the [[esv-def-5-2|Segre series]] satisfy

$$\mathcal S_X(E,V;(-1)^Nq)=\mathcal S_X(V,E;(-1)^rq).$$

The [[esv-def-1-3|degree-zero]] Segre and [[esv-def-5-4|Verlinde series]] satisfy

$$\mathcal S_{X,0}(E,\alpha;q)-\mathcal V_{X,0}(E,\alpha;(-1)^Nq)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{F_n}{(\lambda_1\lambda_2\lambda_3\lambda_4)^{n-2}}\left(\int_Xc_3(X)\right)^2q^n,$$

where $F_n$ is polynomial of total weight degree $4n-6$, depending on $\alpha$ through rank and Chern classes, in the Calabi–Yau weight ring.
fields.evidence: [[esv-lemma-5-6|Lemma 5.6]] makes the fixed-point Euler contribution vanish after $t_1t_2=t_3t_4=1$; symmetry gives the $c_3(X)$ factor. Finite checks appear in (5.11)–(5.12).

notations.esv-orientation: The signs choosing square-root Euler classes at fourfold fixed points.

fields.setting:
$Y=\mathbb C^d$ and

$$E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{r+1}\mathcal O_Y\langle y_j\rangle,\qquad V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathcal O_Y\langle v_i\rangle.$$
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $d\in\{2,4\}$ and $r\ge0$. For $d=4$, impose the Calabi–Yau weight relation.
fields.statement:
For suitable orientation signs in dimension four,

$$\mathcal C_Y(E,V;q)=\exp\!\left(q\int_Y c_{d-1}(Y)\right).$$

The Chern series uses [[esv-def-3-2|Definition 3.2]] for surfaces and [[esv-def-5-2|Definition 5.2]] for fourfolds.
fields.evidence: For $d=2,r=0$ this is [[esv-cor-4-2|Corollary 4.2]]. [[esv-prop-5-9|Proposition 5.9]] proves the fourfold statement conditional on the Nekrasov–Piazzalunga conjecture. Higher-rank surface cases are checked by finite-order localization.

fields.setting: $Y=\mathbb C^d$, $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_Y\langle y_j\rangle$, and $V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathcal O_Y\langle v_i\rangle$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $d\in\{2,4\}$ and $N>1$. In dimension four, use the volume-preserving torus.
fields.statement:
For suitable orientation signs in dimension four,

$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal C_Y(E,V;q)&=1&&\text{for }0\le r\le N-2,\\
\mathcal V_Y(E,-[V];q)&=1&&\text{for }1\le r\le N-1.
\end{aligned}$$
fields.evidence: Checked in finite ranges for surfaces. The cohomological limits in [[esv-prop-5-9|Proposition 5.9]] prove the fourfold Chern assertion conditional on the Nekrasov–Piazzalunga conjecture.

fields.setting:
$X=\mathbb C^4$ and $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_X\langle y_j\rangle$.

$V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^N\mathcal O_X\langle v_i\rangle$ has rank $N$, $s=\prod_{i=1}^N y_iv_i$, and $[x]=x^{1/2}-x^{-1/2}$.

$$\mathcal N_X(E,V;q)=\sum_{n\ge0}q^n\widehat\chi^{\mathrm{vir}}\!\left(\operatorname{Quot}_X(E,n),\frac{\Lambda_{-1}V^{[n]}}{\sqrt{\det(V^{[n]})}}\right).$$
fields.hypotheses: $N>0$. The torus satisfies $t_1t_2t_3t_4=1$.
fields.statement:
For suitable orientation signs,

$$\mathcal N_X(E,V;q)=\term{esv-exp}{\operatorname{Exp}}\!\left(\frac{[t_1t_2][t_2t_3][t_1t_3]}{[t_1][t_2][t_3][t_4]}\frac{[s]}{[s^{1/2}q][s^{-1/2}q]}\right).$$

[NP19, §2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/2303.14266v2#bib.bibx40). Conditional consequences: [[esv-prop-5-8|Proposition 5.8]], [[esv-prop-5-9|Proposition 5.9]].

notations.esv-exp: The plethystic exponential $\operatorname{Exp}(f)=\exp(\sum_{k\ge1}\psi_k(f)/k)$, where $\psi_k$ raises every character and series variable to its $k$th power.

fields.setting: $X=\mathbb C^4$ and $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_X\langle y_j\rangle$. The insertion bundle $V$ has rank $N$.
fields.hypotheses: $N>0$. The torus satisfies $t_1t_2t_3t_4=1$. Assume [[esv-conj-5-7|Conjecture 5.7]] holds with fixed orientation signs.
fields.statement:
The fourfold Nekrasov genus is [[esv-def-2-6|admissible]] in $t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4$ after Calabi–Yau specialization, with plethystic numerator

$$L=(1-t_1t_2)(1-t_2t_3)(1-t_1t_3)\frac{[s]}{[s^{1/2}q][s^{-1/2}q]},\qquad s=\prod_i y_iv_i.$$

The coefficients of $L$ are polynomial in the coordinate characters.

Universal factors: [[esv-prop-2-7|Proposition 2.7]].
fields.proof: Expand the expression inside the plethystic exponential in [[esv-conj-5-7|Conjecture 5.7]]. The identity $t_1t_2t_3t_4=1$ cancels the square-root monomials in its coordinate factor, leaving precisely $L/\prod_i(1-t_i)$.

fields.setting: $X=\mathbb C^4$ and $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_X\langle y_j\rangle$.
fields.hypotheses: $N>0$. The torus satisfies $t_1t_2t_3t_4=1$. Assume [[esv-conj-5-7|Conjecture 5.7]] holds for a rank-$N$ insertion and fixed orientation signs.
fields.statement:
For an equivariant bundle $V$,

$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal C_X(E,V;q)&=\exp\!\left(q\int_X c_3(X)\right)&&\text{if }\operatorname{rk}V=N-1,\\
\mathcal C_X(E,V;q)&=1&&\text{if }0\le\operatorname{rk}V\le N-2.
\end{aligned}$$

In particular,

$$\sum_{n\ge0}q^n\int_{[\operatorname{Quot}_X(E,n)]^{\mathrm{vir}}}1=\begin{cases}\exp\!\left(q\int_Xc_3(X)\right),&N=1,\\1,&N>1,\end{cases}$$

where $\displaystyle\int_Xc_3(X)=\frac{(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)(\lambda_1+\lambda_3)(\lambda_2+\lambda_3)}{\lambda_1\lambda_2\lambda_3(\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3)}$.
fields.proof: Take the cohomological limit in [[esv-conj-5-7|Conjecture 5.7]], then send one insertion weight to infinity with a compensating rescaling of $q$. Only the first term in the plethystic logarithm survives; removing further insertion weights makes every positive-degree term vanish.

fields.setting:
$Y=\mathbb C^d$; $E,V$ have roots $m_j,w_i$, and

$$F(Q;\vec m;\vec w;\vec t)\in\mathbb Q(t_1,\ldots,t_d)[\![Q,m_1,\ldots,m_N,w_1,\ldots,w_r]\!]$$
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $F$ is [[esv-def-2-6|admissible]] in $\vec t$, and symmetric separately in $\vec m$, $\vec w$, and $\vec t$.
fields.statement:
There are series $G_{\mu,\nu,\xi}(Q)$ such that

$$F(Q;\vec m;\vec w;e^{\lambda_1},\ldots,e^{\lambda_d})=\prod_{\mu,\nu,\xi}G_{\mu,\nu,\xi}(Q)^{\int_Yc_\mu(V)c_\nu(Y)c_\xi(E)}.$$

Indices are partitions, including the empty partition.
fields.proof: Admissibility bounds each Laurent exponent in $\log F$ below by $-1$ after $t_i=e^{\lambda_i}$. Multiplication by $\lambda_1\cdots\lambda_d$ leaves a symmetric power series; rewrite it in elementary symmetric functions, divide back using equivariant integration, and exponentiate.

fields.setting: $f(z_1,\ldots,z_k)$ lies in the fraction ring of $\mathbb C[\![z_1,\ldots,z_k]\!]$.
fields.definition:
Expand after simultaneous scaling:

$$f(bz_1,\ldots,bz_k)=\sum_i f_i(z_1,\ldots,z_k)b^i.$$

The part of total degree $i$ is

$$\left.f\right|_{\deg\vec z=i}=f_i.$$

Apply coefficientwise in $q$ to the additive weights, writing multiplicative characters as exponentials.

fields.setting: $W$ is a complex representation of a group $G$.
fields.definition:
The characteristic classes of

$$EG\times_GW\longrightarrow BG$$

are the equivariant characteristic classes of $W$ in $H^*(BG)=H_G^*(\mathrm{pt})$, denoted $c_i^G,e_G,\operatorname{ch}_G,\operatorname{td}_G$.

fields.setting: $F(Q_1,Q_2,\ldots;t_1,\ldots,t_d)$ is formal in finitely many $Q$ variables, with rational-function coefficients in $\vec t$ and constant term $1$.
fields.definition:
Write

$$F=\term{esv-exp}{\operatorname{Exp}}\!\left(\frac L{(1-t_1)\cdots(1-t_d)}\right).$$

$F$ is **admissible in $\vec t$** if every coefficient of $L$ is polynomial in $\vec t$.

notations.esv-exp: The plethystic exponential $\operatorname{Exp}(f)=\exp(\sum_{k\ge1}\psi_k(f)/k)$, where $\psi_k$ raises every character and series variable to its $k$th power.

fields.setting: $M$ is a scheme over $\mathbb C$.
fields.definition:
An obstruction theory is a complex of vector bundles

$$E^\bullet=[\cdots\longrightarrow E^{-2}\longrightarrow E^{-1}\longrightarrow E^0]$$

with a morphism $\varphi:E^\bullet\to L_M^\bullet$ to the cotangent complex in the derived category, such that $h^0(\varphi)$ is an isomorphism and $h^{-1}(\varphi)$ is surjective. It is **two-term perfect** when $E^i=0$ outside degrees $-1,0$. Its virtual tangent class is

$$T^{\mathrm{vir}}=(E^\bullet)^*.$$

cards.title: Definition 3.2 (Surface Segre, Chern, and Verlinde series)

fields.setting: $S=\mathbb C^2$, $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_S\langle y_j\rangle$, and $\alpha\in K_{\mathsf T}(S)$ has rank $r$. $N>0$.
fields.definition:
For $M_n=\operatorname{Quot}_S(E,n)$, let $T_Z^{\mathrm{vir}}$ be its [[esv-def-3-1|virtual tangent class]] and $\alpha_Z^{[n]}=\alpha^{[n]}|_Z$. The virtual series are

$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal S_S(E,\alpha;q)&=\sum_{n\ge0}q^n\sum_{Z\in M_n^{\mathsf T}}\frac{s(\alpha_Z^{[n]})}{e(T_Z^{\mathrm{vir}})},\\
\mathcal C_S(E,\alpha;q)&=\sum_{n\ge0}q^n\sum_{Z\in M_n^{\mathsf T}}\frac{c(\alpha_Z^{[n]})}{e(T_Z^{\mathrm{vir}})},\\
\mathcal V_S(E,\alpha;q)&=\sum_{n\ge0}q^n\sum_{Z\in M_n^{\mathsf T}}\frac{\operatorname{ch}(\det\alpha_Z^{[n]})}{\operatorname{ch}(\Lambda_{-1}(T_Z^{\mathrm{vir}})^\vee)}.
\end{aligned}$$

All characteristic classes are [[esv-def-2-1|equivariant]], and $s(\beta)=c(-\beta)$. The tautological class is $\alpha^{[n]}=p_*(\mathcal F\otimes q^*\alpha)$, with $\mathcal F$ the universal quotient and $p,q$ the two projections.

fields.setting: $X=\mathbb C^4$ and $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_X\langle y_j\rangle$. $N>0$. The torus satisfies $t_1t_2t_3t_4=1$.
fields.definition:
For $n>0$ and $\gamma\in H^*_{\mathsf T}(M_n)$, $M_n=\operatorname{Quot}_X(E,n)$, choose halves $h_Z$ with $T_Z^{\mathrm{vir}}=h_Z+h_Z^\vee$ and orientation signs $\epsilon_Z=(-1)^{o(\mathcal L)|_Z}$. Then

$$\mathcal Q(X,E,n,\gamma)=\sum_{Z\in M_n^{\mathsf T}}\epsilon_Z\frac{\gamma|_Z}{e(h_Z)}.$$

fields.setting: $X=\mathbb C^4$ and $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_X\langle y_j\rangle$. $N>0$. The torus satisfies $t_1t_2t_3t_4=1$.
fields.definition:
Let $\alpha\in K_{\mathsf T}(X)$, with $\epsilon_Z,h_Z$ as in [[esv-def-5-1|Definition 5.1]]. Then

$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal S_X(E,\alpha;q)&=\sum_{n\ge0}q^n\sum_{Z\in M_n^{\mathsf T}}\epsilon_Z\frac{s(\alpha^{[n]}|_Z)}{e(h_Z)},\\
\mathcal C_X(E,\alpha;q)&=\sum_{n\ge0}q^n\sum_{Z\in M_n^{\mathsf T}}\epsilon_Z\frac{c(\alpha^{[n]}|_Z)}{e(h_Z)},
\end{aligned}$$

where $M_n=\operatorname{Quot}_X(E,n)$ and the $n=0$ term is $1$. The coefficients are rational in the additive weights; both series depend on the orientation.

fields.setting: $X=\mathbb C^4$ and $E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N\mathcal O_X\langle y_j\rangle$. $N>0$. The torus satisfies $t_1t_2t_3t_4=1$.
fields.definition:
Let $\alpha\in K_{\mathsf T}(X)$ and $M_n=\operatorname{Quot}_X(E,n)$. For a half $\term{esv-half}{h_Z}$ and orientation sign $\epsilon_Z$, put $\mathsf E_Z=\det((E^\vee)^{[n]}|_Z)$. Then

$$\mathcal V_X(E,\alpha;q)=\sum_{n\ge0}q^n\sum_{Z\in M_n^{\mathsf T}}\epsilon_Z\frac{\operatorname{ch}\bigl((\det h_Z^\vee)^{1/2}\bigr)\operatorname{ch}(\mathsf E_Z^{1/2})\operatorname{ch}\bigl(\det(\alpha^{[n]}|_Z)\bigr)}{\operatorname{ch}(\Lambda_{-1}h_Z^\vee)}.$$

Equivalently, use equivariant Euler characteristics with $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{vir}}$ and determinant insertion. Coefficients lie in the rational character ring.

notations.esv-half: A half of the virtual tangent character: $T_Z^{\mathrm{vir}}=h_Z+h_Z^\vee$.

fields.setting: $n\ge2$, $p$ is the largest prime with $p\le n$, and $H\subset\mathbb R^n$ is a hyperplane through the origin.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $v\in\mathbb R^n$ has distinct coordinates and $\sum_i v_i\ne0$.
fields.statement:
$$|H\cap S_nv|\le\frac{n!}{p}.$$

For $n\ge3$, the maximum equals $(n-1)!$ when $n$ is prime, and $n(n-2)!$ when $n$ is even and $n-1$ is prime.
fields.proof: [[orb-prop-1-7|Proposition 1.7]] reduces to prime dimension; [[orb-cor-4-5|Corollary 4.5]] handles $p=3,5$, and [[orb-thm-5-1|Theorem 5.1]] handles non-dihedral stabilizers. In the dihedral case, [[orb-cor-4-2|Corollary 4.2]] and [[orb-cor-4-4|Corollary 4.4]] reduce to a smallest normal block of size $2\le m<\sqrt{p-1}$; [[orb-lem-6-2|Lemma 6.2]] bounds the orbit intersection when there are enough excluded components, and [[orb-lem-6-3|Lemma 6.3]] contradicts [[orb-prop-6-4|Proposition 6.4]] otherwise. [[orb-ex-1-3|Example 1.3]] and [[orb-ex-1-4|Example 1.4]] give the sharp cases.

fields.setting: For $n\ge3$, $M_n$ is the maximum of $|H\cap S_nv|$ over real vectors $v$ with distinct coordinates and $\sum_i v_i\ne0$, and hyperplanes $H$ through the origin.
fields.statement: $$M_n=\begin{cases}(n-1)!,&n\text{ odd},\\n(n-2)!,&n\text{ even}.\end{cases}$$

fields.setting: $v=(c_1,\ldots,c_n)$ has distinct real coordinates and nonzero sum.
fields.statement:
The hyperplane with normal

$$\left(c_n,\ldots,c_n,-\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}c_i\right)$$

contains exactly the $(n-1)!$ permutations of $v$ whose last coordinate is $c_n$.
fields.proof: On the orbit, the hyperplane equation reduces to $(\sum_i c_i)(x_n-c_n)=0$. The remaining $n-1$ coordinates may be permuted freely.

fields.setting:
For $n\ge3$, $v=(1,2,\ldots,n)$, and $H$ is the hyperplane with normal

$$\left(-\sum_{i=2}^{n-1}i,-\sum_{i=2}^{n-1}i,n+1,\ldots,n+1\right).$$
fields.statement: $H$ contains $(n-1)!$ orbit points for odd $n$, and $n(n-2)!$ for even $n$.
fields.proof: Its equation on the orbit is $x_1+x_2=n+1$. There are $n-1$ ordered distinct complementary pairs when $n$ is odd and $n$ when $n$ is even; each leaves $(n-2)!$ orders for the other coordinates.

fields.setting: $n\ge2$, and $H$ ranges over linear hyperplanes in $\mathbb R^n$.
fields.statement:
For $v$ in a nonempty Zariski open $U\subset\mathbb R^n$,

$$\max_{H\ni0}|H\cap S_nv|=(n-1)!.$$ Choose $U$ with distinct coordinates and nonzero coordinate sum.
fields.proof: For each set of $(n-1)!+1$ orbit vectors, induction on $n$ gives a specialization at which its matrix has full rank. The finitely many rank-drop loci therefore miss a common nonempty Zariski open set; [[orb-ex-1-3|Example 1.3]] gives the matching lower bound.

fields.setting: $1\le k\le n$.
fields.hypotheses:
Suppose every $v\in\mathbb R^n$ with distinct coordinates and nonzero coordinate sum satisfies

$$|H\cap S_nv|\le n!/k$$

for every linear hyperplane $H$.
fields.statement: For every $m\ge n$, the corresponding uniform bound is $|H\cap S_mw|\le m!/k$. In particular, the conjectured bound for an odd dimension implies the conjectured bound for the next dimension.
fields.proof: Partition the orbit according to one fixed coordinate and apply induction to a part exceeding the proposed bound. Its span forces the containing hyperplane to be the fixed-coordinate hyperplane of [[orb-ex-1-3|Example 1.3]], or a coordinate-sum hyperplane when the projected sum is zero; either contains only $(n-1)!$ orbit points, a contradiction.

fields.setting: $v=(c_1,\ldots,c_n)\in\mathbb R^n$ has distinct coordinates.
fields.definition:
Its elementary symmetric curve is the projective variety $C\subset\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$ defined by

$$e_k(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=e_k(c_1,\ldots,c_n)x_0^k,\qquad1\le k\le n-1.$$

The affine chart $x_0=1$ contains the orbit $S_nv$.

fields.setting: $v\in\mathbb R^n$ has distinct coordinates, and $\card{orb-def-3-1}{C}=\bigcup_{i=1}^rC_i$ is its elementary symmetric curve.
fields.statement:
$\dim C_i=1$ and $\deg C=(n-1)!$.

A proper hyperplane section has at most $(n-1)!$ points; thus $|H\cap S_nv|>(n-1)!$ forces some $C_i\subset H$.
fields.proof: Adding the degree-$n$ equation $e_n(x)=e_n(v)x_0^n$ cuts out the $n!$ distinct orbit points, so all components of the intersection of the first $n-1$ hypersurfaces have dimension one. Bézout gives the product $1\cdot2\cdots(n-1)$, and a proper hyperplane section has at most that many points.

fields.setting: $v\in\mathbb R^n$ has distinct coordinates, and its elementary symmetric curve is $\card{orb-def-3-1}{C}=\bigcup_{i=1}^rC_i$.
fields.statement:
$S_n$ acts transitively on the components, with

$$\deg C_i=\frac{(n-1)!}{r},\qquad |C_i\cap S_nv|=\frac{n!}{r}.$$

Each orbit point belongs to exactly one component.
fields.proof: The degree-$n$ symmetric equation cuts the curve transversely in the $n!$ orbit points, so no orbit point lies on two components. Transitivity on orbit points gives transitivity on components, hence equal degrees and equal orbit counts.

fields.setting: $p$ is prime, and $C_i$ is a component of the [[orb-def-3-1|elementary symmetric curve]] of a distinct-coordinate vector $v\in\mathbb R^p$.
fields.statement: $\operatorname{Stab}(C_i)\subset S_p$ contains a $p$-cycle.
fields.proof: [[orb-lem-3-3|Lemma 3.3]] and orbit–stabilizer give $|\operatorname{Stab}(C_i)|=p!/r=p\deg C_i$. Cauchy's theorem supplies an element of order $p$, which in $S_p$ must be a $p$-cycle.

fields.setting:
$p$ is prime, $v\in\mathbb R^p$ has distinct coordinates, and $C_0$ is a component of its [[orb-def-3-1|elementary symmetric curve]].

$$\zeta=e^{2\pi i/p},\qquad w=(\zeta,\zeta^2,\ldots,\zeta^p).$$
fields.statement: $\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb C}(C_0)$ contains $\sigma w$ for some $\sigma\in S_p$.
fields.proof: The stabilizer cycle preserves the complex span of the component. Since an orbit point has distinct coordinates, this span contains a nontrivial cyclic character line, generated by a permutation of $w$.

fields.setting: $v\in\mathbb R^n$ has distinct coordinates, $H$ is a linear hyperplane, and $\card{orb-def-3-1}{C}$ is its elementary symmetric curve.
fields.hypotheses:
Suppose each component $C_i\subset H$ has $n-1$ assigned components $C_{i1},\ldots,C_{i,n-1}$ such that

$$H\cap C_{ij}\cap S_nv=\varnothing,$$

and all assigned components are distinct across all pairs $(i,j)$.
fields.statement: $$|H\cap S_nv|\le(n-1)!.$$
fields.proof: If $H$ contains $q$ of the $r$ components, [[orb-lem-3-3|Lemma 3.3]] counts $n!/r$ orbit points on each, while Bézout bounds each remaining nonassigned component by $(n-1)!/r$. Thus the total is at most $q\,n!/r+(r-nq)(n-1)!/r=(n-1)!$.

fields.setting: $n\ge3$, $v\in\mathbb R^n$ has distinct coordinates, and $H=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)^\perp$ is a hyperplane.
fields.statement:
If $v,(ij)v\in H$, then $a_i=a_j$.

If $\pi$ is an $n$-cycle and $H$ contains both $\pi^mv$ and $(ijk)\pi^mv$ for every integer $m$, then $a_i=a_j=a_k$.
fields.proof: Subtracting $v$ from its transposition isolates a nonzero multiple of $e_i-e_j$. For a three-cycle, subtract along the cyclic orbit and use the position of the smallest coordinate to obtain two independent vectors in the two-dimensional coordinate-sum-zero plane on $i,j,k$; its containment in $H$ forces the three normal entries to agree.

fields.setting: $p\ge3$ is prime, $v\in\mathbb R^p$ has distinct coordinates, and $H=(a_1,\ldots,a_p)^\perp$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose some $a_i$ differs from every $a_j$ with $j\ne i$.
fields.statement: $$|H\cap S_pv|\le(p-1)!.$$
fields.proof: For every component inside $H$, assign its $p-1$ translates by $(ij)$, $j\ne i$. [[orb-lem-4-1|Lemma 4.1]] excludes their orbit points from $H$ and prevents collisions via three-cycles, using the stabilizer cycle from [[orb-lem-3-4|Lemma 3.4]]; [[orb-lem-3-6|Lemma 3.6]] then counts them.

fields.setting: $p\ge5$ is prime, and $C_0$ is a component of the [[orb-def-3-1|elementary symmetric curve]] of a distinct-coordinate vector in $\mathbb R^p$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $H=(a_1,\ldots,a_p)^\perp$ contains $C_0$ and $(ij)(kl)C_0$, with $i,j,k,l$ distinct. $a_i=a_k=a$ and $a_j=a_l=b$.
fields.proof: [[orb-cor-3-5|Corollary 3.5]] supplies $\sigma w$ in the component span, where $w=(\zeta,\ldots,\zeta^p)$, $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/p}$, and we write $q'=\sigma^{-1}(q)$. Subtracting its double transposition yields $(a-b)(\zeta^{i'}-\zeta^{j'}+\zeta^{k'}-\zeta^{l'})=0$; the four distinct exponents and the prime cyclotomic relation force $a=b$.

fields.setting: $p\ge5$ is prime, and $H\subset\mathbb R^p$ is a linear hyperplane.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose its normal has two different values occurring on disjoint sets of sizes $r$ and $s$, with $rs\ge p-1$.
fields.statement:
For every distinct-coordinate $v\in\mathbb R^p$,

$$|H\cap S_pv|\le(p-1)!.$$
fields.proof: Translate each contained component by transpositions between the two blocks. [[orb-lem-4-1|Lemma 4.1]] excludes their orbit points and rules out three-cycle collisions using [[orb-lem-3-4|Lemma 3.4]]; [[orb-lem-4-3|Lemma 4.3]] rules out double-transposition collisions. Choose $p-1$ of the $rs$ distinct translates and apply [[orb-lem-3-6|Lemma 3.6]].

fields.setting: $p\in\{3,5\}$, and $H\subset\mathbb R^p$ is a linear hyperplane.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $v\in\mathbb R^p$ has distinct coordinates and nonzero coordinate sum.
fields.statement: $$|H\cap S_pv|\le(p-1)!.$$
fields.proof: A constant normal gives no orbit points. Otherwise [[orb-cor-4-2|Corollary 4.2]] handles any normal value occurring once; for $p=5$, the only remaining multiplicities are $2$ and $3$, so [[orb-cor-4-4|Corollary 4.4]] applies.

fields.setting: $p\ge5$ is prime, $v\in\mathbb R^p$ has distinct coordinates, and $G\subset S_p$ contains a $p$-cycle.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $$\dim\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb R}(Gv)>3.$$ For distinct $i,j,k,l$, suppose $H=(a_1,\ldots,a_p)^\perp$ contains $Gv$ and $(ij)(kl)Gv$.
fields.statement: $$a_i=a_j,\qquad a_k=a_l.$$
fields.proof: The cyclic representation contains a conjugate pair of nontrivial character lines and a third distinct character line. Applying the double transposition and subtracting gives two independent pair-difference vectors: dependence of all three would contradict the prime cyclotomic relation. Their containment in $H$ forces the two normal-coordinate equalities.

fields.setting: $p\ge7$ is prime, $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/p}$, $w=(\zeta,\ldots,\zeta^p)$, and $\sigma\in S_p$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose the complexification of a real hyperplane $H=(a_1,\ldots,a_p)^\perp$ contains $\sigma w$ and $(ij)(kl)\sigma w$, with $i,j,k,l$ distinct.
fields.statement:
Either $$\sigma^{-1}(i)+\sigma^{-1}(j)\equiv\sigma^{-1}(k)+\sigma^{-1}(l)\pmod p,$$

or $a_i=a_j$ and $a_k=a_l$.
fields.proof: Subtract the two vectors and take complex conjugates. If the resulting pair differences are independent, they force the two normal equalities; otherwise their determinant vanishes, and the prime cyclotomic relation forces the displayed congruence between the four distinct exponents.

fields.setting: $p$ is prime, and $v\in\mathbb R^p$ has distinct coordinates and nonzero coordinate sum. $C_1$ is a component of its [[orb-def-3-1|elementary symmetric curve]].
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $$\operatorname{Stab}(C_1)\not\simeq D_{2p}.$$
fields.statement: $$\max_{H\ni0}|H\cap S_pv|=(p-1)!.$$
fields.proof: [[orb-cor-4-5|Corollary 4.5]] and [[orb-lem-3-2|Lemma 3.2]] reduce to $p\ge7$ and a component inside $H$. [[orb-prop-5-4|Proposition 5.4]] describes its stabilizer; [[orb-lem-3-3|Lemma 3.3]] excludes the cyclic case, and [[orb-lem-5-5|Lemma 5.5]] gives a span of dimension greater than three. [[orb-lem-4-1|Lemma 4.1]] and [[orb-lem-4-6|Lemma 4.6]] then give $p-1$ distinct excluded translates for every contained component, so [[orb-lem-3-6|Lemma 3.6]] bounds the orbit intersection.

fields.setting: $p$ is prime; $v\in\mathbb R^p$ has distinct coordinates and nonzero sum. Let $C_0$ be a component of its [[orb-def-3-1|elementary symmetric curve]] and $H$ a linear hyperplane, with $v\in C_0\subset H$.
fields.statement:
$$\operatorname{Stab}(C_0)=\langle\pi,\sigma\rangle\subset N_{S_p}(\langle\pi\rangle),$$

where $\pi$ is a $p$-cycle and $\sigma$ a power of a $(p-1)$-cycle.
fields.proof: For $G=\operatorname{Stab}(C_0)$, [[orb-lem-3-4|Lemma 3.4]] supplies $\pi$. Burnside's theorem ([Theorem 5.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2001.09123v1#S5.E2)) and the permutation-representation criterion ([Theorem 5.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2001.09123v1#S5.E3), Serre, Exercise 2.6) show that a nonnormal $\langle\pi\rangle$ would make $\operatorname{Span}(Gv)=\mathbb R^p$, contradicting $C_0\subset H$. The normalizer is $\mathbb F_p\rtimes\mathbb F_p^\times$, whose subgroups containing translations have the claimed form.

fields.setting: $p$ is prime, and $\pi\in S_p$ is a $p$-cycle.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $$\langle\pi\rangle\subset G\subset N_{S_p}(\langle\pi\rangle).$$
fields.statement:
For every nontrivial irreducible $G$-subrepresentation $W\subset\mathbb C^p$,
$$\dim W=|G/\langle\pi\rangle|.$$
fields.proof: As in [[orb-prop-5-4|Proposition 5.4]], write $G=\langle\pi,\sigma\rangle$ with $\sigma^{-1}\pi\sigma=\pi^k$. The cyclic character lines satisfy $\sigma V_i=V_{ik}$; each nonzero multiplicative $k$-orbit gives an irreducible summand of dimension $\operatorname{ord}(k)=|G/\langle\pi\rangle|$.

fields.setting:
$p\ge7$ is prime; $v\in\mathbb R^p$ has distinct coordinates and nonzero sum. The components of its [[orb-def-3-1|elementary symmetric curve]] have stabilizer $D_{2p}$.

For $H=(b_1,\ldots,b_p)^\perp$, let $\lambda_M$ be a smallest equal-entry block, $m=|\lambda_M|$, and fix distinct $i,k\in\lambda_M$. The vertices of $\Gamma$ are the components in $H$, with
$$D\sim D'\iff(ij)(kl)D=D'\quad\text{for some }j,l\notin\lambda_M,\ j\ne l.$$
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $C_1\sim C_2$.
fields.statement: There is exactly one pair of distinct $j,l\notin\lambda_M$ with $(ij)(kl)C_1=C_2$.
fields.proof: [[orb-cor-3-5|Corollary 3.5]] and [[orb-lem-4-9|Lemma 4.9]] show that two labels would give matching congruences in the root-of-unity ordering. Their product is then a nonidentity stabilizer element supported on at most six positions: it is neither a $p$-cycle nor a dihedral reflection (for $p=7$, parity also excludes a reflection).

fields.setting:
$p\ge7$ is prime; $v\in\mathbb R^p$ has distinct coordinates and nonzero sum. The components of its [[orb-def-3-1|elementary symmetric curve]] have stabilizer $D_{2p}$.

For $H=(b_1,\ldots,b_p)^\perp$, let $\lambda_M$ be a smallest equal-entry block, $m=|\lambda_M|$, and fix distinct $i,k\in\lambda_M$. The vertices of $\Gamma$ are the components in $H$, with
$$D\sim D'\iff(ij)(kl)D=D'\quad\text{for some }j,l\notin\lambda_M,\ j\ne l.$$ Put $T=\{(ij),(kj):j\notin\lambda_M\}$ and $\mathcal T=\{\tau D:\tau\in T,\ D\in\Gamma\}$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $|\mathcal T|\ge(p-1)|\Gamma|$.
fields.statement: $$|H\cap S_pv|\le(p-1)!.$$
fields.proof:
[[orb-lem-4-1|Lemma 4.1]] shows that every component in $\mathcal T$ has no orbit points in $H$. For the $r$ total components, [[orb-lem-3-3|Lemma 3.3]] and Bézout therefore bound the intersection by

$$\frac{p!}{r}|\Gamma|+\frac{(p-1)!}{r}\bigl(r-|\Gamma|-|\mathcal T|\bigr)\le(p-1)!.$$

fields.setting:
$p\ge7$ is prime; $v\in\mathbb R^p$ has distinct coordinates and nonzero sum. The components of its [[orb-def-3-1|elementary symmetric curve]] have stabilizer $D_{2p}$.

For $H=(b_1,\ldots,b_p)^\perp$, let $\lambda_M$ be a smallest equal-entry block, $m=|\lambda_M|$, and fix distinct $i,k\in\lambda_M$. The vertices of $\Gamma$ are the components in $H$, with
$$D\sim D'\iff(ij)(kl)D=D'\quad\text{for some }j,l\notin\lambda_M,\ j\ne l.$$ $d(D)$ is the vertex degree. Put $T=\{(ij),(kj):j\notin\lambda_M\}$ and $\mathcal T=\{\tau D:\tau\in T,\ D\in\Gamma\}$.
fields.hypotheses: Suppose $2\le m<\sqrt{p-1}$ and $|\mathcal T|<(p-1)|\Gamma|$.
fields.statement:
Some $C_0\in\Gamma$ satisfies

$$\sum_{D\sim C_0}d(D)\ge\kappa+2d(C_0),\qquad\kappa=(p-2m)^2-1.$$
fields.proof: [[orb-lem-4-1|Lemma 4.1]] and [[orb-lem-6-1|Lemma 6.1]] count collisions exactly twice per edge, giving $|\mathcal T|=2(p-m)|\Gamma|-2e$ and $2e>(p-2m+1)|\Gamma|$. If every vertex violated the displayed inequality, summing would give $\sum d(D)^2<\kappa|\Gamma|+4e$, contradicting Cauchy–Schwarz and the lower bound on $e$.

fields.setting:
$p\ge7$ is prime; $v\in\mathbb R^p$ has distinct coordinates and nonzero sum. The components of its [[orb-def-3-1|elementary symmetric curve]] have stabilizer $D_{2p}$.

For $H=(b_1,\ldots,b_p)^\perp$, let $\lambda_M$ be a smallest equal-entry block, $m=|\lambda_M|$, and fix distinct $i,k\in\lambda_M$. The vertices of $\Gamma$ are the components in $H$, with
$$D\sim D'\iff(ij)(kl)D=D'\quad\text{for some }j,l\notin\lambda_M,\ j\ne l.$$ Fix $C_0\in\Gamma$ and put $d=d(C_0)$.
fields.statement: $$\sum_{D\sim C_0}d(D)\le p-m+2d.$$
fields.proof: [[orb-lem-6-6|Lemma 6.6]] bounds the sum by $|\term{orb-R}{R}|+2d$. The injective coordinate projection in [[orb-prop-6-7|Proposition 6.7]] gives $|R|\le p-m$.

notations.orb-R: The edge-label pairs defined in Lemma 6.6.

fields.setting:
$p\ge7$ is prime; $v\in\mathbb R^p$ has distinct coordinates and nonzero sum. The components of its [[orb-def-3-1|elementary symmetric curve]] have stabilizer $D_{2p}$.

For $H=(b_1,\ldots,b_p)^\perp$, let $\lambda_M$ be a smallest equal-entry block, $m=|\lambda_M|$, and fix distinct $i,k\in\lambda_M$. The vertices of $\Gamma$ are the components in $H$, with
$$D\sim D'\iff(ij)(kl)D=D'\quad\text{for some }j,l\notin\lambda_M,\ j\ne l.$$ Fix $C_0\in\Gamma$ with neighbors $C_a=(ij_a)(kl_a)C_0$, $1\le a\le d$, and set $j_0=k$, $l_0=i$. Choose $\sigma w\in\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb C}C_0$ with $w=(\zeta,\ldots,\zeta^p)$ and $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/p}$, and write $q'=\sigma^{-1}(q)$.
fields.statement:
$$i'+j_a'\equiv k'+l_a'\pmod p\qquad(0\le a\le d).$$

Each $j_a$ determines $l_a$ and conversely. Both lists $j_0,\ldots,j_d$ and $l_0,\ldots,l_d$ have distinct entries.
fields.proof: [[orb-cor-3-5|Corollary 3.5]] supplies $\sigma w$. Since the normal values at $i,k$ differ from those at $j_a,l_a$, [[orb-lem-4-9|Lemma 4.9]] forces the congruence; repeated entries would then give the same neighbor, while $j_0,l_0$ lie inside the block and the remaining entries outside.

fields.setting:
$p\ge7$ is prime; $v\in\mathbb R^p$ has distinct coordinates and nonzero sum. The components of its [[orb-def-3-1|elementary symmetric curve]] have stabilizer $D_{2p}$.

For $H=(b_1,\ldots,b_p)^\perp$, let $\lambda_M$ be a smallest equal-entry block, $m=|\lambda_M|$, and fix distinct $i,k\in\lambda_M$. The vertices of $\Gamma$ are the components in $H$, with
$$D\sim D'\iff(ij)(kl)D=D'\quad\text{for some }j,l\notin\lambda_M,\ j\ne l.$$ For $C_0\in\Gamma$ with neighbors $C_a=(ij_a)(kl_a)C_0$, $1\le a\le d$, set
$$\begin{aligned}
R={}&\{(j_a,C_0):1\le a\le d\}\\
&\cup\{(j,C_a):C_a\sim(il)(kj)C_a,\ j,l\notin\lambda_M,\ \{j,l\}\cap\{j_a,l_a\}=\varnothing\}.
\end{aligned}$$
fields.statement: $$\sum_{D\sim C_0}d(D)\le|R|+2d.$$
fields.proof: An edge $C_a\sim(il)(kj)C_a$ outside the encoding must have $\{j,l\}\cap\{j_a,l_a\}\ne\varnothing$. The coordinate relation from [[orb-lem-4-9|Lemma 4.9]] leaves at most one omitted edge with $j=j_a$ and one with $l=l_a$; the crossed equalities give the already encoded edge back to $C_0$.

$p\ge7$ is prime; $v\in\mathbb R^p$ has distinct coordinates and nonzero sum. The components of its [[orb-def-3-1|elementary symmetric curve]] have stabilizer $D_{2p}$.

For $H=(b_1,\ldots,b_p)^\perp$, let $\lambda_M$ be a smallest equal-entry block, $m=|\lambda_M|$, and fix distinct $i,k\in\lambda_M$. The vertices of $\Gamma$ are the components in $H$, with

\end{aligned}$$
fields.statement:
$$R\longrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\setminus\lambda_M,\qquad(j,C_a)\longmapsto j$$

is injective, so $|R|\le p-m$.
fields.proof: Subtract root-of-unity vectors of adjacent components and use [[orb-lem-4-9|Lemma 4.9]] to express a normal-coordinate ratio in terms of their labels. The injectivity in [[orb-lem-6-8|Lemma 6.8]] and the distinct labels in [[orb-lem-6-5|Lemma 6.5]] force each first coordinate $j$ to determine its component $C_a$.

fields.setting: $p\ge7$ is prime, $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/p}$, and $i'\ne k'$ in $\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$.
fields.statement:
The map $$f(t)=\frac{\zeta^{i'}-\zeta^t}{\zeta^{k'}-\zeta^{i'+t-k'}}$$

is injective on $\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z\setminus\{2k'-i'\}$.
fields.proof: After a nonzero rescaling, this is $g(x)=(1-\zeta^{a+x})/(1-\zeta^{b+x})$ with $a\ne b$. Cross-multiplying $g(x)=g(y)$ gives $(\zeta^a-\zeta^b)(\zeta^y-\zeta^x)=0$, hence $x=y$ modulo $p$.

cards.title: Corollary C (Stringy Hodge numbers from cohomology)

fields.setting: $Y/\mathbb C$ is an irreducible log-terminal finite type scheme. $\mathcal X\to Y$ is a crepant resolution by a smooth irreducible finite type Artin stack with affine diagonal.
fields.statement:
Its [[coh-def-1-4|stringy cohomology]] satisfies
$$\operatorname{HD}_{\mathrm{str}}(Y)=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Q}\left(\operatorname{HD}(H_{\mathrm{str}}^{\mathrm{even},i}(\mathcal X))-\operatorname{HD}(H_{\mathrm{str}}^{\mathrm{odd},i}(\mathcal X))\right).$$
If this invariant has only integer exponents, as when $Y$ is $1$-Gorenstein, this becomes
$$\operatorname{HD}_{\mathrm{str}}(Y)=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}(-1)^i\operatorname{HD}(H_{\mathrm{str}}^i(\mathcal X)).$$
When the invariant is polynomial, its sign-corrected coefficients are Batyrev’s stringy Hodge numbers.
fields.proof:
Apply [[coh-thm-b|Theorem B]] and the equality of the stringy invariant of a crepant stack resolution with that of $Y$. The integer-grading observation in [Remark 1.6](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#S1.Thmtheorem6) gives the second formula.

[SU24b, Corollary 1.9 and Proposition 12.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx16)

fields.setting:
$\mathcal X/\mathbb C$ is a smooth equidimensional finite type Artin stack, with affine diagonal and a {{coh-stable|properly stable good moduli space}}; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.

$$\begin{aligned}A^w&=\term{coh-arcs}{\mathcal A_{\mathcal X}}\cap\term{coh-weight}{\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal X}}^{-1}(w),\\A_n^w&=\theta_n(A^w),\qquad Y_n^w=\term{coh-model}{\mathcal Y^{A_n^w}}.\end{aligned}$$
$\theta_n$ is truncation to $\mathscr J_n(\mathcal X)$.
fields.statement:
For $w\in\mathbb Q$, $i\in\mathbb Z$, there is $m\ge0$ such that for all $n\ge m$,
$$\card{coh-def-2-6}{H_c^{i+2nd}}(Y_n^w)(nd)\cong H_c^{i+2md}(Y_m^w)(md)$$
as polarizable mixed Hodge structures.
fields.proof: [[coh-thm-3-1|Theorem 3.1]] gives constructibility and convergence for each weight fiber $A^w$. [[coh-thm-8-1|Theorem 8.1]] then stabilizes its shifted compactly supported cohomology.

notations.coh-arcs: These distinguished arcs come from the canonical reduction of stabilizers.
notations.coh-model: The disjoint union of the canonical reduced locally closed strata of this constructible set.
notations.coh-stable: The good moduli space has a dense stable locus with finite stabilizers.
notations.coh-weight: The rational correction from the stabilizer action along a twisted arc.

fields.setting:
$\mathcal X/\mathbb C$ is a smooth equidimensional finite type Artin stack, with affine diagonal and a {{coh-stable|properly stable good moduli space}}; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.

$$A^w=\term{coh-arcs}{\mathcal A_{\mathcal X}}\cap\term{coh-weight}{\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal X}}^{-1}(w).$$
fields.statement:
For [[coh-def-1-4|stringy cohomology]] and $w\in\mathbb Q$,
$${\chi_{\mathrm{Hdg}}}(\mathbb L^d\nu_{\mathcal X}(A^w))=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}(-1)^i[H_{\mathrm{str}}^{i,w}(\mathcal X)].$$
The [[coh-def-1-1|stringy Hodge–Deligne invariant]] is
$$\operatorname{HD}_{\mathrm{str}}(\mathcal X)=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Q}\left(\operatorname{HD}(H_{\mathrm{str}}^{\mathrm{even},i}(\mathcal X))-\operatorname{HD}(H_{\mathrm{str}}^{\mathrm{odd},i}(\mathcal X))\right).$$
When this series has integer exponents,
$$\chi_{\mathrm{Hdg}}(\mathrm e_{\mathrm{str}}(\mathcal X))=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}(-1)^i[H_{\mathrm{str}}^i(\mathcal X)],$$
with class sums converging in the completed Grothendieck ring of polarizable mixed Hodge structures.
fields.proof: Apply [[coh-thm-3-1|Theorem 3.1]] and [[coh-thm-8-4|Theorem 8.4]] to each weight fiber, then sum the finitely many weights with their Tate shifts.

notations.coh-arcs: These distinguished arcs come from the canonical reduction of stabilizers.
notations.coh-stable: The good moduli space has a dense stable locus with finite stabilizers.
notations.coh-weight: The rational correction from the stabilizer action along a twisted arc.

fields.setting: $\mathcal X/\mathbb C$ is a smooth equidimensional tame finite type Artin stack with affine diagonal.
fields.statement:
For every $i\in\mathbb Q$, its [[coh-def-1-4|stringy]] and [[coh-def-2-12|orbifold cohomology]] satisfy
$$H_{\mathrm{str}}^{\mathrm{even},i}(\mathcal X)\cong H_{\mathrm{orb}}^{\mathrm{even},i}(\mathcal X),\qquad H_{\mathrm{str}}^{\mathrm{odd},i}(\mathcal X)\cong H_{\mathrm{orb}}^{\mathrm{odd},i}(\mathcal X).$$
Thus $H_{\mathrm{str}}^i(\mathcal X)\cong H_{\mathrm{orb}}^i(\mathcal X)$ and $\operatorname{HD}_{\mathrm{str}}(\mathcal X)=\operatorname{HD}_{\mathrm{orb}}(\mathcal X)$.
fields.proof:
Here all twisted arcs are distinguished; [[coh-thm-5-1|Theorem 5.1]] and [[coh-thm-7-1|Theorem 7.1]] identify each stabilized weight piece with its zeroth-jet cohomology. [[coh-prop-9-1|Proposition 9.1]] replaces zeroth jets by inertia components, while [[coh-lem-9-6|Lemma 9.6]] matches the grading and Tate twists; [[coh-thm-b|Theorem B]] then identifies their Hodge–Deligne invariants.

[SU24b, Proposition 4.11](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx16)

fields.setting: $\mathcal X/\mathbb C$ is a smooth equidimensional finite type Artin stack, with affine diagonal and a properly stable good moduli space; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.
fields.definition:
$$\mathrm e_{\mathrm{str}}(\mathcal X)={\mathbb L}^d\int_{\term{coh-arcs}{\mathcal A_{\mathcal X}}}\mathbb L^{-\term{coh-weight}{\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal X}}}\,d\term{coh-nu}{\nu_{\mathcal X}},$$
$$\operatorname{HD}_{\mathrm{str}}(\mathcal X)={\operatorname{HD}}(\mathrm e_{\mathrm{str}}(\mathcal X)).$$
[[coh-cor-3-2|Corollary 3.2]] makes the integral well-defined. Its Hodge–Deligne realization lies in completed Laurent series with rational exponents of bounded denominator.

notations.coh-arcs: These distinguished arcs come from the canonical reduction of stabilizers.
notations.coh-nu: The motivic volume of a set of twisted arcs.
notations.coh-weight: The rational correction from the stabilizer action along a twisted arc.

fields.setting:
$\mathcal X/\mathbb C$ is a smooth equidimensional finite type Artin stack, with affine diagonal and a properly stable good moduli space; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.

$$\begin{aligned}A^w&=\term{coh-arcs}{\mathcal A_{\mathcal X}}\cap\term{coh-weight}{\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal X}}^{-1}(w),\\A_n^w&=\theta_n(A^w),\qquad Y_n^w=\term{coh-model}{\mathcal Y^{A_n^w}}.\end{aligned}$$
$\theta_n$ is truncation to $\mathscr J_n(\mathcal X)$.
fields.definition:
For $j\in\mathbb Z$, $w\in\mathbb Q$, and $m$ in the stable range of [[coh-thm-a|Theorem A]],
$$H_{\mathrm{str}}^{j,w}(\mathcal X)=H_c^{j+2md}(Y_m^w)(md).$$
For $i\in\mathbb Q$ and $\epsilon\in\{0,1\}$, put
$$H_{\mathrm{str}}^{\epsilon,i}(\mathcal X)=\bigoplus_{\substack{w\in\mathbb Q\\i+2w\in2\mathbb Z+\epsilon}}H_{\mathrm{str}}^{i+2w,w}(\mathcal X)(w),$$
where $\epsilon=0,1$ means even, odd, and $H_{\mathrm{str}}^i=H_{\mathrm{str}}^{0,i}\oplus H_{\mathrm{str}}^{1,i}$. The pieces are defined up to isomorphism ([Remark 1.5](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#S1.Thmtheorem5)); weight sums are finite, with rational Tate twists.

notations.coh-model: The disjoint union of the canonical reduced locally closed strata of this constructible set.
notations.coh-weight: The rational correction from the stabilizer action along a twisted arc.

fields.setting: $s:\mathcal Z\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$ is the structure map of a locally finite type Artin stack.
fields.definition:
$$H^i(\mathcal Z)=H^i(s_*\mathbb Q_{\mathcal Z}),\qquad H_c^i(\mathcal Z)=H^i(s_!\mathbb Q_{\mathcal Z}),\quad i\in\mathbb Z.$$
These are rational polarizable mixed Hodge structures, using [Tubach’s cohomologically constructible mixed Hodge modules and their six functors](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx18).

fields.setting: $\mathcal X/\mathbb C$ is smooth, finite type, equidimensional and tame, with affine diagonal.
fields.definition:
For a connected component $F$ of the {{coh-inertia|cyclotomic inertia}}, write $s_F=\operatorname{shft}_{\mathcal X}(F)$. If the tangent characters at $F\subset I_{\mu_\ell}(\mathcal X)$ are $\xi\mapsto\xi^{-a_j}$, $1\le a_j\le\ell$, then
$$s_F=\dim\mathcal X-\frac1\ell\sum_j a_j.$$
For $i\in\mathbb Q$ and parity $\epsilon\in\{0,1\}$, the even and odd pieces are
$$H_{\mathrm{orb}}^{\epsilon,i}(\mathcal X)=\bigoplus_{\substack{F\\i-2s_F\in2\mathbb Z+\epsilon}}H_c^{i-2s_F}(F)(-s_F).$$
Set $H_{\mathrm{orb}}^i=H_{\mathrm{orb}}^{0,i}\oplus H_{\mathrm{orb}}^{1,i}$ and
$$\operatorname{HD}_{\mathrm{orb}}(\mathcal X)=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Q}\left(\operatorname{HD}(H_{\mathrm{orb}}^{0,i})-\operatorname{HD}(H_{\mathrm{orb}}^{1,i})\right).$$

notations.coh-inertia: The stack of points equipped with an injective action of a cyclic group.

fields.setting:
$k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $\mathcal X/k$ is a smooth equidimensional finite type Artin stack, with affine diagonal and a properly stable good moduli space; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.

$$A^w=\term{coh-arcs}{\mathcal A_{\mathcal X}}\cap\term{coh-weight}{\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal X}}^{-1}(w),\qquad A_n^w=\theta_n(A^w).$$
$\theta_n$ is truncation to $\mathscr J_n(\mathcal X)$.
fields.statement:
For each $w\in\mathbb Q$, $A^w$ is measurable, every $A_n^w$ is quasi-compact and locally constructible, and
$$\nu_{\mathcal X}(A^w)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\nu_{\mathcal X}(\theta_n^{-1}(A_n^w)).$$
Each $\theta_n^{-1}(A_n^w)$ is a {{coh-cylinder|bounded cylinder}}.
fields.proof:
Approximate upstairs on the {{coh-reduction|canonical reduction of stabilizers}} by cylinders avoiding the unstable locus. [[coh-prop-3-7|Proposition 3.7]] carries these to bounded cylinders downstairs, and [[coh-lem-3-4|Lemma 3.4]] controls their successive differences; the omitted unstable arcs have measure zero, while Chevalley’s theorem gives the constructible jet images.

[SU24b, Theorem 9.1 and Remark 4.21](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx16)

notations.coh-arcs: These distinguished arcs come from the canonical reduction of stabilizers.
notations.coh-cylinder: A set of arcs specified at a finite jet level, with only finitely many twisting orders.
notations.coh-reduction: Edidin–Rydh’s modification replaces positive-dimensional stabilizers by finite ones.
notations.coh-weight: The rational correction from the stabilizer action along a twisted arc.

fields.setting: $k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $\mathcal X/k$ is a smooth equidimensional finite type Artin stack, with affine diagonal and a properly stable good moduli space; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.
fields.statement: The function $\mathbb L^{-\term{coh-weight}{\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal X}}}$ is integrable on $\mathcal A_{\mathcal X}$.
fields.proof:
[[coh-thm-3-1|Theorem 3.1]] makes every weight fiber measurable. The canonical reduction is tame, so only finitely many weights occur; the integral is a finite weighted sum of their measures.

[SU24b, Proposition 4.19](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx16); [Edidin–Rydh, Theorem 2.11(4c)](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx7)

notations.coh-weight: The rational correction from the stabilizer action along a twisted arc.

fields.setting: $k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ is a representable morphism of finite type Artin stacks.
fields.hypotheses: $|f|$ is surjective.
fields.statement: $$\dim\mathcal Z\le\dim\mathcal Y.$$
fields.proof: Restrict to the smooth dense part of a largest-dimensional component of $\mathcal Z$, then take smooth and étale scheme covers of constant relative dimension. The assertion becomes the usual dimension inequality for a surjective morphism of finite type schemes.

fields.setting: $k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $\mathcal Z/k$ is a finite type Artin stack with affine geometric stabilizers; $\mathrm e$ is motivic class and $\|\cdot\|$ the dimension norm.
fields.hypotheses: $C\subset D\subset|\mathcal Z|$ are constructible.
fields.statement: $$\|\mathrm e(C)\|\le\|\mathrm e(D)\|.$$
fields.proof:
Stratify $C$ and $D\setminus C$ into locally closed substacks, and use $\|\mathrm e(\mathcal W)\|=\exp(\dim\mathcal W)$ from the recalled Proposition 2.2.

[SU23b, Proposition 4.4 (recalled as Proposition 2.2)](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx14)

fields.setting: $k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ is representable, with both stacks finite type and having affine geometric stabilizers.
fields.hypotheses: $C\subset|\mathcal Y|$, $D\subset|\mathcal Z|$ are constructible, with $D\subset f(C)$.
fields.statement: $$\|\mathrm e(D)\|\le\|\mathrm e(C)\|.$$
fields.proof:
Chevalley’s theorem makes $f(C)$ constructible, so [[coh-lem-3-4|Lemma 3.4]] reduces to $D=f(C)$. Compatible locally closed partitions give a representable surjection; [[coh-lem-3-3|Lemma 3.3]] and the motivic dimension formula give the bound.

[Hall–Rydh, Theorem 5.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx8); [Proposition 2.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#S2.Thmtheorem2)

fields.setting: $k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $\mathcal X^{\prime}$ and $\mathcal X$ are finite type Artin stacks with affine diagonal.
fields.hypotheses: $\mathcal X^{\prime}\to\mathcal X$ is representable.
fields.statement:
For every integer $n\ge0$, the induced map
$$\mathscr J_n(\mathcal X^{\prime})\longrightarrow{\mathscr J_n(\mathcal X)}$$
is representable.
fields.proof: An automorphism of a twisted jet upstairs that becomes the identity downstairs is already the identity, by representability of $\mathcal X^{\prime}\to\mathcal X$. Thus the jet map is injective on stabilizers.

fields.setting:
$k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $\mathcal X/k$ is a smooth equidimensional finite type Artin stack, with affine diagonal and a properly stable good moduli space; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.

$\pi:\mathcal X^{\prime}\to\mathcal X$ is the canonical reduction of stabilizers and $U^{\prime}=\pi^{-1}(\mathcal X^s)$ the inverse image of the stable locus.
fields.hypotheses: $C^{\prime}\subset|\mathscr J(\mathcal X^{\prime})|$ is a bounded cylinder containing no arc entirely in $\mathcal X^{\prime}\setminus U^{\prime}$.
fields.statement:
Its image $C$ is a bounded cylinder and
$$\|\nu_{\mathcal X}(C)\|\le\|\nu_{\mathcal X^{\prime}}(C^{\prime})\|.$$
fields.proof:
Satriano–Usatine’s cylinder-image result gives boundedness. [[coh-lem-3-6|Lemma 3.6]] makes the jet maps representable, so [[coh-lem-3-5|Lemma 3.5]] bounds their constructible-image dimensions; the common motivic normalization gives the measure inequality.

[SU24b, Lemma 12.5](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx16)

fields.setting: $\mathcal X/\mathbb C$ is a smooth equidimensional finite type Artin stack, with affine diagonal and a properly stable good moduli space; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.
fields.hypotheses: $\operatorname{HD}_{\mathrm{str}}(\mathcal X)$ is a {{coh-series|completed Laurent series with integer exponents}}.
fields.statement: $${\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal X}}(\mathcal A_{\mathcal X})\subset\mathbb Z.$$
fields.proof: If a nonintegral weight occurred, [[coh-prop-4-4|Proposition 4.4]] would produce a nonzero diagonal monomial with nonintegral exponent, contradicting the hypothesis.

notations.coh-series: Completed Laurent series with integer exponents and finitely many terms above any total-degree bound.

fields.setting: $\mathcal Z/\mathbb C$ is a nonempty finite type Artin stack with affine geometric stabilizers; $e=\dim\mathcal Z$.
fields.statement: $$[u^pv^p]\operatorname{HD}(\mathrm e(\mathcal Z))=0\quad(p\in\mathbb Z,\ p>e),\qquad [u^ev^e]\operatorname{HD}(\mathrm e(\mathcal Z))>0.$$
fields.proof:
Stratify into quotients by general linear groups and use the dimension-filtration argument of Satriano–Usatine: the class of $\operatorname{GL}_n$ is a monic polynomial in $\mathbb L$, so dividing by it preserves the positive top diagonal term.

[SU23b, Lemma 4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx14)

fields.setting:
$\mathcal X/\mathbb C$ is a smooth equidimensional finite type Artin stack, with affine diagonal and a properly stable good moduli space; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.

$$A^w=\mathcal A_{\mathcal X}\cap\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal X}^{-1}(w).$$
$$e=\log\|\nu_{\mathcal X}(A^w)\|\in\mathbb Z\cup\{-\infty\}.$$
fields.statement:
$$[u^pv^p]\operatorname{HD}(
u_{\mathcal X}(A^w))=0\qquad(p\in\mathbb Z,\ p>e).$$
If $A^w
e\varnothing$, its measure is nonzero and
$$[u^ev^e]\operatorname{HD}(
u_{\mathcal X}(A^w))>0.$$
fields.proof:
[[coh-prop-3-7|Proposition 3.7]] supplies a nonempty cylinder inside a nonempty weight fiber, proving nonzero measure. [[coh-thm-3-1|Theorem 3.1]] approximates that measure by a cylinder without changing its top term, and [[coh-lem-4-2|Lemma 4.2]] gives positivity.

[Proposition 2.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#S2.Thmtheorem2); [SU24b, Theorem 9.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx16)

fields.setting:
$\mathcal X/\mathbb C$ is a smooth equidimensional finite type Artin stack, with affine diagonal and a properly stable good moduli space; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.

$$A^w=\mathcal A_{\mathcal X}\cap\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal X}^{-1}(w).$$
fields.hypotheses:
A nonintegral weight occurs. Choose $q$ among these finitely many weights maximizing
$$-q+e_q,\qquad e_q=\log\|\nu_{\mathcal X}(A^q)\|.$$
fields.statement: $$[u^{d-q+e_q}v^{d-q+e_q}]\operatorname{HD}_{\mathrm{str}}(\mathcal X)>0,\qquad d-q+e_q\notin\mathbb Z.$$
fields.proof: Separate integral from nonintegral weight contributions to the stringy integral. [[coh-lem-4-3|Lemma 4.3]] makes every maximal fractional diagonal contribution positive; smaller contributions and integer-weight terms cannot cancel it.

fields.setting: $k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $\mathcal X/k$ is smooth, finite type and equidimensional, with affine diagonal and a good moduli space; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.
fields.statement:
For every $n\ge0$, $\term{coh-jets}{\mathscr J_n(\mathcal X)}$ is smooth and equidimensional of dimension $(n+1)d$, and
$$\theta_n^{n+1}:\mathscr J_{n+1}(\mathcal X)\to\mathscr J_n(\mathcal X)$$
is smooth of constant relative dimension $d$.
fields.proof:
[[coh-prop-5-4|Proposition 5.4]] gives smooth source and target of the claimed dimensions. Satriano–Usatine identify the fibers as smooth stacky affine spaces of dimension $d$; [[coh-prop-5-5|Proposition 5.5]] gives flatness, hence smoothness.

[SU24b, Proposition 4.11](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx16)

notations.coh-jets: Twisted jets are finite-order arcs whose source can have a cyclic stabilizer.

fields.setting:
$k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$, $k^{\prime}/k$ a field extension, $n\ge0$, $\ell>0$ integers. Set
$$\mathcal D_{n,k^{\prime}}^\ell=[\operatorname{Spec}(k^{\prime}[t^{1/\ell}]/(t^{n+1}))/\mu_\ell].$$
fields.hypotheses: $F$ is locally free of rank $r$ on $\mathcal D_{n,k^{\prime}}^\ell$.
fields.proof:
Split $F$ into character twists of the structure sheaf. Each twist has $n+1$ invariant monomials: $t^{a/\ell},t^{1+a/\ell},\ldots,t^{n+a/\ell}$.

[SU24b, Proposition 3.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx16)

fields.setting: $k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $\mathcal X/k$ is smooth, finite type and equidimensional, with affine diagonal and a good moduli space; $d=\dim\mathcal X$. $k^{\prime}/k$ is any field extension and $\mathscr L_1$ is the ordinary first-jet stack.
fields.statement:
For $n\ge0$ and every point $z:\operatorname{Spec}k^{\prime}\to{\mathscr J_n(\mathcal X)}$, there are $r,s\ge0$ with $r-s=(n+1)d$ such that
$$\mathscr L_1(\mathscr J_n(\mathcal X))\times_{\mathscr J_n(\mathcal X)}\operatorname{Spec}k^{\prime}\cong\mathbb A_{k^{\prime}}^r\times{B\mathbb G_{a,k^{\prime}}^s}.$$
fields.proof:
Deformation theory describes deformations and automorphisms by $\operatorname{Ext}^0$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}$ of the pulled-back cotangent complex. A two-term vector-bundle presentation and [[coh-lem-5-2|Lemma 5.2]] compute the difference of dimensions as $(n+1)d$.

[SU24b, Lemma 2.2 and its truncated-disc variant](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx16)

fields.setting: $k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $\mathcal X/k$ is smooth, finite type and equidimensional, with affine diagonal and a good moduli space; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.
fields.statement: For every integer $n\ge0$, ${\mathscr J_n(\mathcal X)}$ is smooth over $k$ and equidimensional of dimension $(n+1)d$.
fields.proof:
Rydh’s mapping-stack theorem gives smoothness because representable maps form an open substack of the Hom stack. [[coh-prop-5-3|Proposition 5.3]] computes every first-jet fiber dimension, which equals the dimension of its smooth component.

[Rydh, Remark 3.13(v)](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx10); [SU24b, Proposition 4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx16); [SU22, Lemma 3.34](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx12)

fields.setting: $k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ is a morphism of equidimensional finite type Artin stacks, with $\mathcal Y$ Cohen–Macaulay and $\mathcal Z$ regular.
fields.hypotheses: Every field-valued fiber has dimension $\dim\mathcal Y-\dim\mathcal Z$.
fields.statement: $f$ is flat.
fields.proof:
Take smooth scheme covers of source and target with constant relative dimension. The fiber-dimension identity becomes the hypothesis of miracle flatness for schemes, and flatness descends through the smooth covers.

[Vakil, §26.2.11](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx20)

cards.title: Proposition 6.5 (Canonical strata of a constructible set)

fields.setting:
$k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $C\subset|\mathcal Z|$ is constructible in a finite type Artin stack. The canonical reduced strata $\mathcal Y_i^C$ are defined successively by
$$C_0=\overline C\setminus\overline{\overline C\setminus C},\qquad \mathcal Y^C=\coprod_i\mathcal Y_i^C,$$
repeating on $C\setminus C_0$. [Notation 6.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#S6.Thmtheorem1)
fields.statement: Only finitely many are nonempty, and they partition $C$. Thus $\mathcal Y^C$ is finite type; with affine geometric stabilizers, $\mathrm e(C)=\mathrm e(\mathcal Y^C)$.
fields.proof: [[coh-lem-6-2|Lemma 6.2]] reduces to a scheme cover. The first stratum contains the generic points of every component of $\overline C$, so the remaining constructible set has strictly smaller dimension; noetherian induction finishes.

fields.setting: $k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $f:\mathcal W\to\mathcal Z$ is smooth between finite type Artin stacks, $C\subset|\mathcal Z|$ is constructible; put $D=f^{-1}(C)$.
fields.statement:
For every $i\ge0$, the canonical reduced strata satisfy
$${\mathcal Y_i^C}\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal W\cong\mathcal Y_i^D.$$
fields.proof: Smooth maps are open, so inverse image commutes with the closures used at each step. Smooth pullback of each reduced stratum is reduced, giving equality as substacks rather than just equality of supports.

fields.setting: $k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. For constructible $C\subset D\subset|\mathcal Z|$ in a finite type Artin stack, write $C_0=|\mathcal Y_0^C|$, $D_0=|\mathcal Y_0^D|$.
fields.statement: $$C_0\mathbin{\triangle}D_0\subset\overline{D\setminus C}.$$
fields.proof: Use the first-stratum formula and $C_0\subset C$, $D_0\subset D$ from [[coh-prop-6-5|Proposition 6.5]]. A point lost from either first stratum has every neighborhood meeting $D\setminus C$, so belongs to its closure.

fields.setting: $k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $C,D\subset|\mathcal Z|$ are constructible in a finite type Artin stack.
fields.statement:
For each $i\ge0$, there is a common locally closed substack $\mathcal Y_i\subset{\mathcal Y_i^C},\mathcal Y_i^D$ whose complements in both strata are supported on
$$\overline{C\setminus D}\cup\overline{D\setminus C}.$$
fields.proof: Apply [[coh-lem-6-6|Lemma 6.6]] to $C\cap D\subset C,D$ to compare their first strata, using [[coh-prop-6-5|Proposition 6.5]] for containment in the original sets. Remove the first strata and repeat; the residual differences stay inside the same closed error set.

fields.setting: $\mathcal Z/\mathbb C$ is finite type with affine geometric stabilizers, and $C\subset D\subset|\mathcal Z|$ are constructible.
fields.hypotheses: $i>1+2\dim(D\setminus C)$.
fields.statement: $$H_c^i({\mathcal Y^C})\cong H_c^i(\mathcal Y^D).$$
fields.proof: [[coh-prop-6-7|Proposition 6.7]] gives a common part of each pair of strata; [[coh-lem-3-4|Lemma 3.4]] bounds its omitted dimensions. [[coh-lem-6-9|Lemma 6.9]] identifies the cohomologies in the stated range, and the finite direct sums give the result.

fields.setting: $\mathcal Z/\mathbb C$ is finite type with affine geometric stabilizers and $\mathcal W\subset\mathcal Z$ is locally closed.
fields.hypotheses: $i>1+2\dim(|\mathcal Z|\setminus|\mathcal W|)$.
fields.statement: $$H_c^i(\mathcal Z)\cong H_c^i(\mathcal W).$$
fields.proof: Factor the immersion as open followed by closed. [[coh-lem-3-4|Lemma 3.4]] bounds the two complement dimensions; the adjacent complement groups in the localization sequences vanish in the stated degree range, giving both isomorphisms.

fields.setting: $i:\mathcal Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal X$ is closed in a locally finite type Artin stack over $\mathbb C$, with open complement $j:\mathcal U\hookrightarrow\mathcal X$. $K$ is a mixed Hodge-module complex.
fields.statement:
There is a distinguished triangle
$$j_!j^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow i_*i^*K.$$
In particular,
$$\cdots\to H_c^r(\mathcal U)\to H_c^r(\mathcal X)\to H_c^r(\mathcal Z)\to H_c^{r+1}(\mathcal U)\to\cdots.$$
fields.proof:
Use the localization triangle in Tubach’s six-functor formalism. Set $K=\mathbb Q_{\mathcal X}$, use $j^!=j^*$ and $i_*=i_!$, and push forward to a point.

[Tubach, Theorem 3.1(4,5,7)](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx18)

fields.setting: $\mathcal Z/\mathbb C$ is a finite type Artin stack.
fields.statement: $$H_c^i(\mathcal Z)=0\qquad\text{if }i>2\dim\mathcal Z.$$
fields.proof:
[[coh-prop-2-7|Proposition 2.7]] reduces to smooth equidimensional strata. Verdier duality and purity reduce to vanishing of ordinary negative-degree cohomology, which follows from a simplicial scheme presentation.

[Tubach, duality and purity](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx18)

fields.setting: $\mathcal Z/\mathbb C$ is a finite type Artin stack with affine geometric stabilizers.
fields.statement: $$h^{p,q}(H_c^i(\mathcal Z))=0\qquad\text{whenever }p+q>i.$$
fields.proof:
Apply Tubach’s weight bound for compactly supported mixed Hodge-module cohomology of stacks with affine stabilizers.

[Tubach, Proposition 3.22](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx18)

cards.title: Theorem 7.1 (Cohomology of a stacky affine fibration)

fields.setting: $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ is smooth of constant relative dimension $d$ between finite type Artin stacks over $\mathbb C$.
fields.hypotheses: Every fiber over every field extension $k^{\prime}/\mathbb C$ is $\mathbb A_{k^{\prime}}^r\times B\mathbb G_{a,k^{\prime}}^s$ for some $r,s\ge0$.
fields.statement: $$f_!f^!\mathbb Q_{\mathcal Z}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb Q_{\mathcal Z},\qquad H_c^{i+2d}(\mathcal Y)(d)\cong H_c^i(\mathcal Z)\quad(i\in\mathbb Z).$$
fields.proof:
Generic spreading gives the product description over a smooth cover of a dense open substack. [[coh-prop-7-7|Proposition 7.7]] proves the assertion there, and [[coh-lem-7-5|Lemma 7.5]] extends it by noetherian induction; purity gives the cohomological shift.

[SU24b, Lemma 2.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx16); [SU22, Proposition 2.8](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx12); [Tubach, Theorem 3.1(7)](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx18)

fields.setting: $\mathcal Z/\mathbb C$ is a finite type Artin stack with affine geometric stabilizers.
fields.statement:
$${\chi_{\mathrm{Hdg}}}(\mathrm e(\mathcal Z))=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}(-1)^i[H_c^i(\mathcal Z)].$$
The sum converges in the completed Grothendieck ring of polarizable mixed Hodge structures.
fields.proof:
[[coh-prop-2-8|Proposition 2.8]] and [[coh-prop-2-9|Proposition 2.9]] give convergence. [[coh-prop-2-7|Proposition 2.7]] and [[coh-thm-7-1|Theorem 7.1]] verify the scissor and affine-fibration relations; Ekedahl’s localization theorem identifies this realization with $\chi_{\mathrm{Hdg}}$.

[Ekedahl, Theorem 1.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx6)

fields.setting: $g:\mathcal W\to\mathcal Y$ and $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ are morphisms of locally finite type Artin stacks over $\mathbb C$, with $f$ smooth of constant relative dimension.
fields.hypotheses: The co-units for $g$ and $f\circ g$ are isomorphisms on constant mixed Hodge modules.
fields.statement: The co-unit for $f$ is an isomorphism.
fields.proof:
Purity identifies $f^!\mathbb Q_{\mathcal Z}$ with a shift and twist of $\mathbb Q_{\mathcal Y}$. Push the co-unit for $g$ through $f_!$ and use compatibility with composition; two known isomorphisms force the third.

[Tubach, Theorem 3.1(7)](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx18)

fields.setting: $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ is smooth of constant relative dimension between locally finite type Artin stacks over $\mathbb C$, and $g$ is its base change along $h:\mathcal W\to\mathcal Z$.
fields.statement: A co-unit isomorphism for $f$ pulls back to one for $g$. Conversely, if $h$ is a smooth cover, a co-unit isomorphism for $g$ descends to one for $f$.
fields.proof:
Base change and purity identify $h^*(f_!f^!\mathbb Q_{\mathcal Z})$ with $g_!g^!\mathbb Q_{\mathcal W}$ compatibly with the co-unit. Pullback along a smooth cover detects isomorphisms.

[Tubach, Theorem 3.1(4,7)](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx18)

fields.setting: $f:\mathcal W\to\mathcal Y$ is smooth of constant relative dimension between locally finite type Artin stacks over $\mathbb C$.
fields.hypotheses: Its co-unit is an isomorphism after base change to a closed substack $\mathcal Z\subset\mathcal Y$ and its open complement.
fields.statement: The co-unit for $f$ is an isomorphism.
fields.proof: [[coh-prop-2-7|Proposition 2.7]] gives a localization triangle. [[coh-lem-7-4|Lemma 7.4]] identifies the restricted co-units; the long exact sequences and five-lemma give the middle isomorphism.

fields.setting: $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ is a morphism of locally finite type Artin stacks over $\mathbb C$.
fields.hypotheses: After a smooth cover of $\mathcal Z$, $f$ becomes $\mathbb A^r\times\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Z$ for some $r\ge0$.
fields.statement: $$f_!f^!\mathbb Q_{\mathcal Z}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb Q_{\mathcal Z}.$$
fields.proof: Over a point, the affine-space trace is dual to pullback on ordinary cohomology, an isomorphism by contractibility. [[coh-lem-7-4|Lemma 7.4]] extends this by base change and descent.

fields.setting: $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ is a morphism of locally finite type Artin stacks over $\mathbb C$.
fields.hypotheses: After a smooth cover of $\mathcal Z$, $f$ becomes $\mathbb A^r\times B\mathbb G_a^s\times\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Z$ for some $r,s\ge0$.
fields.statement: $$f_!f^!\mathbb Q_{\mathcal Z}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb Q_{\mathcal Z}.$$
fields.proof: The standard $\mathbb G_a^s$-torsor removes the classifying-stack factor. [[coh-prop-7-6|Proposition 7.6]] applies to that torsor and the composite projection; [[coh-lem-7-3|Lemma 7.3]] cancels them, and [[coh-lem-7-4|Lemma 7.4]] descends the result.

fields.setting:
$\mathcal X/\mathbb C$ is smooth, finite type and equidimensional, with affine diagonal and a good moduli space. Set
$$d=\dim\mathcal X,\qquad A\subset|\mathscr J(\mathcal X)|,\qquad C_n=\theta_n(A).$$
fields.hypotheses:
$A$ is measurable, each $C_n$ quasi-compact and locally constructible, and
$$\nu_{\mathcal X}(A)=\lim_n\nu_{\mathcal X}(\theta_n^{-1}(C_n)).$$
fields.statement:
For each $i\in\mathbb Z$, there is $m\ge0$ such that for every $n\ge m$,
$$H_c^{i+2nd}(\term{coh-model}{\mathcal Y^{C_n}})(nd)\cong H_c^{i+2md}(\mathcal Y^{C_m})(md).$$
fields.proof:
Convergence makes $C_n$ differ from the pullback of $C_m$ in dimension below $(i+2nd-1)/2$, so [[coh-cor-6-8|Corollary 6.8]] identifies their cohomology in degree $i+2nd$. [[coh-thm-5-1|Theorem 5.1]] and [[coh-lem-6-2|Lemma 6.2]] make successive pullbacks smooth stacky affine fibrations, and [[coh-thm-7-1|Theorem 7.1]] identifies their normalized cohomologies.

[Proposition 2.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#S2.Thmtheorem2); [SU24b, Proposition 4.11](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx16)

notations.coh-model: The disjoint union of the canonical reduced locally closed strata of this constructible set.

fields.setting:
$\mathcal X/\mathbb C$ is smooth, finite type and equidimensional, with affine diagonal and a good moduli space. Set
$$d=\dim\mathcal X,\qquad A\subset|\mathscr J(\mathcal X)|,\qquad C_n=\theta_n(A).$$
fields.hypotheses:
