$A$ is measurable, each $C_n$ quasi-compact and locally constructible, and
$$\nu_{\mathcal X}(A)=\lim_n\nu_{\mathcal X}(\theta_n^{-1}(C_n)).$$
fields.statement:
For the stable groups $H^i(A)$ supplied by [[coh-thm-8-1|Theorem 8.1]],
$${\chi_{\mathrm{Hdg}}}(\mathbb L^d\nu_{\mathcal X}(A))=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}(-1)^i[H^i(A)].$$
fields.proof: [[coh-prop-6-5|Proposition 6.5]] identifies the cylinder classes with their canonical finite-type models, and [[coh-cor-7-2|Corollary 7.2]] realizes those classes cohomologically. Stabilization handles any fixed finite range of degrees; the bounds $H^i(A)=0$ for $i>2d$ and $h^{p,q}(H^i(A))=0$ for $p+q>i$ make the remaining tails tend to zero.

fields.setting:
$\mathcal X/\mathbb C$ is smooth, finite type, equidimensional and tame, with affine diagonal; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.

$F\subset\term{coh-inertia}{I_{\mu_\ell}(\mathcal X)}$ is a connected component. The map
$$\pi_\ell:\mathscr J_0^\ell(\mathcal X)\to I_{\mu_\ell}(\mathcal X)$$
restricts a zeroth jet to $B\mu_\ell$.
fields.statement:
For every $i\in\mathbb Z$,
$$H_c^{i+2(d-\dim F)}(\pi_\ell^{-1}(F))(d-\dim F)\cong H_c^i(F).$$
fields.proof: Filter the twisted zeroth disc by powers of $t^{1/\ell}$. [[coh-prop-9-3|Proposition 9.3]], [[coh-prop-9-4|Proposition 9.4]] and [[coh-prop-5-5|Proposition 5.5]] make each stage a smooth affine fibration; [[coh-thm-7-1|Theorem 7.1]] computes its trace, and [[coh-thm-5-1|Theorem 5.1]] gives total relative dimension $d-\dim F$.

notations.coh-inertia: The stack of points equipped with an injective action of a cyclic group.

fields.setting:
$k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $\mathcal X/k$ is smooth, finite type, equidimensional and tame, with affine diagonal; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.

$F\subset I_{\mu_\ell}(\mathcal X)$ is connected. For $1\le n\le\ell$, $F_n^\ell$ parametrizes representable maps from
$$[\operatorname{Spec}(k[t^{1/\ell}]/(t^{n/\ell}))/\mu_\ell]$$
whose reduced source maps into $F$. Let $d_a(F)$ be the multiplicity of tangent character $\xi\mapsto\xi^{-a}$, $a\in\mathbb Z/\ell\mathbb Z$.
fields.statement:
$F_n^\ell$ is smooth and equidimensional, with
$$\dim F_n^\ell=\sum_{a=0}^{n-1}d_a(F).$$
In particular, $\dim F=d_0(F)$.
fields.proof:
The representable Hom stack is smooth by Rydh’s theorem. A first-order deformation is a section of the pulled-back tangent bundle, whose character-$a$ summand contributes precisely when $0\le a<n$; summing gives the dimension.

[Rydh, Remark 3.13(v)](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx10); [SU22, Lemma 3.34](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx12); [SU24b, Proposition 3.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19344v1#bib.bibx16)

fields.setting:
$k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $\mathcal X/k$ is smooth, finite type, equidimensional and tame, with affine diagonal; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.

$F\subset I_{\mu_\ell}(\mathcal X)$ is connected. For $1\le n\le\ell$, $F_n^\ell$ parametrizes representable maps from
$$[\operatorname{Spec}(k[t^{1/\ell}]/(t^{n/\ell}))/\mu_\ell]$$
whose reduced source maps into $F$. Let $d_a(F)$ be the multiplicity of tangent character $\xi\mapsto\xi^{-a}$, $a\in\mathbb Z/\ell\mathbb Z$.
fields.hypotheses: $1\le n<\ell$.
fields.statement:
For every field extension $k^{\prime}/k$ and point $\operatorname{Spec}k^{\prime}\to F_n^\ell$,
$$F_{n+1}^\ell\times_{F_n^\ell}\operatorname{Spec}k^{\prime}\cong\mathbb A_{k^{\prime}}^{d_n(F)}.$$
fields.proof: The new square-zero layer is generated by $t^{n/\ell}$ and has character $-n$. Deformation theory identifies the lifts with $H^0((f_0^*T_{\mathcal X})(-n))$, a vector space of dimension $d_n(F)$.

fields.setting:
$k=\overline k$, $\operatorname{char}k=0$. $\mathcal X/k$ is smooth, finite type, equidimensional and tame, with affine diagonal; $d=\dim\mathcal X$.

For a connected component $F\subset {I_{\mu_\ell}(\mathcal X)}$, let ${d_a(F)}$ be its tangent-character multiplicities and set
$$w(F)=d-\frac1\ell\sum_{a=1}^\ell a\,d_{-a}(F),\qquad s_F=d-\frac1\ell\sum_{a=1}^\ell a\,d_a(F).$$
fields.statement: $$-s_F=w(F)+\dim F-d.$$
fields.proof: [[coh-prop-9-3|Proposition 9.3]] gives $\dim F=d_0(F)$. Reindex by $a\mapsto\ell-a$, using periodicity $d_\ell=d_0$ and $\sum_{a=1}^\ell d_a=d$, to obtain the identity.

fields.setting: $V$ is a real inner-product space, with $\|x\|^2=\langle x,x\rangle$.
fields.statement: $$\langle x,y\rangle=\frac14\bigl(\|x+y\|^2-\|x-y\|^2\bigr).$$ The norm determines the inner product.
fields.proof: Expand both squared norms using bilinearity and symmetry; their difference is $4\langle x,y\rangle$.

fields.setting: $V$ is a real vector space with norm $\|\cdot\|$.
fields.statement: The norm comes from an inner product if and only if $$\|x+y\|^2+\|x-y\|^2=2\|x\|^2+2\|y\|^2\qquad(x,y\in V).$$ In that case [[m245-polarization|polarization]] recovers the inner product (Jordan–von Neumann theorem).
fields.proof: Expand the squared norms for the forward direction. Conversely, polarization defines the required inner product.

fields.setting: $V$ is a real or complex inner-product space.
fields.definition: A set $S\subseteq V$ is **orthogonal** if $\langle x,y\rangle=0$ whenever $x,y\in S$ are distinct. A vector is a **unit vector** if $\|x\|=1$. For $x\ne0$, its **normalization** is $\widehat x=x/\|x\|$. An orthogonal set of unit vectors is **orthonormal**.

fields.text: Let $S$ be an [[m245-orthonormal|orthogonal]] set of nonzero vectors. Show that $S$ is linearly independent. Deduce that an orthonormal set in an $n$-dimensional inner-product space has at most $n$ vectors and is a basis if it has $n$.

fields.setting: $B=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ is an [[m245-orthonormal|orthogonal basis]] of a real or complex inner-product space; the pairing is linear in its first slot.
fields.statement: $B'=(\widehat x_1,\ldots,\widehat x_n)$ is orthonormal and $$x=\sum_{i=1}^n\langle x,\widehat x_i\rangle\widehat x_i=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{\langle x,x_i\rangle}{\langle x_i,x_i\rangle}x_i.$$ Thus the coefficients in the first sum are $[x]_{B'}$ and those in the second are $[x]_B$.
fields.proof: For an orthonormal basis, pairing an expansion with its $i$th basis vector extracts the $i$th coefficient (Example 2.3). Substitute $\widehat x_i=x_i/\|x_i\|$ to obtain the orthogonal-basis formula.

fields.text: The vectors $(1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$ form an orthogonal basis of $\mathbb R^2$. Both have norm $\sqrt2$, so [[m245-orthonormal|normalization]] gives $$\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}(1,1),\frac1{\sqrt2}(1,-1)\right),$$ an orthonormal basis.

fields.setting: $V$ is a real or complex inner-product space; the pairing is linear in its first slot.
fields.hypotheses: $(v_1,\ldots,v_k)$ is linearly independent.
fields.statement: Set $$w_1=v_1,\qquad w_i=v_i-\sum_{j<i}\frac{\langle v_i,w_j\rangle}{\langle w_j,w_j\rangle}w_j.$$ The $w_i$ are nonzero and mutually [[m245-orthonormal|orthogonal]], with $$\operatorname{span}(w_1,\ldots,w_i)=\operatorname{span}(v_1,\ldots,v_i)\qquad(1\le i\le k).$$
fields.proof: Inductively, $v_i-w_i$ lies in the preceding span, so adjoining either vector gives the same span; $w_i=0$ would contradict independence. Expanding $\langle w_i,w_j\rangle$ cancels the component along $w_j$.

fields.setting: $V$ is a finite-dimensional real or complex inner-product space.
fields.statement: $V$ has an [[m245-orthonormal|orthonormal basis]].
fields.proof: Apply [[m245-gram-schmidt|Theorem 3.1]] to a basis and normalize the resulting orthogonal vectors.

fields.text: Suppose $(v_1,\ldots,v_{k-1})$ is linearly independent but $(v_1,\ldots,v_k)$ is dependent. Show that the next subtraction in [[m245-gram-schmidt|Gram–Schmidt]] gives $w_k=0$.

For $a,b,c\in\mathbb C$ with $a\ne0$, the roots of $az^2+bz+c$ are $$z=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}.$$ Completing the square proves the formula. Conversely, a monic quadratic with roots $r_1,r_2$ is $$z^2-(r_1+r_2)z+r_1r_2.$$ Its coefficients are [[m145-symmetric|symmetric polynomials]] in the roots.

fields.setting: $f\in\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$.
fields.definition: The polynomial is **symmetric** if $$f(x_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,x_{\sigma(n)})=f(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$$ for every permutation $\sigma\in S_n$. The [[m145-elementary|elementary symmetric polynomials]] are basic examples.

fields.setting: $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are variables over $\mathbb C$.
fields.definition: For $1\le j\le n$, $$e_j(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{1\le i_1<\cdots<i_j\le n}x_{i_1}\cdots x_{i_j}.$$ In particular, $e_1=x_1+\cdots+x_n$ and $e_n=x_1\cdots x_n$. Each $e_j$ is homogeneous of degree $j$.

fields.setting: $f\in\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ is [[m145-symmetric|symmetric]]; $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ are the [[m145-elementary|elementary symmetric polynomials]].
fields.statement: $$f=g(e_1,\ldots,e_n)\quad\text{for some }g\in\mathbb C[t_1,\ldots,t_n].$$
fields.proof: The {{m145-lex|lexicographically}} leading monomial $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}$ has $a_1\ge\cdots\ge a_n$. Subtract its coefficient times $e_1^{a_1-a_2}e_2^{a_2-a_3}\cdots e_n^{a_n}$ to lower the leading monomial. Repetition terminates because the total degree stays bounded, leaving only finitely many possible monomials.

notations.m145-lex: Compare exponent vectors at the first coordinate where they differ.

fields.text: Continuing roots around a loop may permute them: this is **monodromy**. For $w^m=z$ over $z\ne0$, one counterclockwise loop multiplies a chosen root by $e^{2\pi i/m}$ and cycles the $m$ roots.
fields.argument: Along $z(t)=e^{it}$, choose $w(t)=e^{it/m}$; at $t=2\pi$ it reaches the next root.

fields.text: For $w^2=z$, take $z(t)=e^{it}$, $0\le t\le2\pi$, and continue the root $w(0)=1$. Then $w(t)=e^{it/2}$ and $w(2\pi)=-1$. One loop exchanges the roots; two loops return them. At $z=0$ the two roots coincide.

cards.title: The general quintic has no formula by radicals

fields.setting: The general monic quintic is $$z^5+a_4z^4+a_3z^3+a_2z^2+a_1z+a_0,\qquad a_i\in\mathbb C.$$
fields.statement: No formula expresses its roots using the coefficients, constants, finitely many arithmetic operations, and extraction of integer roots (Abel–Ruffini theorem). Individual quintics may still be solvable by radicals.
fields.proof: The general quintic has [[m145-quintic-monodromy|monodromy $S_5$]], while [[m145-solvability|radical expressions have solvable monodromy]]. Since $S_5$ is not solvable, no such formula exists.

fields.setting: $U\subset\mathbb C^5$ parameterizes monic quintics with five distinct roots. Fix a base point and label its roots.
fields.statement: Continuing the roots along loops in $U$ realizes every permutation of those five roots.
fields.context: The excluded **discriminant locus** consists of polynomials with a repeated root. A small transverse loop near a polynomial with exactly one double root exchanges the two nearby roots.

cards.title: A collision of two quintic roots

fields.text: The polynomial $(z-1)^2(z-2)(z-3)(z-4)$ lies on the discriminant locus. In the family $$((z-1)^2-t)(z-2)(z-3)(z-4),$$ a small loop of $t$ around $0$ exchanges $1+\sqrt t$ and $1-\sqrt t$, while the other roots stay fixed. This is [[m145-square-root|square-root monodromy]] inside the quintic family.

A formula built from successive radicals has a {{m145-solvable|solvable}} monodromy group, but $S_5$ is not solvable. A radical tower builds successive cyclic extensions; merely generating a group by cycles is insufficient. In contrast, $S_2,S_3,S_4$ are solvable, as required for quadratic, cubic, and quartic formulas.

notations.m145-solvable: A group that can be broken into successive normal steps with abelian quotient groups.

fields.text: Let $B=(v_1,\ldots,v_k)$ be an ordered basis of a subspace $S\subseteq\mathbb R^n$. Every $a\in S$ has a unique expression $$a=b_1v_1+\cdots+b_kv_k,\qquad {[a]_B}=\begin{pmatrix}b_1\\\vdots\\b_k\end{pmatrix}.$$ The coordinate column has $k=\dim S$ entries, even when the ambient space is larger. Coordinates with respect to $B$ are only defined for vectors in $S$.
fields.examples:
[[m136-plane-example|Compute coordinates in a plane]]
[[m136-reordered|Basis order matters]]
[[m136-reconstruct|Recover a vector from its coordinates]]

fields.text: Let $$S=\{(x_1,x_2,x_3):x_1+2x_2-x_3=0\},\quad B=((-2,1,0),(1,0,1)).$$ For $a=(-5,4,3)$, $$4(-2,1,0)+3(1,0,1)=a,\qquad {[a]_B}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix}.$$ In contrast, $(1,0,0)\notin S$, so it has no $B$-coordinates.

For the plane $S=\{x_3=0\}\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, take the ordered basis $B=((0,1,0),(1,0,0))$. Then $$(-5,4,0)=4(0,1,0)-5(1,0,0),\qquad {[(-5,4,0)]_B}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\-5\end{pmatrix}.$$ The first coordinate belongs to the first listed basis vector.

cards.title: Recover a vector from its coordinates

fields.setting: $B=(v_1,\ldots,v_k)$ and $C$ are ordered bases of $S\subseteq\mathbb R^n$.
fields.definition: The matrix from $B$-coordinates to $C$-coordinates is $${}_CP_B=\begin{bmatrix}[v_1]_C&\cdots&[v_k]_C\end{bmatrix}.$$ It satisfies $$[a]_C={}_CP_B[a]_B\qquad(a\in S).$$ Its columns express the source basis in the target basis.

cards.title: Compute a basis change by row reduction

fields.text: For the plane $x_1+2x_2-x_3=0$, let $$B=((-2,1,0),(1,0,1)),\qquad C=((-1,1,1),(-5,4,3)).$$ Simultaneously solving for the $C$-coordinates of both vectors in $B$ gives $$\left[\begin{array}{cc|cc}-1&-5&-2&1\\1&4&1&0\\1&3&0&1\end{array}\right]\sim\left[\begin{array}{cc|cc}1&0&-3&4\\0&1&1&-1\\0&0&0&0\end{array}\right].$$ Hence $${}_CP_B=\begin{pmatrix}-3&4\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$ These are the columns prescribed by [[m136-change|Definition 5.2.13]].

fields.setting: $B,C$ are ordered bases of the same $k$-dimensional subspace.
fields.statement: The [[m136-change|change-of-coordinates matrices]] satisfy $${}_BP_C\,{}_CP_B=I_k={}_CP_B\,{}_BP_C.$$ Thus ${}_BP_C=({}_CP_B)^{-1}$.
fields.proof: Changing coordinates from $B$ to $C$ and back fixes every coordinate column; the reverse composition does the same.

cards.title: Changing to and from standard coordinates

fields.text: For $B=((1,2,3),(1,0,1),(-2,0,-3))$ in $\mathbb R^3$, the matrix to the standard basis is simply the matrix of basis columns: $${}_{B_{\rm std}}P_B=A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&-2\\2&0&0\\3&1&-3\end{pmatrix}.$$ To convert standard coordinates back to $B$-coordinates, row-reduce $[A\mid I_3]$ to $[I_3\mid A^{-1}]$, as [[m136-inverse|the inverse property]] predicts.

fields.introduction: A complex curve has complex dimension one and real dimension two. A multivalued formula can become a single geometric surface whose projection records its branches.
fields.topics:
[[ag464-graphs|Graphs of holomorphic functions]]
[[ag464-circle-gluing|Gluing the complex circle]]
[[ag464-monodromy|Definition 1.8 · Monodromy]]
[[ag464-square-root|The square-root covering]]

fields.text: For a {{ag464-holomorphic|holomorphic}} function $f:U\to\mathbb C$ on an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb C$, its graph $\Gamma_f=\{(z,f(z)):z\in U\}$ is a Riemann surface, biholomorphic to $U$. The surface $y^2=x$ is likewise biholomorphic to $\mathbb C$ via $(x,y)\mapsto y$.
fields.calculation: Projection onto $z$ has holomorphic inverse $z\mapsto(z,f(z))$. For $y^2=x$, use $y\mapsto(y^2,y)$.

notations.ag464-holomorphic: Complex differentiable in a neighbourhood of every point.

fields.text: The two branches of $\sqrt{1-x^2}$ on $\mathbb C\setminus[-1,1]$ form two sheets. Glue opposite banks of the slit so that the $y$-values match, identifying the endpoints over $x=\pm1$. The resulting affine curve $x^2+y^2=1$ is a cylinder.
fields.calculation: Continuation around either endpoint exchanges the branches. Crosswise gluing joins the sheets into a connected surface with two ends.

fields.setting: $p:X\to Y$ is a degree-$d$ {{ag464-covering|covering}} of connected, locally path-connected spaces. Fix $y_0\in Y$ and label $F=p^{-1}(y_0)$.
fields.definition:
Lifting loops gives an action
$$\rho:\term{ag464-fundamental}{\pi_1(Y,y_0)}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}(F)\cong S_d,\qquad \rho([\gamma])(x)=\widetilde\gamma_x(1).$$
The monodromy group is $\operatorname{im}\rho$. A change of labels conjugates this subgroup; changing the base point uses a chosen connecting path.

notations.ag464-covering: A map that locally looks like disjoint copies of its target.
notations.ag464-fundamental: Loops based at one point, considered up to continuous deformation.

fields.text: The degree-two covering $p:\mathbb C^*\to\mathbb C^*$, $p(z)=z^2$, has fiber $\{1,-1\}$ over $1$. The loop $\gamma(t)=e^{2\pi it}$ lifts to $e^{\pi it}$ from $1$ and $-e^{\pi it}$ from $-1$; each ends at the other root. Thus its [[ag464-monodromy|monodromy]] is the transposition, and the monodromy group is $S_2$.

fields.introduction: A lattice quotient is a compact complex torus. Cubic equations describe an affine part of the same kind of surface; the point at infinity completes the curve.
fields.topics:
[[ag464-lattice-torus|A torus from a lattice]]
[[ag464-cubic-cover|A cubic as a branched double cover]]
[[ag464-elliptic|Definition 2.10 · Elliptic curves]]
[[ag464-weierstrass|The Weierstrass function]]

fields.setting: $\Gamma=\mathbb Z\omega_1+\mathbb Z\omega_2\subset\mathbb C$, where $\omega_1,\omega_2$ are real-linearly independent.
fields.text: Identifying opposite sides of the fundamental parallelogram gives the compact complex torus $\mathbb C/\Gamma$, with group law induced by addition. For $\Gamma=\mathbb Z+i\mathbb Z$, the parallelogram is the unit square.
fields.calculation: Every class has a representative $a\omega_1+b\omega_2$ with $0\le a,b<1$. Holomorphic translations identify the edges and give compatible complex charts.

fields.text: The smooth projective completion of $y^2=x(x-1)(x-2)$ maps to [[ag464-projective-line|$\mathbb P^1$]] by the $x$-coordinate. This map has degree two and {{ag464-branch|branch values}} $0,1,2,\infty$. Cut two spheres along $[0,1]$ and $[2,\infty]$, then glue opposite banks: the result is a torus.
fields.calculation: Each sphere cut along two arcs becomes a cylinder, and joining the corresponding boundaries gives a torus. In $Y^2Z=X(X-Z)(X-2Z)$, setting $Z=0$ forces $X=0$, so the affine cubic acquires the single point $[0:1:0]$.

notations.ag464-branch: A target value where the sheets of a covering come together.

cards.title: Definition 2.10 · Elliptic curves in Weierstrass form

fields.setting:
$a,b\in\mathbb C$, with $4a^3+27b^2
e0$.
fields.definition: The smooth projective curve $$Y^2Z=X^3+aXZ^2+bZ^3$$ with marked point $[0:1:0]$ is an **elliptic curve**. Its affine part is $y^2=x^3+ax+b$, the complement of the marked point.

fields.introduction:
For a lattice $\Gamma\subset\mathbb C$, the {{ag464-meromorphic|meromorphic}} function
$$\wp_\Gamma(z)=\frac1{z^2}+\sum_{\omega\in\Gamma\setminus\{0\}}\left(\frac1{(z-\omega)^2}-\frac1{\omega^2}\right)$$
is $\Gamma$-periodic and descends to [[ag464-lattice-torus|$\mathbb C/\Gamma$]]. Its only pole on the torus is a double pole at $0$, with expansion $\wp(z)=z^{-2}+O(z^2)$.

cards.title: From a torus to a cubic

fields.setting: $\Gamma\subset\mathbb C$ is a lattice, with $g_2=60\sum_{\omega\in\Gamma\setminus\{0\}}\omega^{-4}$ and $g_3=140\sum_{\omega\in\Gamma\setminus\{0\}}\omega^{-6}$.
fields.text:
The [[ag464-weierstrass|Weierstrass function]] satisfies
$$\wp'(z)^2=4\wp(z)^3-g_2\wp(z)-g_3.$$
The map $z\mapsto[\wp(z):\wp'(z)/2:1]$ extends at $z=0$ to $[0:1:0]$ and identifies the torus with the projective cubic
$$Y^2Z=X^3-\frac{g_2}{4}XZ^2-\frac{g_3}{4}Z^3.$$
For the square lattice, $g_3=0$; rescaling the coordinates gives $y^2=x(x-1)(x+1)$.

fields.introduction: Projective coordinates add the missing points at infinity. Homogeneous equations make that addition explicit.
fields.topics:
[[ag464-projective-line|Definition 2.3 · The projective line]]
[[ag464-projective-charts|Two charts and rational functions]]
[[ag464-circle-parameter|A rational parameter for the complex circle]]
[[ag464-projective-plane|The projective plane]]
[[ag464-circle-compact|Compactifying the complex circle]]
[[ag464-cubic-compact|Compactifying a cubic]]
[[ag464-projective-lines|Lines in the projective plane]]

fields.setting: $\mathbb C^2$ has its usual topology.
fields.definition:
The **projective line** is
$$\mathbb P^1=(\mathbb C^2\setminus\{0\})/\sim,\qquad (x,y)\sim(\lambda x,\lambda y),\quad\lambda\in\mathbb C^*.$$
Write an equivalence class as $[x:y]$. Equivalently, $\mathbb P^1$ is the set of one-dimensional linear subspaces of $\mathbb C^2$, with the quotient topology.

cards.title: Two charts on the Riemann sphere

fields.text:
On [[ag464-projective-line|$\mathbb P^1$]], the chart $y\ne0$ has coordinate $z=x/y$, and the chart $x\ne0$ has coordinate $w=y/x$. On the overlap, $w=1/z$. Thus $\mathbb P^1\cong\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$; the missing point of the first chart is $[1:0]$.

A polynomial in $x,y$ invariant under every nonzero scaling is constant. The slope $x/y$ instead defines a rational function, and $\mathbb C(\mathbb P^1)=\mathbb C(x/y)$.
fields.calculation: The inverses of the two chart maps are $z\mapsto[z:1]$ and $w\mapsto[1:w]$. Their transition map is reciprocal, giving the sphere with its two usual complex charts.

cards.title: A rational parameter for the complex circle

fields.text:
The map
$$t\longmapsto\left(\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2},\frac{2t}{1+t^2}\right)$$
identifies $\mathbb P^1\setminus\{i,-i\}$ with $C=\{x^2+y^2=1\}\subset\mathbb C^2$, taking $\infty$ to $(-1,0)$. Thus $C$ is a sphere minus two points.
fields.calculation: Substitution gives $x^2+y^2=1$. Away from $(-1,0)$ the inverse is $t=y/(1+x)$; the remaining point corresponds to $t=\infty$.

fields.text: Write $\mathbb P^2=(\mathbb C^3\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb C^*$. The chart $Z\ne0$ is $\mathbb C^2$ via $[X:Y:Z]\mapsto(X/Z,Y/Z)$; its complement $Z=0$ is [[ag464-projective-line|$\mathbb P^1$]]. Hence $$\mathbb P^2=\mathbb C^2\sqcup\mathbb C\sqcup\{\infty\}.$$ Repeating this decomposition gives $\mathbb P^n=\bigsqcup_{j=0}^n\mathbb C^j$.

The projective compactification of $C=\{x^2+y^2=1\}$ is
$$\overline C=\{[X:Y:Z]\in\mathbb P^2:X^2+Y^2=Z^2\}.$$
The two added points are $[1:i:0]$ and $[1:-i:0]$. This smooth conic is a sphere.
fields.calculation: Substitute $x=X/Z$, $y=Y/Z$ and clear denominators. At $Z=0$, solve $X^2+Y^2=0$; the two points cap the ends of the affine cylinder.

fields.text:
The projective closure is
$$\overline E=\{[X:Y:Z]\in\mathbb P^2:Y^2Z=X(X-Z)(X+Z)\}.$$
Its only added point is $[0:1:0]$. The completion is a torus; the original affine curve is a torus with that point removed.
fields.calculation: At infinity, $Z=0$ forces $X^3=0$, leaving $[0:1:0]$. Glue two spheres along cuts joining the branch values $-1,0$ and $1,\infty$ to obtain a torus.

cards.title: Lines of $\mathbb P^2$ and planes of $\mathbb C^3$

fields.text: A projective line is $\mathbb P(V)$ for a two-dimensional subspace $V\subset\mathbb C^3$. Equivalently, it has an equation $$aX+bY+cZ=0,\qquad(a,b,c)\ne(0,0,0).$$ Under $\pi:\mathbb C^3\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbb P^2$, its inverse image is $V\setminus\{0\}$; adjoining the origin recovers the plane $V$.

fields.introduction: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, GIT constructs quotients from semistable orbits. A graded unipotent radical makes certain non-reductive quotients accessible by affine slices.
fields.Topics:
[[cam-affine|Theorem 1.4 (Affine GIT)]]
[[cam-projective|Theorem 1.7 (Projective GIT)]]
[[cam-hilbert-mumford|Theorem 1.8 (Hilbert–Mumford)]]
[[cam-hkkn|Theorem 1.14 (Instability strata)]]
[[cam-twisted|Twisted affine GIT]] → [[cam-uhat|Theorem 1.23 (The $\widehat U$ theorem)]]
[[cam-weighted|Weighted hypersurfaces]]

fields.setting: $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero.
fields.definition: A linear algebraic group is an affine group scheme of finite type. It is reductive if every finite-dimensional rational representation is a direct sum of irreducible representations. It is unipotent if it embeds as a closed subgroup of upper triangular matrices with diagonal entries $1$.

fields.setting: $G$ acts on a projective scheme $X$.
fields.definition: A projective linearization is a $G$-equivariant closed embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P(V)$ for a finite-dimensional representation $V$. It gives $\mathcal O_X(1)$ a compatible $G$-action.

fields.setting: A [[cam-groups|reductive group]] $G$ acts on $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of finite type over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.
fields.statement: $A^G$ is finitely generated, and $$X\longrightarrow X/\!/G:=\operatorname{Spec}A^G$$ is a {{cam-good-quotient|good quotient}}. Two orbits have the same image iff their closures meet.

notations.cam-good-quotient: An invariant affine quotient that preserves invariant functions and separates disjoint closed invariant sets.

fields.setting: $G$ is reductive over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, acting on projective $X=\operatorname{Proj}A$ with a [[cam-linearization|linearization]].
fields.statement: The semistable locus $$X^{ss}=\{x:\exists n>0,\ f\in A_n^G,\ f(x)\ne0\}$$ has a good quotient $X^{ss}\to\operatorname{Proj}A^G$ with projective target. On $$X^s=\{x\in X^{ss}:Gx\text{ is closed in }X^{ss},\ \dim G_x=0\},$$ the quotient is geometric with quasi-projective target.
fields.proof: Cover $X^{ss}$ by invariant affine opens, apply [[cam-affine|Theorem 1.4]], and glue the quotients.

fields.setting: Reductive $G$ acts on projective $X\subset\mathbb P(V)$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Fix a maximal torus $T$ and the convex hull $\operatorname{Conv}_T(x)$ of the $T$-weights occurring in a representative of $x$.
fields.statement: $x$ is semistable iff $0\in\operatorname{Conv}_T(gx)$ for every $g\in G$. It is stable iff $0$ lies in the interior in $X^*(T)\otimes\mathbb R$ for every $g\in G$.
fields.Example: For the diagonal $\mathrm{SL}_2$-action on $(\mathbb P^1)^n$ with equal weights, semistability means no point occurs more than $n/2$ times; stability requires strictly fewer.

fields.setting: Reductive $G$ acts linearly on projective $X$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Fix a Weyl-invariant norm on one-parameter subgroups and an unstable point $x$.
fields.statement: The function $M(x,\lambda)=\mu(x,\lambda)/\|\lambda\|$ attains its negative minimum. The minimizing rays determine one parabolic $$P(x)=P(\lambda)=\{g:\lim_{t\to0}\lambda(t)g\lambda(t)^{-1}\text{ exists}\}.$$ Their primitive representatives are conjugate under $P(x)$.

fields.setting: Reductive $G$ acts linearly on projective $X$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, with an invariant norm. The parabolics $P_\beta$ and attracting slices $Y_\beta^{ss}$ come from [[cam-optimal|optimal destabilization]].
fields.statement: There is a finite set of instability types $B$ and a stratification $$X=\bigsqcup_{\beta\in B}S_\beta,\qquad S_0=X^{ss},\qquad S_\beta\cong G\times^{P_\beta}Y_\beta^{ss}.$$ The closure of $S_\beta$ lies in the union of strata with $\|\gamma\|\ge\|\beta\|$.
fields.Quotients: Quotienting $S_\beta$ by $G$ reduces to quotienting $Y_\beta^{ss}$ by $P_\beta$, whose unipotent radical is [[cam-graded|graded]].

fields.calculation: The transformations $$z\longmapsto z+ax^2+bxy+cy^2$$ form a normal unipotent subgroup $\mathbb G_a^3$ of its automorphism group.
fields.result: Degree-$d$ weighted homogeneous polynomials parameterize hypersurfaces. Quotienting by automorphisms is a non-reductive GIT problem.

fields.setting: $H=U\rtimes R$ is a linear algebraic group in characteristic zero, with unipotent radical $U$ and reductive Levi subgroup $R$.
fields.definition: The radical is graded if some $$\lambda:\mathbb G_m\to Z(R)$$ acts on $\operatorname{Lie}U$ with strictly positive weights. Write $\widehat U=U\rtimes\lambda(\mathbb G_m)$.

fields.setting: $H=U\rtimes R$ has a [[cam-graded|graded unipotent radical]] and acts linearly on projective $X\subset\mathbb P(V)$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Set $$Z_{\min}=X\cap\mathbb P(V_{\min}),\qquad X^\circ_{\min}=\{x:\lim_{t\to0}\lambda(t)x\in Z_{\min}\}.$$
fields.hypotheses: $\operatorname{Stab}_U(z)=\{e\}$ for every $z\in Z_{\min}$, and the character twist is {{cam-well-adapted|well-adapted}}.
fields.statement: $X^\circ_{\min}\setminus UZ_{\min}$ has a geometric $\widehat U$-quotient with projective target $X/\!/\widehat U$. A residual quotient by $R/\lambda(\mathbb G_m)$ gives a projective good quotient of a suitable $H$-semistable locus.
fields.proof: Over affine opens of $Z_{\min}$, apply [[cam-graded-slice|Propositions 1.31–1.32]] successively along a filtration of $U$ with additive quotients. The invariant rings are finitely generated; twisted affine GIT glues their quotients over $Z_{\min}$, and reductive GIT gives the residual quotient.

notations.cam-well-adapted: A small character twist placing zero just above the lowest grading weight.

fields.setting: Reductive $G$ acts on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, with character $\chi:G\to\mathbb G_m$.
fields.text: Put $$R_\chi=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\{f\in A:g\cdot f=\chi(g)^nf\}.$$ The locus where a positive-degree semi-invariant is nonzero has quotient $\operatorname{Proj}R_\chi$, projective over $\operatorname{Spec}A^G$. An auxiliary variable of opposite character identifies $R_\chi$ with an invariant ring.

fields.setting: $A$ is a $k$-algebra.
fields.definition: A derivation is a $k$-linear map $D:A\to A$ satisfying $D(fg)=fD(g)+gD(f)$. It is locally nilpotent if every $f\in A$ satisfies $D^n(f)=0$ for some integer $n\ge1$.

fields.setting: $A$ is a $k$-algebra in characteristic zero.
fields.statement: Algebraic $\mathbb G_a$-actions on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ correspond to [[cam-lnd|locally nilpotent derivations]] via $$\sigma^*(f)=\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{D^n(f)}{n!}t^n,\qquad D(f)=\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\sigma^*(f)\right|_{t=0}.$$ Their invariant ring is $A^{\mathbb G_a}=\ker D$.

fields.setting: A $\mathbb G_a$-action on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ has [[cam-lnd|derivation]] $D$.
fields.definition:
A slice is $s\in A$ with $D(s)=1$. A local slice satisfies $D^2(s)=0$ and $D(s)\ne0$.

If $t=D(s)$, then $t\in\ker D$ and $s/t$ is a slice in $A_t$. The plinth ideal is $\ker D\cap\operatorname{im}D\subset\ker D$.

fields.setting: A $\mathbb G_a$-action on $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ over a characteristic-zero field has derivation $D$.
fields.statement:
The following are equivalent:

- A [[cam-slice|slice]] $s\in A$ exists.
- $A=(\ker D)[s]$ and $D=\partial/\partial s$.
- $X\cong X'\times\mathbb A^1$ equivariantly, with translation on $\mathbb A^1$ and trivial action on $X'$.

fields.setting: $\mathbb G_a\rtimes\mathbb G_m$ acts on $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. The torus grades $\operatorname{Lie}\mathbb G_a$ positively, and every $\lim_{t\to0}\lambda(t)x$ exists.
fields.statement:
A [[cam-slice|slice]] exists iff the additive action has no fixed point. Equivalently, the additive stabilizer is trivial on the limit locus.

A $\mathbb G_a$-action admits a slice iff it extends to such a semidirect-product action with trivial additive stabilizers on the limit locus.

fields.introduction: The scalar-curvature equation is a moment-map equation. Complexified orbits fix a Kähler class; test configurations give an algebraic stability criterion.
fields.Topics:
[[cam-canonical|Theorem 2.2 (Canonically polarized moduli)]]
[[cam-moment-map|Theorem 2.4 (Scalar curvature as a moment map)]]
[[cam-complexified|Propositions 2.5–2.6 (Complexified orbits)]]
[[cam-k-stability|Test configurations and K-polystability]]
[[cam-deformations|Theorem 2.7 (Small deformations)]]
[[cam-blowups|Canonical metrics on blowups]]

fields.setting: Compact complex manifolds $M$ have ample canonical bundle and polarization $[\omega]=c_1(K_M)=-c_1(M)$.
fields.statement: They admit a Hausdorff complex moduli space.

fields.setting: $(M,\omega_0)$ is compact symplectic, and $\mathcal J$ is the space of $\omega_0$-compatible almost complex structures, with its natural symplectic form.
fields.statement: The Hamiltonian symplectomorphism group acts on $\mathcal J$ with a moment map given by Hermitian scalar curvature, up to a constant. On the integrable locus, $$\mu(J)=s(\omega_0,J)-\widehat s,$$ where $\widehat s$ is the average scalar curvature. Its zeroes are constant-scalar-curvature Kähler structures.

fields.setting: $(M,\omega_0)$ is compact symplectic. On the integrable locus of compatible complex structures, let $D$ be the tangent distribution generated by Hamiltonian orbits and their complex multiples.
fields.statement: $D$ is formally integrable. If $[\omega_0]=c_1(L)$, its leaf through $J$ consists of pullbacks of $J$ by diffeomorphisms matching $\omega_0$ to Kähler forms in $[\omega_0]$.
fields.Consequence: Solving [[cam-moment-map|the moment-map equation]] on this leaf is equivalent to finding a cscK metric in the fixed Kähler class.

fields.setting: $(M,L)$ is a smooth polarized projective variety of dimension $n$.
fields.text:
A normal test configuration is a flat $\mathbb C^*$-equivariant family over $\mathbb A^1$, with a relatively ample equivariant line bundle and general fiber $(M,L^r)$ for some $r>0$.

Compactify over $\mathbb P^1$ and normalize the polarization to a rational line bundle $\mathcal L$ restricting to $L$. The Donaldson–Futaki invariant, up to a positive factor, is $$\operatorname{DF}(\mathcal X,\mathcal L)=\frac{n\mu}{n+1}\mathcal L^{n+1}+K_{\mathcal X/\mathbb P^1}\cdot\mathcal L^n,\qquad\mu=\frac{c_1(M)\cdot L^{n-1}}{L^n}.$$

K-polystability requires $\operatorname{DF}\ge0$, with equality only for product test configurations. The Yau–Tian–Donaldson conjecture equates K-polystability with cscK existence; Chen–Donaldson–Sun establish the smooth Fano case.

fields.setting: $(M,L)$ carries a cscK metric. Its compact Hamiltonian isometry group $K$ acts on a sufficiently small local space of integrable polarized deformations, with complexification $K^{\mathbb C}$.
fields.statement: A small deformation admits a cscK metric in its polarization iff its local $K^{\mathbb C}$-orbit is polystable. Equivalently, it is K-polystable (Corollary 2.8).

fields.setting: $(M,\omega,J)$ is cscK, $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ are distinct points, and $\mu:M\to\operatorname{Lie}K^\vee$ is the moment map for Hamiltonian isometries.
fields.text: If $$\sum_i\mu(p_i)=0,\qquad\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Bl}_{p_1,\ldots,p_m}M)=\{e\},$$ then, for sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the blowup has a cscK metric in $$\pi^*[\omega]-\varepsilon^2\sum_i[E_i],$$ where $E_i$ are the exceptional divisors.

fields.introduction: Stacks retain families and automorphisms. Coarse moduli spaces parameterize individual isomorphism classes; good moduli spaces identify objects with the same closed specialization.
fields.Topics:
[[cam-stack-definition|Definition 3.1 (Algebraic stacks)]]
[[cam-quotient-stack|Quotient stacks]]
[[cam-coarse|Definition 3.8 (Coarse moduli spaces)]]
[[cam-good|Definition 3.11 (Good moduli spaces)]]
[[cam-local|Theorem 3.19 (Local quotient structure)]]
[[cam-existence|Theorem 3.25 (Existence of good moduli spaces)]]
[[cam-intrinsic|Intrinsic moduli construction]]
[[cam-topological|A return to non-reductive GIT]]

fields.definition:
An algebraic stack is a stack in groupoids on schemes for the étale topology, with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas from a scheme. It is Deligne–Mumford if it admits an étale atlas, equivalently if its diagonal is unramified.

For finite-type stacks with affine stabilizers over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the Deligne–Mumford condition is equivalent to finite geometric stabilizers.

fields.setup: An algebraic group $G$ acts on a scheme $X$.
fields.result: An object of $[X/G]$ over $T$ is a $G$-torsor $P\to T$ with a $G$-equivariant map $P\to X$. Geometric points represent orbits, with stabilizers as automorphism groups. Quasi-coherent sheaves on $[X/G]$ correspond to $G$-equivariant sheaves on $X$.
fields.Examples: $BG=[\operatorname{Spec}k/G]$ classifies $G$-torsors. The stack $\Theta=[\mathbb A^1/\mathbb G_m]$ has a nonzero orbit specializing to the origin, whose stabilizer is $\mathbb G_m$.

fields.setting: $\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack.
fields.definition: A coarse moduli space is a map $\pi:\mathcal X\to X$ to an algebraic space, universal for maps to algebraic spaces and bijective on geometric points up to isomorphism.
fields.Examples: $BG\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, weighted projective stacks mapping to weighted projective spaces, and $[X^s/G]\to X^s/G$ from [[cam-projective|stable GIT]].

fields.setting: $\pi:\mathcal X\to X$ maps an algebraic stack to an algebraic space.
fields.definition: It is a good moduli space if it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $$\pi_*:\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{QCoh}(X)\ \text{is exact},\qquad\mathcal O_X\cong\pi_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}.$$
fields.Examples: For reductive $G$ in characteristic zero, $[\operatorname{Spec}A/G]\to\operatorname{Spec}A^G$ and $[X^{ss}/G]\to X/\!/G$.

fields.setting: $\pi:\mathcal X\to X$ is a [[cam-good|good moduli space]] in the finite-type noetherian setting.
fields.text:
- $\pi$ is universally closed, with one closed point in each geometric fiber.
- Every map to an algebraic space factors uniquely through $X$.
- Good moduli spaces commute with arbitrary base change on $X$.
- Finite type descends to $X$, and $\pi_*$ preserves coherent sheaves.
fields.Example: For the weight-$(1,-1)$ action on $\mathbb A^2$, the quotient is $(x,y)\mapsto xy$. Both punctured axes and the origin map to $0$; the origin is the unique closed orbit in that fiber.

fields.setting: $\mathcal X$ is a finite-type algebraic stack with affine diagonal over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.
fields.hypotheses: $x$ is closed and its stabilizer $G_x$ is reductive.
fields.statement: There is a pointed étale neighbourhood $$([\operatorname{Spec}A/G_x],w)\longrightarrow(\mathcal X,x)$$ with $w$ closed and the same stabilizer as $x$. If $\mathcal X$ has a good moduli space, these may be chosen as étale Cartesian charts on that space near the image of $x$ (Corollary 3.21).

fields.setting: $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ is étale between noetherian algebraic stacks with good moduli spaces $U,V$.
fields.hypotheses: $u$ is closed, $f$ preserves its stabilizer, and $f(u)$ is closed in its moduli fiber.
fields.statement: After shrinking around the image of $u$ in $U$, the induced map $U\to V$ is étale and the square of stacks and moduli spaces is Cartesian.

fields.setting: For a DVR $R$, put $\Theta_R=[\mathbb A^1_R/\mathbb G_m]$ and remove its closed origin $0$.
fields.definition: An algebraic stack $\mathcal X$ is $\Theta$-reductive ($\Theta$-complete) if every map $\Theta_R\setminus\{0\}\to\mathcal X$ extends uniquely, up to unique isomorphism, to $\Theta_R\to\mathcal X$, for every $R$.

fields.setting: For a DVR $R$ with uniformizer $\pi$, put $$\overline{\mathrm{ST}}_R=[\operatorname{Spec}R[s,t]/(st-\pi)\,/\mathbb G_m],$$ where $s,t$ have weights $1,-1$, and remove the closed origin $s=t=0$.
fields.definition: An algebraic stack $\mathcal X$ is S-complete if every map from this punctured stack extends uniquely, up to unique isomorphism, over the origin, for every $R$.

fields.setting: $\mathcal X$ is a finite-type algebraic stack with affine diagonal over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.
fields.statement: $\mathcal X$ admits a separated [[cam-good|good moduli space]] iff it is [[cam-theta|$\Theta$-reductive]] and [[cam-s-complete|S-complete]].
fields.proof: S-completeness gives reductive closed stabilizers and stabilizer compatibility. [[cam-local|Theorem 3.19]] supplies local quotient charts. The extension conditions let [[cam-luna|Luna’s lemma]] descend their overlaps to an étale equivalence relation; its quotient is the moduli space.

fields.introduction:
1. Realize the moduli problem as an open substack $\mathcal M$ of an algebraic stack.
2. Prove boundedness.
3. Check separation or the extension conditions in [[cam-existence|Theorem 3.25]] to obtain a moduli space.
4. Prove the existence part of the valuative criterion for properness.
5. Construct an ample line bundle for projectivity.
fields.Topics: [[cam-good-properties|Properties of good moduli spaces]]

fields.setting: A group with [[cam-graded|graded unipotent radical]] acts linearly on projective $X$.
fields.text: Contraction to $Z_{\min}$ gives a {{cam-topological-moduli|topological moduli space}} $$[X^\circ_{\min}/\widehat U]\longrightarrow Z_{\min}.$$ If $\operatorname{Stab}_U(z)=\{e\}$ for every $z\in Z_{\min}$, the closed stabilizers are reductive. Theorem 3.32 makes the quotient a good moduli space; a character twist recovers the projective quotient in [[cam-uhat|Theorem 1.23]].

notations.cam-topological-moduli: A quotient retaining the unique closed specialization in each fiber.

fields.text: [[pw-derived-category|Derived categories]] identify quasi-isomorphic complexes. [[pw-derived-functor|Derived functors]] compute cohomology, while exact triangles ([[pw-triangles|Theorem 1.5]]) encode its exact sequences. [[pw-t-structure|$t$-structures]] select abelian hearts, including [[pw-perverse|perverse sheaves]].

fields.setting: $\mathcal A$ is abelian; $A^\bullet,B^\bullet$ are complexes.
fields.definition: A chain map $f:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ is null-homotopic if maps $h^i:A^i\to B^{i-1}$ satisfy $$f^i=d_B^{i-1}h^i+h^{i+1}d_A^i.$$ The homotopy category $K(\mathcal A)$ has complexes as objects and chain maps modulo null-homotopic maps as morphisms.

fields.setting: $\mathcal A$ is an abelian category.
fields.definition: $D(\mathcal A)$ is the localization of [[pw-homotopy|$K(\mathcal A)$]] at quasi-isomorphisms. Morphisms are roofs $$A^\bullet\xleftarrow{\simeq}C^\bullet\longrightarrow B^\bullet,$$ modulo common refinements in $K(\mathcal A)$. The subcategories $D^+,D^-,D^b$ have cohomology bounded below, above, or both. The shift convention is $A[n]^i=A^{i+n}$.

fields.setting: $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ is left exact and additive; $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives.
fields.definition: For $A^\bullet\in D^+(\mathcal A)$, choose a quasi-isomorphism $A^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ with $I^\bullet$ bounded below and injective. Then $$RF(A^\bullet)=F(I^\bullet),\qquad R^iF(A^\bullet)=H^i(RF(A^\bullet)).$$

fields.setting: $\mathcal A$ is an abelian category.
fields.statement: The [[pw-derived-category|derived category]] $D(\mathcal A)$ is triangulated, with distinguished triangles isomorphic to $$X^\bullet\xrightarrow fY^\bullet\longrightarrow\operatorname{Cone}(f)\longrightarrow X^\bullet[1].$$
fields.proof: Take $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$ with differential $\begin{pmatrix}d_Y&f\\0&-d_X\end{pmatrix}$; mapping cones supply the triangle operations.

fields.setting: $D$ is triangulated, with full subcategories $D^{\le0},D^{\ge0}$. Set $D^{\le n}=D^{\le0}[-n]$, $D^{\ge n}=D^{\ge0}[-n]$.
fields.definition:
They form a $t$-structure when:

1. $D^{\le-1}\subseteq D^{\le0}$ and $D^{\ge1}\subseteq D^{\ge0}$.
2. $\operatorname{Hom}(D^{\le0},D^{\ge1})=0$.
3. Every $X$ fits into a triangle $X_0\to X\to X_1\to X_0[1]$ with $X_0\in D^{\le0}$ and $X_1\in D^{\ge1}$.

It is bounded if every object lies in some $D^{\ge a}\cap D^{\le b}$. Its heart $D^{\le0}\cap D^{\ge0}$ is abelian by [[pw-heart|Theorem 1.7]].

fields.setting: $(D^{\le0},D^{\ge0})$ is a [[pw-t-structure|$t$-structure]] on $D$.
fields.statement: Its heart $\mathcal A=D^{\le0}\cap D^{\ge0}$ is abelian.

fields.setting: $X$ is a complex algebraic variety.
fields.definition: A stratification is a locally finite partition into locally closed strata $X_\alpha$, each closure being a union of strata. A sheaf of $\mathbb Q$- or $\mathbb C$-vector spaces is constructible if it is locally constant of finite rank on such strata. $D_c^b(X)$ consists of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology.

fields.setting: $X$ is a complex algebraic variety; $\mathbb D$ is Verdier duality on [[pw-constructible|$D_c^b(X)$]].
fields.definition: The middle perverse $t$-structure is $$\begin{aligned}F\in{}^pD^{\le0}&\iff\dim\operatorname{supp}H^j(F)\le-j\quad\forall j,\\F\in{}^pD^{\ge0}&\iff\dim\operatorname{supp}H^j(\mathbb DF)\le-j\quad\forall j.\end{aligned}$$ Perverse sheaves form its abelian heart ([[pw-heart|Theorem 1.7]]).
fields.example: [[pw-perverse-examples|Local systems]] on a smooth $d$-fold are perverse after shift $[d]$.

fields.setting: $X$ is smooth of complex dimension $d$ and $L\ne0$ is a local system.
fields.statement: $L[n]$ is [[pw-perverse|perverse]] exactly when $n=d$. A skyscraper sheaf is perverse in degree zero; a local system on a smooth curve becomes perverse after $[1]$, also after pushforward by a closed embedding.
fields.proof: The support conditions for $L[n]$ and its Verdier dual $L^\vee[2d-n]$ give $d\le n$ and $n\le d$.

fields.setting: $C$ is a smooth projective complex curve of genus $g\ge2$, with rank $n\ge1$, degree $d$, and $\gcd(n,d)=1$.
fields.text:
$M_{\mathrm{Dol}}$ parametrizes stable Higgs bundles $(E,\theta:E\to E\otimes\omega_C)$ of rank $n$ and degree $d$. The Hitchin map records the characteristic polynomial: $$h:M_{\mathrm{Dol}}\to A=\bigoplus_{i=1}^nH^0(C,\omega_C^i).$$ Its fibres are described by [[pw-spectral|spectral curves]].

$M_B$ is the simultaneous-conjugation GIT quotient $$\left\{(A_i,B_i)\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb C)^{2g}:\prod_{i=1}^g[A_i,B_i]=e^{2\pi id/n}I_n\right\}\!\mathbin{/\!/}\operatorname{GL}_n.$$ Both moduli spaces are smooth, $h$ is projective, and nonabelian Hodge theory identifies their cohomology.

fields.setting: $M_{\mathrm{Dol}}$ and $M_B$ are the coprime [[pw-moduli|Dolbeault and Betti moduli]] of a smooth projective complex curve of genus at least two.
fields.statement: Under nonabelian Hodge theory, $$\card{pw-perverse-filtration}{P_kH^*(M_{\mathrm{Dol}},\mathbb Q)}=\card{pw-weight}{W_{2k}H^*(M_B,\mathbb Q)}=W_{2k+1}H^*(M_B,\mathbb Q).$$ This is the de Cataldo–Hausel–Migliorini conjecture, proved by Maulik–Shen.
fields.proof: [[pw-twisted-support|Theorem 2.22]], Maulik–Shen critical charts, and Yun’s global Springer theory establish $c_k(\gamma)\cup P_i\subseteq P_{i+k}$. Applying these operators to $1\in P_0$ gives the product bound in [[pw-pw-criterion|Proposition 2.21]], hence $P=W$.

fields.setting: $X$ is a compact Kähler manifold.
fields.statement: $$H^k(X,\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(X),\qquad H^{p,q}(X)=H^q(X,\Omega_X^p),\qquad\overline{H^{p,q}}=H^{q,p}.$$ This is a pure Hodge structure of weight $k$.

fields.setting: $V$ is a finitely generated abelian group.
fields.definition: A mixed Hodge structure consists of finite filtrations $W_\bullet$ increasing on $V_\mathbb Q$ and $F^\bullet$ decreasing on $V_\mathbb C$, such that $\operatorname{Gr}^W_kV=W_k/W_{k-1}$ with the induced $F$ is a pure [[pw-hodge|Hodge structure]] of weight $k$. For smooth varieties, logarithmic forms construct these filtrations via [[pw-logarithmic|Proposition 2.5]].

fields.setting: $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is the complement of a simple normal crossing divisor $D$ in a smooth complex variety.
fields.statement:
$$Rj_*\mathbb C_U\simeq\Omega_X^\bullet(\log D),\qquad H^k(U,\mathbb C)\cong\mathbb H^k(X,\Omega_X^\bullet(\log D)).$$ Locally at $D=(z_1\cdots z_r=0)$, logarithmic one-forms are generated by $dz_i/z_i$ for $i\le r$ and $dz_i$ for $i>r$.

If $X$ is proper, form-degree truncation gives $F$. Filtering by the number of logarithmic factors gives $$W_mH^k(U)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\mathbb H^k(X,W_{m-k}\Omega_X^\bullet(\log D))\to H^k(U)\bigr).$$

fields.setting: $E$ is an elliptic curve, with rank-one moduli $M_B=(\mathbb C^*)^2$ and $M_{\mathrm{Dol}}=\operatorname{Pic}^d(E)\times\mathbb C\cong E\times\mathbb C$.
fields.statement: Under their common topology $(S^1)^2\times\mathbb R^2$, the Hitchin projection satisfies $P_k=W_{2k}=H^{\le k}$.
fields.proof: $H^0,H^1,H^2$ of $(\mathbb C^*)^2$ have weights $0,2,4$, while $$Rh_*\mathbb Q_{E\times\mathbb C}=\mathbb Q_\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb Q_\mathbb C^2[-1]\oplus\mathbb Q_\mathbb C[-2].$$ Its normalized perverse filtration is the Leray filtration, giving the same pieces.

fields.setting: $f:X\to Y$ is proper between smooth complex varieties. Set $d_X=\dim X$, $r=\dim(X\times_YX)-d_X$, and $K=Rf_*\mathbb Q_X[d_X-r]$.
fields.definition: Using the [[pw-perverse|perverse $t$-structure]], $$P_kH^m(X)=\operatorname{im}\left[\mathbb H^{m-d_X+r}(Y,{}^p\tau_{\le k}K)\to H^m(X,\mathbb Q)\right].$$ For the Hitchin map, $r=\dim A$ and the filtration starts at $P_0$.
fields.lefschetz: For an $f$-ample class $\eta$, relative hard Lefschetz gives $\eta^i:\operatorname{Gr}^P_{r-i}H^m\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Gr}^P_{r+i}H^{m+2i}$.

fields.setting: $\mathcal U$ is a universal bundle on $C\times M_{\mathrm{Dol}}$ for the coprime [[pw-moduli|Higgs moduli]], with projections $p$ to $M_{\mathrm{Dol}}$ and $q$ to $C$.
fields.statement: The classes $$c_k(\gamma)=p_*\bigl(q^*\gamma\cdot\operatorname{ch}_k(\mathcal U)\bigr),\qquad\gamma\in H^*(C,\mathbb Q),$$ generate $H^*(M_{\mathrm{Dol}},\mathbb Q)$ as an algebra (Markman). Weight and perversity statements use the {{pw-normalized|normalized Chern character}}.

notations.pw-normalized: The universal Chern character adjusted so its first Chern class lies in $H^1(C)⊗ H^1(M)$.

fields.setting: $N$ is the moduli of stable vector bundles of coprime rank $n$ and degree $d$ on a smooth projective complex curve $C$.
fields.statement: $H^*(N,\mathbb Q)$ is generated by universal-bundle tautological classes.
fields.proof: On $N\times N$, the derived Hom complex of the two universal bundles degenerates on the diagonal. Porteous and Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch express the diagonal class in tautological classes; its action as the identity forces these classes to generate.

fields.setting: $C$ is a smooth projective curve and $\gcd(n,d)=1$.
fields.text:
A Higgs field makes $E$ a $\operatorname{Sym}(T_C)$-module, hence a sheaf on $T^*C$ finite over $C$. Its characteristic polynomial defines a spectral curve $C_a\subset T^*C$.

For integral $C_a$, pushing forward rank-one torsion-free sheaves of the corresponding degree identifies the Hitchin fibre with the compactified Jacobian $\overline J(C_a)$. For smooth $C_a$, this is the ordinary Jacobian.

fields.setting: $f:X\to Y$ is proper between complex algebraic varieties, with $X$ smooth.
fields.text: The Beilinson–Bernstein–Deligne–Gabber decomposition theorem gives $$Rf_*\mathbb Q_X\simeq\bigoplus_i{}^pH^i(Rf_*\mathbb Q_X)[-i].$$ Each perverse cohomology sheaf is semisimple with summands $\operatorname{IC}_Z(L)$, where $Z$ is irreducible closed and $L$ is an irreducible local system on a smooth dense open subset. These $Z$ are the supports of $f$.

fields.setting: $f:X\to Y$ is proper and surjective, with $X,Y$ smooth and every fibre of dimension $d$.
fields.hypotheses: $Z$ is a [[pw-decomposition|support]] of $f$.
fields.statement: $\operatorname{codim}_Y Z\le d$. Equality forces $Z$ to occur in $R^{2d}f_*\mathbb Q_X$ on a suitable open subset.
fields.proof: Verdier duality gives a perverse degree $m\ge\dim X$ supported on $Z$. Its local system occurs in ordinary degree $m-\dim Z\le2d$, yielding the bound and its equality case.

cards.title: Theorem 2.17 (Ngô’s support theorem on the integral locus)

fields.setting: $A^0$ is the integral spectral locus of the [[pw-moduli|Hitchin system]], and $h^0:h^{-1}(A^0)\to A^0$.
fields.statement: The only [[pw-decomposition|support]] of $h^0$ is $A^0$.
fields.proof: Let $\delta(Z)$ be the generic dimension of the affine part of $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C_a)$ along $Z$. Severi’s inequality and Ngô’s enhanced support bound give $\delta(Z)\le\operatorname{codim}Z\le\delta(Z)$ for every support, with equality forcing detection in top fibre cohomology. Integral locally planar spectral curves have irreducible compactified Jacobians, so the top direct image is a rank-one local system on $A^0$.

fields.setting: $M_B$ is the coprime [[pw-moduli|Betti moduli]]. Set $ {}^k\!\operatorname{Hdg}^m=H^m(M_B,\mathbb Q)\cap W_{2k}H^m(M_B,\mathbb C)\cap F^kH^m(M_B,\mathbb C)$.
fields.statement: $$H^m(M_B,\mathbb Q)=\bigoplus_k{}^k\!\operatorname{Hdg}^m.$$ The normalized tautological class $c_k(\gamma)$ has Hodge weight $(k,k)$.
fields.proof: The Chern classes on $B\operatorname{GL}_n$ have weight $(k,k)$; functoriality transfers this to $c_k(\gamma)$. [[pw-tautological|Theorem 2.10]] and multiplicativity of $W,F$ give the decomposition.

fields.setting: $M_B$ is the coprime [[pw-moduli|Betti moduli]], with $D=\dim_\mathbb C M_B$.
fields.statement: There exists $w\in W_4H^2(M_B,\mathbb Q)$ such that $$w^i:\operatorname{Gr}^{W}_{D-2i}H^m(M_B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Gr}^{W}_{D+2i}H^{m+2i}(M_B),\qquad i\ge0.$$
fields.proof: Use a torus stratification of $M_B$ to extend the Lefschetz symmetry of $(\mathbb C^*)^2$.

fields.setting: $M_{\mathrm{Dol}}$ and $M_B$ are the coprime [[pw-moduli|Hitchin and Betti moduli]], with [[pw-tautological|normalized tautological classes]].
fields.statement: $P=W$ holds if and only if every product satisfies $$\prod_jc_{k_j}(\gamma_j)\in P_{\sum_jk_j}H^*(M_{\mathrm{Dol}},\mathbb Q).$$
fields.proof: The product bound gives $W_{2k}\subseteq P_k$. [[pw-mellit|Theorem 2.20]] and [[pw-perverse-filtration|relative hard Lefschetz]] give symmetries about the same middle index, forcing equality.

fields.setting: Fix the coprime [[pw-moduli|Hitchin data]] and $p\in C$. Twisted Higgs fields $\theta:E\to E\otimes\omega_C(p)$ give $$h^p:M^p\to A^p=\bigoplus_{i=1}^nH^0(C,\omega_C(p)^{\otimes i}).$$
fields.statement: The only [[pw-decomposition|support]] of $h^p$ is $A^p$.

fields.text: [[pw-stability|Bridgeland stability]] selects stable complexes. [[pw-hypersurface|Kuznetsov components]] of cubic fourfolds are Calabi–Yau categories of dimension two, and their stable-object moduli give [[pw-hyperkahler-moduli|hyperkähler varieties]].
fields.topics:
[[pw-fourier-mukai|Fourier–Mukai transforms]]
[[pw-sod|Semiorthogonal decompositions]]
[[pw-surface-stability|Stability on surfaces]]
[[pw-cubic-stability|Stability on cubic components]]

fields.setting: $S$ is a smooth projective complex surface.
fields.definition: $S$ is a K3 surface if $\omega_S\cong\mathcal O_S$ and $\pi_1(S)=1$. Smooth quartic surfaces in $\mathbb P^3$ and double covers of $\mathbb P^2$ branched over smooth sextics are examples.

fields.setting: $X$ is a smooth projective complex variety.
fields.definition: $X$ is hyperkähler if $\pi_1(X)=1$ and $H^0(X,\Omega_X^2)=\mathbb C\omega$ for an everywhere nondegenerate holomorphic two-form $\omega$. Examples include [[pw-k3|K3 surfaces]], their Hilbert schemes of points, and Fano varieties of lines on smooth cubic fourfolds.

fields.setting: $X,Y$ are smooth projective complex varieties, $K\in D^b(X\times Y)$, and $p_X,p_Y$ are the projections.
fields.definition: The Fourier–Mukai functor with kernel $K$ is $$\Phi_K(F)=Rp_{Y*}(Lp_X^*F\otimes^{\mathbf L}K).$$ The kernels $\mathcal O_{\Gamma_f}$ and $\mathcal O_\Delta$ give $Rf_*$ and the identity. [[pw-orlov|Theorem 3.7]] represents derived equivalences this way.

fields.setting: $X,Y$ are smooth projective complex varieties.
fields.statement: Every exact $\mathbb C$-linear equivalence $D^b(X)\to D^b(Y)$ is a [[pw-fourier-mukai|Fourier–Mukai functor]] with kernel unique up to isomorphism.
fields.examples: Mukai’s Poincaré transform gives $D^b(A)\simeq D^b(\widehat A)$ for an abelian variety. [[pw-derived-torelli|Theorem 3.9]] characterizes derived equivalence of K3 surfaces.

cards.title: Mukai lattice and Mukai vector of a K3 surface

fields.setting: $S$ is a [[pw-k3|K3 surface]].
fields.definition: The Mukai lattice $$\widetilde H(S,\mathbb Z)=H^0(S,\mathbb Z)\oplus H^2(S,\mathbb Z)\oplus H^4(S,\mathbb Z)$$ has weight two, with $H^0,H^4$ placed in type $(1,1)$, and pairing $$\langle(r,c,s),(r^{\prime},c^{\prime},s^{\prime})\rangle=c\cdot c^{\prime}-rs^{\prime}-r^{\prime}s.$$ The Mukai vector is $v(E)=\operatorname{ch}(E)\sqrt{\operatorname{td}(S)}$, so $\langle v(E),v(F)\rangle=-\chi(E,F)$.

fields.setting: $S,S^{\prime}$ are complex projective [[pw-k3|K3 surfaces]].
fields.statement: $D^b(S)\simeq D^b(S^{\prime})$ if and only if their [[pw-mukai|Mukai lattices]] admit an integral Hodge isometry.
fields.proof: For the reverse implication, realize an isotropic Mukai class as a K3 moduli surface with a universal family. Its Fourier–Mukai transform and classical Torelli identify the surfaces.

fields.setting: $D$ is triangulated, with full triangulated subcategories $\mathcal A_1,\ldots,\mathcal A_n$.
fields.definition: $D=\langle\mathcal A_1,\ldots,\mathcal A_n\rangle$ is a semiorthogonal decomposition if $\operatorname{Hom}(F,G)=0$ for $F\in\mathcal A_i$, $G\in\mathcal A_j$, $i>j$, and every $F$ has a filtration by triangles with successive cones in the $\mathcal A_i$.

fields.setting: $E\in D^b(X)$.
fields.definition: $E$ is exceptional if $$\operatorname{Hom}(E,E)=\mathbb C,\qquad\operatorname{Hom}(E,E[i])=0\quad(i\ne0).$$ Then $V\mapsto V\otimes E$ embeds $D^b(\mathbb C)$ fully faithfully, with image $\langle E\rangle$ and right adjoint $R\operatorname{Hom}(E,-)$.

fields.setting: $\alpha:\mathcal A\hookrightarrow D$ is a full triangulated inclusion.
fields.definition: $\mathcal A$ is right admissible if $\alpha$ has a right adjoint $\alpha^!$, left admissible if it has a left adjoint $\alpha^*$, and admissible if both exist. Components of a semiorthogonal decomposition of $D^b(X)$ for smooth projective $X$ are admissible (Bondal).

fields.setting: $\alpha:\mathcal A\hookrightarrow D$ is [[pw-admissible|right admissible]].
fields.statement: $$D=\langle\mathcal A^\perp,\mathcal A\rangle,\qquad\mathcal A^\perp=\{F:\operatorname{Hom}(E,F)=0\ \forall E\in\mathcal A\}.$$
fields.proof: The counit triangle $\alpha\alpha^!F\to F\to B$ and adjunction give $\operatorname{Hom}(\alpha E,B[i])=0$ for all $E\in\mathcal A$ and $i\in\mathbb Z$, so $B\in\mathcal A^\perp$.

fields.setting: $X$ is smooth projective and $E_1,\ldots,E_n\in D^b(X)$ are [[pw-exceptional|exceptional objects]].
fields.hypotheses: $\operatorname{Ext}^*(E_i,E_j)=0$ for $i>j$.
fields.statement: $$D^b(X)=\langle\operatorname{Ku}(X),E_1,\ldots,E_n\rangle,\qquad\operatorname{Ku}(X)=\langle E_1,\ldots,E_n\rangle^\perp.$$ For a smooth Fano variety with $-K_X=rH$, the line bundles $\mathcal O_X,\ldots,\mathcal O_X((r-1)H)$ form such a collection.
fields.proof: Apply [[pw-admissible-sod|Lemma 3.14]] successively to the right-admissible subcategories $\langle E_i\rangle$.

fields.setting: $\Delta\subset\mathbb P^n\times\mathbb P^n$ is the diagonal.
fields.statement: $$0\to\Omega^n(n)\boxtimes\mathcal O(-n)\to\cdots\to\Omega^1(1)\boxtimes\mathcal O(-1)\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_\Delta\to0$$ is exact.
fields.proof: The section of $T_{\mathbb P^n}(-1)\boxtimes\mathcal O(1)$ sending $(x,y)$ to $\langle y\rangle\to V/\langle x\rangle$ vanishes exactly on $\Delta$. Take its Koszul resolution.

fields.setting: $\mathbb P^n$ is complex projective space.
fields.statement: $$D^b(\mathbb P^n)=\langle\mathcal O,\mathcal O(1),\ldots,\mathcal O(n)\rangle$$ is a full [[pw-sod|semiorthogonal decomposition]].
fields.proof: [[pw-diagonal|Lemma 3.18]] expresses the identity Fourier–Mukai functor using $\mathcal O(-n),\ldots,\mathcal O$. Twist by $\mathcal O(n)$ for the displayed collection.

fields.setting: $D$ is a $\mathbb C$-linear triangulated category with finite-dimensional Hom spaces.
fields.definition: A Serre functor is an autoequivalence $S_D$ with functorial isomorphisms $$\operatorname{Hom}(E,F)^\vee\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,S_D(E)).$$ On a smooth projective $n$-fold, $S_{D^b(X)}=(-)\otimes\omega_X[n]$. It is unique up to isomorphism when it exists.

fields.setting: $D$ is triangulated with [[pw-serre|Serre functor]] $S_D$.
fields.definition: $D$ is Calabi–Yau of dimension $n$ if $S_D=[n]$, and fractional Calabi–Yau of dimension $p/q$ if $S_D^q=[p]$. The relation $S_D^2=[4]$ alone need not imply $S_D=[2]$. For a [[pw-k3|K3 surface]], $D^b(S)$ is Calabi–Yau of dimension two.

fields.setting: $X\subset\mathbb P^n$ is a smooth Fano hypersurface of degree $d\le n$, with $$D^b(X)=\langle\operatorname{Ku}(X),\mathcal O_X,\ldots,\mathcal O_X(n-d)\rangle.$$ Set $c=\gcd(d,n+1)$.
fields.statement: The residual [[pw-serre|Serre functor]] satisfies $$S_{\operatorname{Ku}(X)}^{d/c}=\left[\frac{(n+1)(d-2)}c\right].$$ Thus the component is [[pw-calabi-yau|fractional Calabi–Yau]]. For cubic threefolds, $S^3=[5]$; for cubic fourfolds, $S=[2]$.
fields.proof: For a cubic fourfold, put $\mathcal A=\langle\mathcal O,\mathcal O(1),\mathcal O(2)\rangle$. [[pw-mutation-serre|Proposition 3.31]] gives $S^{-1}=L_{\mathcal A}((-)\otimes\mathcal O(3))[-4]$. Applying this to the divisor triangle $Li^*i_*F\to F\to F(-3)[2]$, the first term is killed by mutation and the last gives $S^{-1}F=F[-2]$.

fields.setting: $\alpha:\mathcal A\hookrightarrow D$ is [[pw-admissible|admissible]].
fields.definition: Left and right mutations are defined by $$\alpha\alpha^!F\to F\to L_{\mathcal A}F,\qquad R_{\mathcal A}F\to F\to\alpha\alpha^*F.$$ Their images lie in $\mathcal A^\perp$ and ${}^\perp\mathcal A$, respectively. For $\mathcal A=\langle E\rangle$, these maps are evaluation from $R\operatorname{Hom}(E,F)\otimes E$ and coevaluation to $R\operatorname{Hom}(F,E)^\vee\otimes E$.

fields.setting: $\mathcal A\subset D$ is admissible.
fields.statement: Both [[pw-mutation|mutation functors]] annihilate $\mathcal A$ and restrict to inverse equivalences between ${}^\perp\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A^\perp$. If $D$ has a Serre functor, $$S_{\mathcal A^\perp}=S_D\circ R_{\mathcal A}|_{\mathcal A^\perp},\qquad S_{\mathcal A^\perp}^{-1}=L_{\mathcal A}\circ S_D^{-1}|_{\mathcal A^\perp}.$$
fields.proof: For the Serre formulas, compose the mutation equivalences with Serre duality between the orthogonals; adjunction verifies the required Hom-duality.

fields.setting: $D$ is triangulated; fix a finite-rank lattice $\Lambda$ and $v:K_0(D)\to\Lambda$.
fields.definition:
A stability condition is a pair $(\mathcal A,Z)$, with $\mathcal A$ the heart of a bounded [[pw-t-structure|$t$-structure]] and $Z:\Lambda\to\mathbb C$ a homomorphism, satisfying:

1. For $0\ne E\in\mathcal A$, $Z(E)$ lies in the upper half-plane or negative real axis. Set $\mu(E)=-\Re Z(E)/\Im Z(E)$, with $\mu=+\infty$ on that axis. Semistability means $\mu(F)\le\mu(E)$ for every nonzero proper subobject $F$.
2. Every object has a finite Harder–Narasimhan filtration with semistable factors of strictly decreasing slope.
3. A quadratic form $Q$ on $\Lambda_\mathbb R$ is negative definite on $\ker Z$ and nonnegative on all semistable classes.

[[pw-stability-space|Theorem 3.35]] describes their deformations.

fields.setting: Fix $(\Lambda,v)$ for the [[pw-stability|stability conditions]] on $D$.
fields.statement: The central-charge map $$\operatorname{Stab}_{\Lambda,v}(D)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda,\mathbb C),\qquad(\mathcal A,Z)\mapsto Z$$ is a local homeomorphism.

fields.setting: $\mathcal A$ is an abelian category.
fields.definition: A torsion pair $(\mathcal T,\mathcal F)$ consists of full subcategories with $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T,\mathcal F)=0$, such that every object fits into $$0\to T_E\to E\to F_E\to0,\qquad T_E\in\mathcal T,\quad F_E\in\mathcal F.$$ Torsion and torsion-free coherent sheaves give an example.

fields.setting: $(\mathcal T,\mathcal F)$ is a [[pw-torsion-pair|torsion pair]] in the heart $\mathcal A$ of a bounded $t$-structure.
fields.statement: The tilted category $$\mathcal A^\sharp=\{E:H_{\mathcal A}^0(E)\in\mathcal T,\ H_{\mathcal A}^{-1}(E)\in\mathcal F,\ H_{\mathcal A}^i(E)=0\text{ for }i\ne-1,0\}$$ is a bounded heart, equal to the extension closure $\langle\mathcal F[1],\mathcal T\rangle$.

fields.setting: $X$ is a smooth projective complex surface with ample $H$. Set $\mu_H=Hc_1/(H^2\operatorname{rk})$ and $\operatorname{ch}^\beta=e^{-\beta H}\operatorname{ch}$.
fields.hypotheses: $\alpha>0$, $\beta\in\mathbb R$. Let $\mathcal T_\beta$ contain torsion sheaves and sheaves with all torsion-free HN slopes $>\beta$, and $\mathcal F_\beta$ the torsion-free sheaves with all HN slopes $\le\beta$.
fields.statement: The tilted heart $\operatorname{coh}^\beta(X)=\langle\mathcal F_\beta[1],\mathcal T_\beta\rangle$ from [[pw-tilted-heart|Lemma 3.39]] and central charge $$Z_{\alpha,\beta}(E)=\frac\alpha2H^2\operatorname{ch}_0^\beta(E)-\operatorname{ch}_2^\beta(E)+iH\operatorname{ch}_1^\beta(E)$$ define a [[pw-stability|stability condition]].
fields.proof: For positivity at $\beta=0$, the torsion pair gives $\Im Z\ge0$. On the boundary, a nonzero zero-dimensional sheaf has charge $-\operatorname{length}<0$, and a shifted slope-zero semistable torsion-free sheaf has negative real charge by Bogomolov’s inequality.

fields.setting: $D=\langle D^{\prime},E_1,\ldots,E_n\rangle$ is an exceptional decomposition, with $D^{\prime}=\langle E_1,\ldots,E_n\rangle^\perp$ and Serre functor $S_D$. Let $(\mathcal A,Z)$ be a {{pw-weak|weak stability condition}}.
fields.hypotheses:
$E_i\in\mathcal A$, $S_D(E_i)\in\mathcal A[1]$, $Z(E_i)
e0$, and $Z(F)
e0$ for every $0
e F\in\mathcal A\cap D^{\prime}$.
fields.statement: $(\mathcal A\cap D^{\prime},Z|_{K_0(D^{\prime})})$ is a stability condition on $D^{\prime}$.
fields.proof: To obtain a bounded heart, take the lowest nonzero $\mathcal A$-cohomology of $F\in D^{\prime}$. Its truncation triangle and Serre duality force all Ext groups from $E_i$ to vanish. Inductively every cohomology object remains in $D^{\prime}$.

notations.pw-weak: A stability-like condition that can allow nonzero objects with zero central charge.

fields.text:
For a smooth cubic threefold $X$, start with $(\operatorname{coh}^{-1/2}(X),Z_{\alpha,-1/2})$. For sufficiently small $\alpha>0$, tilt at slope zero and rotate to $-iZ_{\alpha,-1/2}$. The exceptional objects and their Serre images then satisfy [[pw-restriction|Proposition 3.44]], giving stability on $\operatorname{Ku}(X)$.

For a smooth cubic fourfold, blow up a line and project to $\mathbb P^3$. The conic fibration has an even Clifford algebra sheaf $\mathcal B_0$; the embedding $\operatorname{Ku}(X)\hookrightarrow D^b(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal B_0)$ permits the analogous construction.

fields.setting: $X$ is smooth projective over $\mathbb C$, and $T$ is a finite-type $\mathbb C$-scheme.
fields.definition: A perfect complex is locally a bounded complex of finite-rank vector bundles. Such an $E$ on $X\times T$ is universally gluable over $T$ if $$\operatorname{Ext}^i(E_t,E_t)=0\quad\text{for every geometric }t\in T\text{ and }i<0.$$ The groupoid-valued functor $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pug}}(X)$ assigns these complexes to $T$.

fields.setting: $X$ is a smooth projective complex variety.
fields.statement: The stack [[pw-pug|$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pug}}(X)$]] of perfect universally gluable complexes is algebraic and locally of finite type over $\mathbb C$ (Lieblich).

cards.title: Moduli of stable and semistable objects

fields.setting: Fix a [[pw-stability|stability condition]] $\sigma=(\mathcal A,Z)$ on $D^b(X)$, a class $v\in\Lambda$, and a phase $\phi$ with $Z(v)\in\mathbb R_{>0}e^{i\pi\phi}$. Shifting by $[j]$ increases phase by $j$.
fields.text: The stacks $\mathcal M_\sigma(v)$ and $\mathcal M_\sigma^s(v)$ parametrize perfect families of semistable and stable objects of class $v$ and phase $\phi$. They lie in the algebraic stack $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pug}}(X)$ of [[pw-pug-stack|Theorem 3.51]]. Good moduli spaces identify semistable objects up to {{pw-s-equivalence|S-equivalence}}.

notations.pw-s-equivalence: Semistable objects with the same stable factors, counted with multiplicity.

fields.setting: $X$ is smooth projective over $\mathbb C$, with numerical stability condition $\sigma$. Let $S$ be a proper algebraic space of finite type over $\mathbb C$.
fields.hypotheses: $E$ is a perfect family on $X\times S$ of $\sigma$-semistable objects of fixed nonzero class $v$ and phase.
fields.statement: The numerical divisor defined on projective integral curves $C\subset S$ by $$D_{\sigma,E}\cdot C=\Im\left(-\frac{Z(Rp_{X*}(E|_{X\times C}))}{Z(v)}\right)$$ is nef. Its degree on $C$ is zero exactly when two general fibres over $C$ are {{pw-s-equivalence|S-equivalent}}.

notations.pw-s-equivalence: Semistable objects with the same stable factors, counted with multiplicity.

fields.setting: $f:X\to S$ and $D\subset D_{\mathrm{perf}}(X)$ is a full triangulated subcategory.
fields.definition: $D$ is $S$-linear if $D\otimes Lf^*D_{\mathrm{perf}}(S)\subseteq D$. When $f$ is smooth proper and $D$ is admissible and $S$-linear, $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pug}}(D/S)$ assigns to $T\to S$ the perfect objects of the base-changed category $D_T$ that are universally gluable over $T$.

fields.setting: $f:X\to S$ is smooth proper, with an admissible [[pw-relative-linear|$S$-linear]] semiorthogonal decomposition $D_{\mathrm{perf}}(X)=\langle D_1,\ldots,D_n\rangle$.
fields.statement: Derived base change to $s\in S$ gives $$D_{\mathrm{perf}}(X_s)=\langle D_1|_s,\ldots,D_n|_s\rangle.$$ For every admissible $S$-linear component $D$, $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pug}}(D/S)$ is algebraic and locally of finite type over $S$.

fields.setting: $X$ is a smooth cubic fourfold.
fields.statement: The component $\operatorname{Ku}(X)$ has an integral Mukai lattice $\widetilde H(\operatorname{Ku}(X),\mathbb Z)$ with weight-two Hodge structure and Mukai vector $v:K_0(\operatorname{Ku}(X))\to\widetilde H$, satisfying $$\langle v(E),v(F)\rangle=-\chi(E,F).$$ If $\operatorname{Ku}(X)\simeq D^b(S)$ for a K3 surface, it identifies with [[pw-mukai|$\widetilde H(S,\mathbb Z)$]].

fields.setting: $X$ is a smooth cubic fourfold, with Mukai lattice $\widetilde H(\operatorname{Ku}(X),\mathbb Z)$ from [[pw-cubic-mukai|Proposition 3.58]].
fields.hypotheses: $0\ne v\in\widetilde H_{\mathrm{alg}}(\operatorname{Ku}(X),\mathbb Z)$ is primitive, $\sigma\in\operatorname{Stab}^{\dagger}(\operatorname{Ku}(X))$ is $v$-generic, and $Z(v)\in\mathbb R_{>0}e^{i\pi\phi}$ for a fixed phase $\phi$.
fields.statement: The [[pw-semistable-moduli|moduli space]] $M_\sigma(v)$ is nonempty exactly when $v^2\ge-2$. When nonempty, it is smooth projective of dimension $v^2+2$, deformation-equivalent to $S^{[v^2/2+1]}$ for a K3 surface $S$. It is [[pw-hyperkahler|hyperkähler]] for $v^2\ge0$, and a point for $v^2=-2$. (Bayer–Lahoz–Macrì–Nuer–Perry–Stellari).

fields.setting: $X$ is a smooth cubic fourfold.
fields.statement: There exists a projective [[pw-k3|K3 surface]] $S$ with $\operatorname{Ku}(X)\simeq D^b(S)$ if and only if the algebraic part of its Mukai lattice ([[pw-cubic-mukai|Proposition 3.58]]) contains a hyperbolic plane: $$\begin{pmatrix}\langle u,u\rangle&\langle u,v\rangle\\\langle v,u\rangle&\langle v,v\rangle\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.$$ Addington–Thomas and Bayer–Lahoz–Macrì–Nuer–Perry–Stellari.

fields.setting: $R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, where $k$ is a field.
fields.definition: A **monomial order** is a total order on $x^\alpha$, $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, satisfying $$x^\alpha<x^\beta\Rightarrow x^{\alpha+\gamma}<x^{\beta+\gamma},\qquad 1<x^\alpha\quad(\alpha\ne0).$$ Divisibility implies weak inequality.

fields.text:
For $x^\alpha,x^\beta$ in $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$:

- **Lex:** $x^\alpha>x^\beta$ when the first nonzero entry of $\alpha-\beta$ is positive.
- **Graded lex:** compare total degree first, then lex.
- **Graded reverse lex:** compare total degree first; at equal degree, $x^\alpha>x^\beta$ when the last nonzero entry of $\alpha-\beta$ is negative.

All are [[gb-order|monomial orders]].

fields.setting: $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ has a fixed [[gb-order|monomial order]].
fields.statement: Every nonempty set of monomials has a least element.
fields.proof: The polynomial ring is {{gb-noetherian|Noetherian}}, so the ideal generated by the set is generated by a finite subset. Every original monomial is divisible by one of these generators; the least generator is therefore least in the original set.

notations.gb-noetherian: Ascending chains of ideals eventually stop growing.

fields.setting: $R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ has a fixed [[gb-order|monomial order]].
fields.definition: For $0\ne f\in R$, the **initial term** $\operatorname{in}(f)$ is its largest term, including its coefficient. The **initial ideal** of $I\subset R$ is $$\operatorname{in}(I)=\langle\operatorname{in}(f):0\ne f\in I\rangle.$$ Nonzero scalar coefficients do not affect this monomial ideal.
fields.notation: For monic monomials, $\gcd(x^\alpha,x^\beta)=x^{\min(\alpha,\beta)}$ and $\operatorname{lcm}(x^\alpha,x^\beta)=x^{\max(\alpha,\beta)}$, with coordinatewise minimum and maximum.

fields.setting: $R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ has a fixed [[gb-order|monomial order]] and [[gb-initial|initial term]] notation.
fields.hypotheses: $f_1,\ldots,f_s\in R$ are nonzero.
fields.statement:
Every $f\in R$ admits
$$f=\sum_{i=1}^s q_if_i+r,$$
where no monomial of $r$ is divisible by any $\operatorname{in}(f_i)$, and $\operatorname{in}(q_if_i)\le\operatorname{in}(f)$ whenever $q_if_i\ne0$.
fields.proof: Cancel the leading term using some $f_i$, or move it to $r$ if none applies. The leading monomial strictly decreases, so [[gb-well-order|Lemma 2.2]] gives termination while $f=\sum q_if_i+p+r$ remains invariant.
fields.consequences:
[[gb-standard|Standard monomials and ideal membership]]
[[gb-bad-generators|Why arbitrary generators are insufficient]]

fields.text:
For $I=\langle xy,y^2-x\rangle\subset k[x,y]$, use graded lex order. Then
$$y(xy)-x(y^2-x)=x^2\in I,$$
but $x^2\notin\langle xy,y^2\rangle=\langle\operatorname{in}(xy),\operatorname{in}(y^2-x)\rangle$.
Thus the initial terms of arbitrary generators need not generate [[gb-initial|the initial ideal]]. A [[gb-basis|Gröbner basis]] removes this obstruction.

fields.setting: $I\subset R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, with a fixed [[gb-order|monomial order]].
fields.statement: The monomials outside [[gb-initial|$\operatorname{in}(I)$]] form a $k$-basis of $R/I$. Thus division by a [[gb-basis|Gröbner basis]] has a unique remainder, independent of division choices, and $$f\in I\iff\operatorname{remainder}(f)=0.$$
fields.proof: A nonzero combination of standard monomials cannot lie in $I$, since its leading term would belong to $\operatorname{in}(I)$. By [[gb-well-order|Lemma 2.2]], a least-leading-term counterexample to spanning exists; subtracting its standard leading term, or an element of $I$ with that leading term, contradicts minimality.

fields.setting: $I=\langle x^\alpha:\alpha\in A\rangle\subset k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ is a monomial ideal.
fields.statement: Finitely many monomials from the given set generate $I$.
fields.proof: Induct on $n$. Finite generators after forgetting $x_n$ give a bound $m$ for the last exponent; they handle all exponents at least $m$. Apply induction separately to each of the finitely many slices with last exponent $0,\ldots,m-1$.

fields.setting: $I\subset R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, with a fixed [[gb-order|monomial order]].
fields.definition: A **Gröbner basis** is a finite subset $G=\{g_1,\ldots,g_t\}\subset I\setminus\{0\}$ satisfying $$\operatorname{in}(I)=\langle\operatorname{in}(g_1),\ldots,\operatorname{in}(g_t)\rangle.$$ The empty set is a Gröbner basis of the zero ideal.

fields.setting: $I\subset k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, with a fixed monomial order.
fields.statement: There is a finite [[gb-basis|Gröbner basis]] $G$ of $I$, and $G$ generates $I$ as an ideal.
fields.proof: [[gb-dickson|Theorem 3.1]] gives finitely many generators of $\operatorname{in}(I)$; choose polynomials in $I$ with those initial terms. [[gb-division|Theorem 2.7]] leaves a remainder in $I$ with no monomial in $\operatorname{in}(I)$, forcing it to vanish.

fields.setting: $F=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ is an ordered tuple of nonzero polynomials, with a fixed monomial order.
fields.definition: The **determinate remainder** $\overline f^{\,F}$ is the remainder from [[gb-division|division]] choosing the largest applicable divisor index at each step. For a [[gb-basis|Gröbner basis]], [[gb-standard|Theorem 2.9]] makes it independent of the ordering.

fields.setting: $f,g\in k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ are nonzero, with a fixed monomial order. Let $M$ be the monic least common multiple of their leading monomials.
fields.definition:
The S-polynomial is
$$S(f,g)=\frac{M}{\operatorname{in}(f)}f-\frac{M}{\operatorname{in}(g)}g.$$
Its largest terms cancel, so $S(f,g)=0$ or $\operatorname{in}(S(f,g))<M$.

fields.setting: $p_1,\ldots,p_t\in k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\setminus\{0\}$ have the same leading monomial, with coefficients $d_1,\ldots,d_t\in k^\times$.
fields.hypotheses: The leading terms cancel: $\sum_i d_i=0$.
fields.statement: $$\sum_{i=1}^t p_i=-\sum_{j=2}^t d_j\card{gb-s-polynomial}{S(p_1,p_j)}.$$
fields.proof: Substitute $S(p_1,p_j)=p_1/d_1-p_j/d_j$ and use $\sum_i d_i=0$ to collect the coefficient of $p_1$.

fields.setting: $G=\{g_1,\ldots,g_t\}\subset k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\setminus\{0\}$ generates $I$, with a fixed monomial order.
fields.statement: $G$ is a [[gb-basis|Gröbner basis]] if and only if each [[gb-s-polynomial|S-polynomial]] $S(g_i,g_j)$ has zero [[gb-remainder|remainder]] on division by $G$. It suffices that each pair admit such a reduction to zero.
fields.proof: [[gb-division|Theorem 2.7]] gives the forward implication. Conversely, [[gb-well-order|Lemma 2.2]] lets us minimize the largest summand monomial in $f=\sum f_ug_u$. If the top terms cancel, [[gb-cancellation|Lemma 4.4]] rewrites them using S-polynomials; their zero remainders lower that maximum, a contradiction.

fields.setting: $F$ is a finite tuple of nonzero generators of an ideal in $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, with a fixed monomial order.
fields.statement: Repeatedly append a nonzero remainder $\overline{S(f_i,f_j)}^{\,F}$ until all pairs reduce to zero. This terminates with a [[gb-basis|Gröbner basis]] of the same ideal.
fields.proof: By [[gb-division|Theorem 2.7]], each appended remainder strictly enlarges the ideal of current initial terms. {{gb-noetherian|Noetherianity}} gives termination, and [[gb-criterion|Theorem 4.3]] proves correctness.

notations.gb-noetherian: Ascending chains of ideals eventually stop growing.

fields.setting: $R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\subset S=R[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$.
fields.definition:
An elimination order for the $y$ variables is a [[gb-order|monomial order]] on $S$ such that
$$\operatorname{in}(f)\in R\Longrightarrow f\in R.$$
Lexicographic order with every $y$ variable before every $x$ variable has this property.

fields.setting: $R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\subset S=R[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$, and $I\subset S$.
fields.hypotheses: $G$ is a Gröbner basis of $I$ for an [[gb-elimination-order|elimination order]].
fields.statement: $$G\cap R\quad\text{is a Gröbner basis of}\quad I\cap R.$$
fields.proof: Each initial monomial of $I\cap R$ is divisible by the initial monomial of some $g\in G$. That divisor uses only $x$ variables, so the elimination order forces $g\in R$, proving equality of the initial ideals.
fields.applications:
[[gb-solve|A two-variable system]]
[[gb-algebraic-number|An algebraic-number equation]]
[[gb-projection|Closure of a projection]]

fields.text:
Over $\mathbb C$, consider
$$12x^2-3y=0,\qquad 6xy-10y^2-3y=0.$$
With lex order $x>y$, the first S-polynomial reduces to
$$\frac{25}{9}y^3+\frac{17}{12}y^2+\frac14y.$$
The solutions are
$$(x,y)=(0,0),\quad\left(\frac{3\pm i\sqrt{111}}{40},\frac{-51\pm3i\sqrt{111}}{200}\right),$$
with matching signs.
fields.calculation: Use [[gb-s-polynomial|leading cancellation]] and division to obtain the polynomial in $y$. Solve it and substitute each root into the original equations; the substitution verifies the complete solution set.

fields.text:
Suppose $z^5+\sqrt2z-a^2z+a=0$ and $a^3+a-1=0$. In $\mathbb Q[x,a,z]$, use
$$I=\langle x^2-2,\ a^3+a-1,\ z^5+xz-a^2z+a\rangle.$$
A Gröbner basis for lex order $x>a>z$ gives equations in $I\cap\mathbb Q[z]$ that vanish at $z$.
