fields.calculation: Eliminate $x,a$ using lex order $x>a>z$. The resulting univariate equations have the minimal polynomial as a factor; choose the factor corresponding to the given value of $z$.

fields.setting: $k$ is algebraically closed, $I\subset k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, and $\pi:k^n\to k^m$ projects onto the first $m$ coordinates.
fields.statement: $$\overline{\pi(V(I))}=V(I\cap k[x_1,\ldots,x_m]),$$ where the closure is Zariski closure.
fields.proof: Every eliminated polynomial vanishes on the image. Conversely, if $f$ vanishes on the image, it vanishes on $V(I)$, so the Nullstellensatz gives $f^N\in I\cap k[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$. Taking vanishing sets proves equality.
fields.computation: [[gb-elimination|Proposition 5.1]] computes the ideal on the right.

fields.setting: $I\subset R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$.
fields.hypotheses: $R/I$ is finite-dimensional over $k$.
fields.statement: $$|V_k(I)|\le\dim_k(R/I).$$ If $k$ is algebraically closed, equality holds exactly when $I$ is {{gb-radical|radical}}.
fields.computation: [[gb-standard|Theorem 2.9]] computes the dimension by counting standard monomials.

notations.gb-radical: An ideal containing every polynomial whose power lies in it.

fields.text: The [[vfc-intrinsic-cone|intrinsic normal cone]] records singularities. A [[vfc-pot|perfect obstruction theory]] embeds it in a vector bundle stack; zero-section intersection gives the [[vfc-class|virtual fundamental class]].

fields.setting: $X\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed embedding with ideal $I$.
fields.text: The normal cone is $$C_{X/Y}=\operatorname{Spec}_X\!\left(\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^n/I^{n+1}\right).$$ Its grading gives scaling and a zero section. For a regular embedding, it equals the normal bundle $\operatorname{Spec}_X\operatorname{Sym}(I/I^2)$.

fields.setting: $X$ is a Deligne–Mumford stack. Choose an étale chart $U\to X$ and a closed embedding $U\hookrightarrow V$ into a smooth variety, with ideal $I$.
fields.text: The quotients $$\mathfrak C_X|_U=[\card{vfc-normal-cone}{C_{U/V}}/T_V|_U],\qquad\mathfrak N_X|_U=[N_{U/V}/T_V|_U],\qquad N_{U/V}=\operatorname{Spec}_U\operatorname{Sym}(I/I^2)$$ glue independently of the embedding. They give the intrinsic normal cone $\mathfrak C_X\hookrightarrow\mathfrak N_X=h^1/h^0(L_X^\vee)$, where $L_X$ is the cotangent complex.

fields.setting: $X$ is a Deligne–Mumford stack, with cotangent complex $L_X$.
fields.definition: An obstruction theory is a morphism $\phi:E^\bullet\to L_X$ with $h^0(\phi)$ an isomorphism and $h^{-1}(\phi)$ surjective. It is perfect of amplitude $[-1,0]$ if $E^\bullet$ is locally represented by vector bundles $[E^{-1}\to E^0]$. A global such presentation gives $$\mathfrak E=h^1/h^0((E^\bullet)^\vee)=[(E^{-1})^\vee/(E^0)^\vee],\qquad T^{\mathrm{vir}}=(E^\bullet)^\vee,$$ with a closed embedding $\mathfrak N_X\hookrightarrow\mathfrak E$ of the [[vfc-intrinsic-cone|intrinsic normal sheaf]].

fields.setting: $E^\bullet=[E^{-1}\to E^0]\to L_X$ is a [[vfc-pot|perfect obstruction theory]]. Put $E_1=(E^{-1})^\vee$ and $\mathfrak E=[E_1/(E^0)^\vee]$.
fields.definition: The virtual fundamental class is $$[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}=0^!_{E_1}\bigl[\card{vfc-intrinsic-cone}{\mathfrak C_X}\times_{\mathfrak E}E_1\bigr]\in A_d(X),\qquad d=\operatorname{rk}E^0-\operatorname{rk}E^{-1},$$ where $0^!$ is the zero-section Gysin map and $d$ is the virtual dimension.

fields.text: [[vfc-zero-locus|Zero loci]] realize virtual classes as top Chern classes. For [[vfc-bundles|stable bundles]], Ext groups give tangent and obstruction spaces in [[vfc-deformation|deformation–obstruction theory]].

fields.setting: $Y$ is smooth of dimension $n$, $F\to Y$ has rank $r$, and $X=Z(s)$ for a section $s$. Write $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$.
fields.statement: The section gives a [[vfc-pot|perfect obstruction theory]] $$[F^\vee|_X\xrightarrow{ds}\Omega_Y|_X]\longrightarrow L_X$$ of virtual dimension $n-r$, with $$i_*[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}=c_r(F)\cap[Y].$$ If $s$ is regular, $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}=[X]$.

fields.setting: $D$ is a deformation functor on local Artin $\mathbb C$-algebras, and $T,O$ are finite-dimensional vector spaces.
fields.definition: A deformation–obstruction theory assigns to each small extension $A\twoheadrightarrow B$ with kernel $I$ ($\mathfrak m_AI=0$) a functorial obstruction map $$o:D(B)\to O\otimes_\mathbb C I.$$ An object lifts exactly when its obstruction vanishes; each nonempty set of lifts is a torsor under $T\otimes_\mathbb C I$.

cards.title: Tangent and obstruction spaces of a bundle

fields.setting: $F$ is a stable vector bundle on a smooth projective complex variety $X$.
fields.statement: Its [[vfc-deformation|deformation functor]] has tangent and obstruction spaces $$T=\operatorname{Ext}^1(F,F),\qquad O=\operatorname{Ext}^2(F,F).$$ On a curve, $O=0$ and the stable-bundle moduli space is smooth.
fields.proof: Across a small extension with kernel $I$, the defects of lifted transition maps form a Čech $2$-cocycle in $\mathcal End(F)\otimes I$. Its class in $\operatorname{Ext}^2(F,F)\otimes I$ vanishes exactly when the lifts can be corrected to a gluing. Differences between corrected gluings form the $\operatorname{Ext}^1(F,F)\otimes I$ torsor.

fields.setting: $f:X\to Y$ is of Deligne–Mumford type, with a closed embedding of its relative intrinsic normal cone in a vector bundle stack $\mathfrak E$ of rank $e$.
fields.text: Specialization to the cone, pushforward, and zero-section intersection define $$f^!_{\mathfrak E}:A_k(Y)\to A_{k-e}(X).$$ The construction applies after base change. For a relative perfect obstruction theory of virtual dimension $d$, $e=-d$.

fields.setting: $f:X\to Y$ has a relative [[vfc-pot|perfect obstruction theory]]. In a Cartesian square, write $f^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to Y^{\prime}$, $p:X^{\prime}\to X$, and $q:Y^{\prime}\to Y$.
fields.statement: The base-changed [[vfc-pullback|virtual pullbacks]] commute with proper pushforward and flat pullback: $$f^!q_*=p_*f^{\prime!}\quad(q\text{ proper}),\qquad f^{\prime!}q^*=p^*f^!\quad(q\text{ flat}).$$ They equal the operations induced by the pulled-back obstruction theory (Manolache).

cards.title: Compatible obstruction theories and virtual classes

fields.setting: $f:X\to Y$ has perfect obstruction theories $E_Y^\bullet,E_X^\bullet,E_{X/Y}^\bullet$.
fields.hypotheses: They fit into a distinguished triangle $$f^*E_Y^\bullet\to E_X^\bullet\to E_{X/Y}^\bullet\xrightarrow{+1}$$ compatible with the cotangent-complex triangle.
fields.statement: The [[vfc-pullback|virtual pullback]] satisfies $$[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}=f^!_{E_{X/Y}}[Y]^{\mathrm{vir}}$$ (Manolache, Corollary 4.9).

fields.setting: A torus $T$ acts on a proper Deligne–Mumford moduli space $X$ with a $T$-equivariant [[vfc-pot|perfect obstruction theory]].
fields.statement: Each fixed component $F$ inherits a virtual class, and in localized equivariant Chow groups $$[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}=\sum_Fi_{F*}\frac{[F]^{\mathrm{vir}}}{e_T(N_F^{\mathrm{vir}})}.$$ Here $N_F^{\mathrm{vir}}$ is the moving part of $T^{\mathrm{vir}}|_F$.

cards.title: Oh–Thomas virtual classes on Calabi–Yau fourfolds

fields.setting: $X$ is a smooth projective Calabi–Yau fourfold and $M$ a projective moduli space of Gieseker-stable sheaves of a fixed class, with no strictly semistable sheaves.
fields.text: A three-term [[vfc-self-dual|self-dual obstruction theory]], an {{vfc-orientation|orientation}}, and an isotropic cone give a [[vfc-square-root|square-root virtual class]] of half the complex’s virtual dimension.

notations.vfc-orientation: A compatible choice of square root of the determinant quadratic form.

fields.setting: In the [[vfc-ot|Calabi–Yau fourfold setting]], let $\pi:M\times X\to M$ and assume a universal sheaf $\mathcal F$ exists.
fields.text: The Atiyah class gives $$E^\bullet=R\pi_*R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal F)_0[3]\to L_M,$$ where $0$ denotes the trace-free part. Assume amplitude $[-2,0]$. Serre duality gives $E^\bullet\simeq(E^\bullet)^\vee[2]$. In an oriented self-dual presentation $[T\to E\to T^*]$ in degrees $-2,-1,0$, the middle bundle is orthogonal and the lifted intrinsic normal cone $C\subset E$ is isotropic.

fields.setting: The oriented [[vfc-self-dual|self-dual obstruction theory]] has presentation $[T\to E\to T^*]$, with $\operatorname{rk}E=2r$ and isotropic cone $C\subset E$.
fields.text: The localized square-root Euler operation gives $$[M]^{\mathrm{vir}}=\sqrt{0_E^!}[C]\in A_d(M,\mathbb Z[\tfrac12]),\qquad d=\operatorname{rk}T-r.$$ Oh–Thomas also construct the K-theoretic class $\widehat{\mathcal O}^{\mathrm{vir}}$ using localized square-root Euler classes.

fields.setting: $M$ is proper, and $\tau_M$ is the Riemann–Roch map from coherent-sheaf K-theory to rational Chow groups.
fields.statement: For a [[vfc-pot|perfect obstruction theory]], Fantechi–Göttsche give $$\tau_M(\mathcal O^{\mathrm{vir}})=\operatorname{td}(T^{\mathrm{vir}})\cap[M]^{\mathrm{vir}}.$$ In the [[vfc-ot|oriented Calabi–Yau fourfold setting]], Oh–Thomas give $$\tau_M(\term{vfc-ohat}{\widehat{\mathcal O}^{\mathrm{vir}}})=\sqrt{\operatorname{td}(T^{\mathrm{vir}})}\cap[M]^{\mathrm{vir}},$$ hence for $V\in K^0(M)$, $$\chi(M,V\otimes\widehat{\mathcal O}^{\mathrm{vir}})=\int_{[M]^{\mathrm{vir}}}\operatorname{ch}(V)\sqrt{\operatorname{td}(T^{\mathrm{vir}})}.$$

notations.vfc-ohat: The K-theoretic virtual class constructed with square-root Euler classes.

fields.setting: In the [[vfc-ot|Calabi–Yau fourfold setting]], a torus action preserves the holomorphic volume form and oriented obstruction theory.
fields.hypotheses: The fixed components carry compatible orientations.
fields.statement: In localized rational equivariant Chow groups, $$[M]^{\mathrm{vir}}=\sum_Fi_{F*}\frac{[F]^{\mathrm{vir}}}{\sqrt{e_T}(N_F^{\mathrm{vir}})}.$$ Here $N_F^{\mathrm{vir}}$ is the moving part of the virtual tangent complex, and $\sqrt{e_T}$ is its oriented square-root Euler class.

fields.introduction: Vertex algebras connect graded characters with Poisson varieties and arc spaces.
fields.Topics:
[[ren-moonshine|Moonshine and characters]] · [[ren-vertex-algebra|Vertex algebras]]
[[ren-heisenberg|Heisenberg example]] · [[ren-virasoro|Virasoro examples]] · [[ren-affine|Affine vertex algebras]]
[[ren-associated|Associated variety]] → [[ren-li-filtration|Li filtration]] → [[ren-arc-support|Theorem 1.17 (Singular support)]]

fields.introduction: The moonshine module is a graded Monster representation $V=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}V_n$ with $$\sum_{n\ge0}(\dim V_n)q^{n-1}=j(\tau)-744,\qquad q=e^{2\pi i\tau}.$$
fields.Characters: For a conformal [[ren-vertex-algebra|vertex algebra]] with finite-dimensional graded pieces and central charge $c$, $$\chi_V(q)=\operatorname{tr}_V q^{L_0-c/24}=q^{-c/24}\sum_n(\dim V_n)q^n.$$ Here $V_n$ is the $n$-eigenspace of $L_0$.

fields.setting: $V$ is a complex vector space.
fields.definition:
A vertex algebra structure consists of $\mathbf1\in V$, $T\in\operatorname{End}V$, and a linear assignment of [[ren-local-fields|fields]] $$a\longmapsto Y(a,z)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}a_{(n)}z^{-n-1}$$ satisfying:

- $Y(\mathbf1,z)=\mathrm{id}$ and $Y(a,z)\mathbf1\in a+zV[\![z]\!]$.
- $T\mathbf1=0$ and $[T,Y(a,z)]=Y(Ta,z)=\partial_zY(a,z)$.
- Every pair $Y(a,z),Y(b,w)$ is mutually local.

fields.setting: $V$ is a complex vector space.
fields.definition: A series $a(z)\in(\operatorname{End}V)[\![z,z^{-1}]\!]$ is a field if $a(z)b\in V((z))$ for every $b\in V$. Two fields are mutually local if $$(z-w)^N[a(z),b(w)]=0$$ for some integer $N\ge0$.

fields.setting: $a(z),b(z),c(z)$ are pairwise [[ren-local-fields|mutually local fields]].
fields.statement: The fields $\partial_z a(z)$ and $b(z)$ are mutually local, as are the {{ren-normal-order|normal-ordered product}} $:a(z)b(z):$ and $c(z)$.

notations.ren-normal-order: A product of fields with their singular part removed.

fields.setup: $H=\mathbb C[x_1,x_2,\ldots]$, with $h_{-n}=x_n$, $h_n=n\partial_{x_n}$ for $n>0$, and $h_0=0$. The vacuum is $1$ and $h(z)=\sum_nh_nz^{-n-1}$.
fields.result: With $\deg x_n=n$ and central charge $1$, the [[ren-moonshine|character]] is $$\chi_H(q)=q^{-1/24}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{-1}.$$

Universal Virasoro vertex algebras allow central charge $c$. Their simple quotients at $$c_{u,v}=1-\frac{6(u-v)^2}{uv},\qquad u,v\ge2\text{ coprime},$$ are the minimal models. In the $(2,2r+1)$ family, the [[ren-associated|associated algebra]] is $R_V\simeq\mathbb C[x]/(x^r)$.

fields.setting: $V$ is a vertex algebra.
fields.text: Put $$C_2(V)=\operatorname{span}\{a_{(-2)}b:a,b\in V\},\qquad R_V=V/C_2(V).$$ The operations $\bar a\bar b=\overline{a_{(-1)}b}$ and $\{\bar a,\bar b\}=\overline{a_{(0)}b}$ make $R_V$ a commutative Poisson algebra. If $R_V$ is finitely generated, $$\widetilde X_V=\operatorname{Spec}R_V,\qquad X_V=(\widetilde X_V)_{\mathrm{red}}.$$
fields.Example: For the Heisenberg algebra, $R_H=\mathbb C[x_1]$ with zero bracket.
fields.Topics: [[ren-li-filtration|Li filtration]] · [[ren-quasilisse|Lisse and quasi-lisse]]

cards.title: Li filtration and the arc-space map

fields.setting: $V$ is a vertex algebra with [[ren-associated|associated algebra]] $R_V$. Its Li filtration is $$F^pV=\operatorname{span}\{a^1_{(-n_1-1)}\cdots a^s_{(-n_s-1)}\mathbf1:n_i\ge0,\ \sum n_i\ge p\}.$$
fields.statement: $\operatorname{gr}^F V$ is a differential Poisson algebra generated differentially by $R_V=F^0V/F^1V$. There is a natural surjection $$JR_V\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}^F V,$$ hence a closed embedding $\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{gr}^F V\hookrightarrow J_\infty\widetilde X_V$ into the {{ren-arc|arc space}}.
fields.proof: The universal property of $JR_V$ extends $R_V\to\operatorname{gr}^F V$ to a differential-algebra map; differential generation makes it surjective.

notations.ren-arc: A space whose points are formal curves in the original space.

fields.setup: $\mathfrak g$ is a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra with a nondegenerate invariant symmetric form. Its affine central extension has bracket $$[xt^m,yt^n]=[x,y]t^{m+n}+m(x|y)\delta_{m,-n}K.$$
fields.result: The vacuum module at level $k$ is the universal affine vertex algebra $V^k(\mathfrak g)$, with $$R_{V^k(\mathfrak g)}\simeq\mathbb C[\mathfrak g^*],\qquad \operatorname{gr}^F V^k(\mathfrak g)\simeq J\mathbb C[\mathfrak g^*].$$ Its simple quotients can have smaller [[ren-associated|associated varieties]].

fields.setting: $V$ has finitely generated [[ren-associated|associated algebra]] $R_V$.
fields.definition: $V$ is lisse if $\dim_{\mathbb C}R_V<\infty$; in the connected positively graded case, this is equivalent to $X_V$ being a point. It is quasi-lisse if $X_V$ has finitely many {{ren-leaf|symplectic leaves}}.

notations.ren-leaf: A maximal connected piece on which the Poisson structure is symplectic.

fields.setting: $V$ is a finitely strongly generated, nonnegatively graded vertex algebra with $V_0=\mathbb C\mathbf1$.
fields.hypotheses: $V$ is [[ren-quasilisse|quasi-lisse]].
fields.statement: The natural [[ren-li-filtration|arc-space embedding]] identifies the reduced spaces: $$\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{gr}^F V\bigr)_{\mathrm{red}}\simeq\bigl(J_\infty\widetilde X_V\bigr)_{\mathrm{red}}.$$

fields.introduction: Contractions produce minimal models. Discrepancies measure the resulting singularities; multiplier ideals connect them to vanishing and adjunction.
fields.Topics:
[[ren-surfaces|Minimal surfaces]]
[[ren-discrepancy|Discrepancies]] → [[ren-resolution-test|Testing singularities on a resolution]]
[[ren-multiplier|Multiplier ideals]] → [[ren-multiplier-test|Detecting klt and lc pairs]]
[[ren-vanishing|Vanishing theorems]] · [[ren-adjunction|Inversion of adjunction]]

fields.setting: $S$ is a smooth projective complex surface.
fields.statement: Every $(-1)$-curve contracts to a smooth point, and every birational morphism between smooth projective surfaces factors into point blow-ups. Repeated contraction reaches a minimal surface, which has semiample canonical divisor or is $\mathbb P^2$ or a geometrically ruled surface.
fields.proof: For existence of a minimal model, each contraction lowers the second Betti number, so the process terminates.

fields.setting: $X$ is a normal variety.
fields.definition: A canonical divisor $K_X$ is a Weil divisor restricting to the canonical line bundle $\det\Omega^1_{X_{\mathrm{sm}}}$. It is well defined up to linear equivalence. Its divisor pullback requires $K_X$ to be $\mathbb Q$-Cartier.
A pair $(X,D)$ consists of a normal complex variety $X$ and a $\mathbb Q$-Weil divisor $D$ such that $K_X+D$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier, where $K_X$ is a [[ren-canonical|canonical divisor]].

fields.setting: $(X,D)$ is a [[ren-pair|pair]].
fields.definition: A log resolution is a proper birational map $f:Y\to X$ with $Y$ smooth, divisorial exceptional locus, and $\operatorname{Exc}(f)\cup\operatorname{Supp}\widetilde D$ simple normal crossing. Here $\widetilde D$ is the strict transform; simple normal crossing means locally a union of distinct coordinate hyperplanes.

fields.setting: $(X,D)$ is a [[ren-pair|pair]] and $f:Y\to X$ is a birational model.
fields.definition:
In $$K_Y=f^*(K_X+D)+\sum_Ea(E,X,D)E,$$ the coefficient $a(E,X,D)$ is the discrepancy of $E$. The strict transform of a component $D_i$ with coefficient $d_i$ has discrepancy $-d_i$.

The discrepancy of $(X,D)$ is the infimum over exceptional divisors on all birational models; the total discrepancy includes divisors on $X$.
fields.Topics: [[ren-singularities|Singularity classes]]

fields.setting: $(X,D)$ is an effective [[ren-pair|pair]], with [[ren-discrepancy|discrepancies]] $a(E,X,D)$.
fields.definition:
- klt: $a(E,X,D)>-1$ for every divisor over $X$.
- lc: $a(E,X,D)\ge-1$ for every divisor over $X$.
- plt: every coefficient of $D$ is at most $1$, and every exceptional discrepancy is $>-1$.
- For $D=0$, terminal means every exceptional discrepancy is $>0$; canonical means every exceptional discrepancy is $\ge0$.

fields.setting: $(X,D)$ is an effective [[ren-pair|pair]] and $f:Y\to X$ is a [[ren-log-resolution|log resolution]].
fields.statement: $(X,D)$ is klt or lc iff every exceptional and strict-transform discrepancy on $Y$ is respectively $>-1$ or $\ge-1$. For $(X,0)$, terminality and canonicity are equivalent to the exceptional discrepancies being $>0$ or $\ge0$.
fields.proof: Compare any divisor over $X$ on a common higher resolution. Blowing up a smooth center $Z$ of codimension $c$ gives discrepancy $c-1+\sum_{Z\subset E_i}a_i$. The normal-crossing condition bounds the number of components through $Z$ and preserves the inequalities.

fields.setup: $D=(x^m-y^m=0)\subset\mathbb A^2$ is a union of $m$ distinct lines, and $c\ge0$.
fields.calculation: Blowing up the origin gives $$K_Y=\pi^*(K_{\mathbb A^2}+cD)-c\widetilde D+(1-cm)E.$$
fields.result: $(\mathbb A^2,cD)$ is lc iff $c\le\min(1,2/m)$, and klt iff $c<\min(1,2/m)$.

fields.setting: $X$ is smooth over $\mathbb C$, $D\ge0$ is a $\mathbb Q$-divisor, and $\mu:Y\to X$ is a [[ren-log-resolution|log resolution]].
fields.definition: The multiplier ideal is $$\mathcal I(X,D)=\mu_*\mathcal O_Y\!\left(K_{Y/X}-\lfloor\mu^*D\rfloor\right).$$ It is an ideal subsheaf of $\mathcal O_X$, independent of $\mu$.
fields.Topics: [[ren-multiplier-test|Lemma 2.22]] · [[ren-analytic|Analytic multiplier ideal]]

fields.setting: $X$ is smooth over $\mathbb C$ and $D\ge0$ is a $\mathbb Q$-divisor, with [[ren-multiplier|multiplier ideal]] $\mathcal I(X,D)$.
fields.statement: $$(X,D)\text{ is klt}\iff\mathcal I(X,D)=\mathcal O_X.$$ Also, $(X,D)$ is lc iff $\mathcal I(X,cD)=\mathcal O_X$ for every $0<c<1$.
fields.proof: On a log resolution, the coefficient condition $a_i-\lfloor b_i\rfloor\ge0$ is equivalent to $a_i-b_i>-1$, including strict-transform coefficients. This gives klt; scaling $D$ by $c<1$ gives lc.

fields.setting: $\varphi$ is plurisubharmonic on a complex manifold.
fields.definition: $\mathcal I(\varphi)$ consists of holomorphic germs $g$ with $|g|^2e^{-2\varphi}\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$. For $D=\sum a_iD_i$ with local equations $f_i$, take $\varphi_D=\sum a_i\log|f_i|$; then $$g\in\mathcal I(\varphi_D)\iff\frac{|g|^2}{\prod_i|f_i|^{2a_i}}\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}.$$
fields.Topics: [[ren-comparison|Theorem 2.29]]

fields.setting: $X$ is smooth over $\mathbb C$, and $D=\sum a_iD_i$ is an effective $\mathbb Q$-divisor.
fields.statement: The [[ren-multiplier|algebraic]] and [[ren-analytic|analytic]] multiplier ideals agree: $$\mathcal I(X,D)^{\mathrm{an}}=\mathcal I(\varphi_D).$$
fields.proof: For an SNC divisor $D_i=(z_i=0)$, a monomial $\prod z_i^{m_i}$ is integrable iff $m_i-a_i>-1$, or equivalently $m_i\ge\lfloor a_i\rfloor$. Thus the ideal is $\mathcal O(-\lfloor D\rfloor)$.

fields.setting: $B$ is a $\mathbb Q$-Cartier divisor on a projective variety $X$.
fields.definition: $B$ is nef if $B\cdot C\ge0$ for every integral curve $C$. It is big if $$\limsup_{m\to\infty}\frac{h^0(X,\mathcal O_X(mB))}{m^{\dim X}}>0,$$ with $m$ restricted to sufficiently divisible integers.

fields.introduction: Positivity of an adjoint divisor forces higher cohomology to vanish; multiplier ideals allow singular boundaries.
fields.Topics:
[[ren-kodaira|Kodaira and nef–big vanishing]] → [[ren-kv|Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing]]
[[ren-local-vanishing|Local vanishing]] · [[ren-nadel|Nadel vanishing]]

fields.setting: $X$ is smooth projective over $\mathbb C$, and $B$ is Cartier.
fields.hypotheses: $B$ is [[ren-nef-big|nef and big]].
fields.statement: $$H^i(X,\mathcal O_X(K_X+B))=0\qquad(i>0).$$ The ample case is Kodaira vanishing.

fields.setting: $X$ is smooth projective over $\mathbb C$, and $N$ is Cartier.
fields.hypotheses: $N\equiv B+\Delta$, where $B$ is a nef and big $\mathbb Q$-divisor and $\Delta=\sum a_i\Delta_i$ has simple normal crossing support with $a_i\in\mathbb Q\cap(0,1)$.
fields.statement: $$H^j(X,\mathcal O_X(K_X+N))=0\qquad(j>0).$$
fields.proof: Use [[ren-covering|Lemmas 2.37–2.38]] to remove fractional boundary components by finite and cyclic covers. Induct on their number, starting from [[ren-kodaira|Theorem 2.33]], and descend vanishing by [[ren-trace|Lemma 2.39]].

fields.setting: $X$ is smooth projective over $\mathbb C$, $L$ is a line bundle, and $m>0$ is an integer.
fields.statement:
There is a finite surjection $f:Y\to X$ such that $f^*L$ is an $m$th tensor power.

If a smooth divisor $D$ satisfies $\mathcal O_X(D)=L^{\otimes m}$, its cyclic cover $\gamma:Y\to X$ is smooth, locally given by $u^m=f_D$, and $$\gamma_*\mathcal O_Y=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{m-1}L^{-i}.$$
fields.proof: For the finite-root construction, write $L$ as a quotient of very ample bundles. Pull back their embeddings by $[x_0:\cdots:x_N]\mapsto[x_0^m:\cdots:x_N^m]$ and normalize.

fields.setting: $f:Y\to X$ is a finite surjection of normal complex projective varieties, and $E$ is a vector bundle on $X$.
fields.statement: $$H^j(X,E)\longrightarrow H^j(Y,f^*E)$$ is injective for every $j$.

fields.setting: $X$ is smooth over $\mathbb C$, $D\ge0$ is a $\mathbb Q$-divisor, and $\mu:Y\to X$ is a [[ren-log-resolution|log resolution]].
fields.statement: $$R^i\mu_*\mathcal O_Y\!\left(K_{Y/X}-\lfloor\mu^*D\rfloor\right)=0\qquad(i>0).$$

fields.setting: $X$ is smooth projective over $\mathbb C$, $D\ge0$ is a $\mathbb Q$-divisor, and $L$ is Cartier.
fields.hypotheses: $L-D$ is [[ren-nef-big|nef and big]].
fields.statement: $$H^i\!\left(X,\mathcal O_X(K_X+L)\otimes\mathcal I(X,D)\right)=0\qquad(i>0),$$ where $\mathcal I(X,D)$ is the [[ren-multiplier|multiplier ideal]].

fields.setting: $X$ is normal over $\mathbb C$, $S$ is a normal prime Cartier divisor, and $B\ge0$ is a $\mathbb Q$-divisor not containing $S$.
fields.hypotheses: $K_X+S+B$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier, with adjunction $$(K_X+S+B)|_S=K_S+B_S.$$
fields.statement: $(X,S+B)$ is [[ren-singularities|plt]] near $S$ iff $(S,B_S)$ is [[ren-singularities|klt]].

fields.introduction: Hodge filtrations and Bernstein–Sato polynomials measure hypersurface singularities through multiplier ideals, the minimal exponent, and higher Du Bois and rationality criteria.
fields.Topics:
[[ren-dmodules|D-modules and Riemann–Hilbert]]
[[ren-bfunction|Bernstein–Sato polynomial]] → [[ren-minimal-exponent|Minimal exponent]]
[[ren-vfiltration|V-filtration]] → [[ren-hodge-ideals|Hodge ideals]]
[[ren-du-bois|Du Bois complex]] → [[ren-db-criterion|Theorem 3.21 (Higher Du Bois criterion)]]
[[ren-higher-rational|Theorem 3.24 (Higher rational criterion)]]

fields.setting: $X$ is a smooth complex $n$-fold.
fields.text:
$\mathcal D_X$ is generated by functions and vector fields. Its order filtration gives $\operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_X\simeq\operatorname{Sym}T_X$. For a coherent $\mathcal D_X$-module $M$ with a good filtration, $$\operatorname{Char}(M)=\operatorname{Supp}(\operatorname{gr}M)_{\mathrm{red}}\subset T^*X$$ is independent of the filtration.

Riemann–Hilbert identifies regular holonomic algebraic $\mathcal D_X$-modules with algebraically constructible {{ren-perverse|perverse sheaves}} over $\mathbb C$.
fields.Topics: [[ren-holonomic|Holonomic modules]] · [[ren-characteristic|Theorem 3.1 (Kashiwara)]]

notations.ren-perverse: A constructible complex whose support conditions fit dimensions of strata.

fields.setting: $M$ is a coherent $\mathcal D_X$-module on a smooth complex $n$-fold $X$.
fields.definition: $M$ is holonomic if $M=0$ or its [[ren-dmodules|characteristic variety]] has dimension $n$. Holonomic modules form an abelian category of finite-length objects.
fields.Example: $\mathcal O_X$ is holonomic: its characteristic variety is the zero section of $T^*X$.

fields.setting: $M\ne0$ is a coherent $\mathcal D_X$-module on a smooth complex $n$-fold.
fields.statement: Every irreducible component of its [[ren-dmodules|characteristic variety]] has dimension at least $n$.

fields.setting: $f\ne0$ is regular on a smooth complex variety $X$, with $\partial(f^s)=s(\partial f)f^{s-1}$.
fields.statement: There is a nonzero polynomial $b(s)$ such that $$b(s)f^s\in\mathcal D_X[s]f^{s+1}.$$ The monic generator of all such polynomials is the Bernstein–Sato polynomial $b_f(s)$.
fields.Topics: [[ren-b-roots|Theorem 3.8 and Corollary 3.9]] · [[ren-b-examples|Example 3.5]]

fields.calculation: $$\partial_{x_1}x_1^{s+1}=(s+1)x_1^s,\qquad \sum_i\partial_{x_i}^2f^{s+1}=4(s+1)(s+n/2)f^s.$$ The second identity uses the quadratic $f$.
fields.result: The [[ren-bfunction|Bernstein–Sato polynomial]] is $s+1$ in the first case and divides $(s+1)(s+n/2)$ in the second.

fields.setting: $f$ is nonconstant on a smooth complex variety $X$, with nonempty zero divisor. On a log resolution, write $\pi^*(f=0)=\sum a_iE_i$ and $K_{Y/X}=\sum k_iE_i$.
fields.statement: Every root of [[ren-bfunction|$b_f(s)$]] is a negative rational number of the form $-(k_i+\ell)/a_i$ for some $a_i>0$ and integer $\ell>0$. Its largest root is $-\operatorname{lct}(X,(f=0))$.

fields.setting: $Z=(f=0)$ is a reduced hypersurface in a smooth complex variety, with [[ren-bfunction|Bernstein–Sato polynomial]] $b_f(s)$.
fields.definition: The minimal exponent is $$\widetilde\alpha(Z)=-\max\{\text{roots of }b_f(s)/(s+1)\},$$ with value $\infty$ if the reduced polynomial is $1$. It satisfies $$\operatorname{lct}(X,Z)=\min(1,\widetilde\alpha(Z)).$$
fields.Topics: [[ren-rational|Theorem 3.11 (Saito)]] · [[ren-thom-sebastiani|Theorem 3.18]]

fields.setting: $Z$ is a reduced hypersurface in a smooth complex variety $X$, with [[ren-minimal-exponent|minimal exponent]] $\widetilde\alpha(Z)$.
fields.statement: $Z$ has rational singularities iff $$\widetilde\alpha(Z)>1,$$ equivalently, iff $(X,Z)$ is [[ren-singularities|plt]].

fields.setting: $f\ne0$ is regular on a smooth complex variety $X$. The graph embedding $\iota:X\to X\times\mathbb A^1$ gives $$B_f=\iota_+\mathcal O_X=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}\mathcal O_X\partial_t^j\term{ren-delta}{\delta}.$$
fields.text: The Kashiwara–Malgrange filtration $V^\alpha B_f$ is discrete, decreasing, exhaustive, and rationally indexed. It satisfies $tV^\alpha\subset V^{\alpha+1}$, with equality for $\alpha>0$, and $\partial_tV^\alpha\subset V^{\alpha-1}$; $\partial_tt-\alpha$ acts nilpotently on $\operatorname{gr}_V^\alpha$. Its graded pieces encode nearby and vanishing cycles.
fields.Topics: [[ren-v-roots|Theorem 3.12]] · [[ren-budur-saito|Theorem 3.14 (Budur–Saito)]] · [[ren-local-cohomology|Localization and local cohomology]]

notations.ren-delta: The class $[1/(f-t)]$ representing the graph embedding.

fields.setting: $B_f$ carries the [[ren-vfiltration|V-filtration]]. For $u\in B_f$, let $b_u(s)$ be its {{ren-bsection|section Bernstein polynomial}}, with $s=-\partial_tt$.
fields.statement: $$V^\alpha B_f=\{u:\text{every root of }b_u(s)\text{ is }\le-\alpha\}.$$ In particular, $\delta\in V^\alpha B_f$ iff $\alpha\le\operatorname{lct}(X,(f=0))$.

notations.ren-bsection: The monic polynomial of least degree sending $u$ into $\mathcal D_X\langle s,t\rangle tu$.

fields.setting: $Z=(f=0)$ is an effective divisor on a smooth complex variety $X$, and $B_f$ carries the [[ren-vfiltration|V-filtration]].
fields.hypotheses: $\alpha>0$ and $0<\varepsilon\ll1$.
fields.statement: $$\{g\in\mathcal O_X:g\delta\in V^\alpha B_f\}=\mathcal I(X,(\alpha-\varepsilon)Z),$$ where $\mathcal I$ is the [[ren-multiplier|multiplier ideal]].

fields.setting: $Z$ is a reduced divisor on a smooth complex variety $X$.
fields.text: The localization $\mathcal O_X(*Z)$ underlies a {{ren-mhm|mixed Hodge module}}. Its Hodge filtration lies inside the pole-order filtration and defines the Hodge ideals by $$F_p\mathcal O_X(*Z)=I_p(Z)\otimes\mathcal O_X((p+1)Z)\quad(p\ge0).$$ If $Z$ is smooth, all $I_p(Z)=\mathcal O_X$.
fields.Topics: [[ren-trivial-hodge|Trivial Hodge ideals]] · [[ren-restriction|Theorem 3.17]] · [[ren-local-cohomology|Local cohomology]]

notations.ren-mhm: A package of a D-module, rational perverse sheaf, and Hodge and weight filtrations.

cards.title: Trivial Hodge ideals and the minimal exponent

fields.setting: $Z=(f=0)$ is a reduced hypersurface in smooth $X/\mathbb C$, and $p\ge0$ is an integer. Write $I_p(Z)$ for its [[ren-hodge-ideals|Hodge ideal]] and $\widetilde\alpha(Z)$ for its [[ren-minimal-exponent|minimal exponent]].
fields.statement: $$I_p(Z)=\mathcal O_X\iff\widetilde\alpha(Z)\ge p+1.$$ Also, $I_0(Z)=\mathcal I(X,(1-\varepsilon)Z)$ for $0<\varepsilon\ll1$.
fields.proof: The V-filtration formula $$I_p(Z)=\left\{\sum_{i=0}^pi!h_if^{p-i}:\sum_{i=0}^ph_i\partial_t^i\delta\in V^1B_f\right\}$$ makes triviality equivalent to $\partial_t^p\delta\in V^1B_f$, hence to the minimal-exponent bound. At $p=0$, the same formula gives the multiplier ideal.

fields.setting: $Z$ is a reduced divisor on smooth $X/\mathbb C$, and $H\subset X$ is a smooth divisor.
fields.hypotheses: $Z|_H$ is reduced.
fields.statement: For every integer $k\ge0$, $$I_k(Z|_H)\subseteq I_k(Z)\mathcal O_H.$$ Equality holds for sufficiently general $H$ in a basepoint-free linear system. Here $I_k$ denotes the [[ren-hodge-ideals|Hodge ideal]].

fields.setting: $f,g$ are nonzero regular functions on smooth complex varieties $X,Y$, with $f(p)=g(q)=0$.
fields.statement: For $f+g$ on $X\times Y$, the local [[ren-minimal-exponent|minimal exponents]] satisfy $$\widetilde\alpha_{(p,q)}(f+g)=\widetilde\alpha_p(f)+\widetilde\alpha_q(g).$$

fields.setting: $X$ is a smooth complex $n$-fold.
fields.text:
For a reduced hypersurface $Z=(f=0)$, $$0\to\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X(*Z)\to H_Z^1(\mathcal O_X)\to0$$ is exact as filtered $\mathcal D_X$-modules; local cohomology carries the quotient Hodge filtration.

For any closed embedding $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with complement $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, the localization triangle is $$i_*i^!\mathbb Q_X^H[n]\to\mathbb Q_X^H[n]\to j_*\mathbb Q_U^H[n]\xrightarrow{+1}.$$
fields.Topics: [[ren-hodge-ideals|Hodge ideals]]

fields.setting: $Z$ is a reduced complex variety.
fields.text: The filtered Du Bois complex $(\underline\Omega_Z^\bullet,F)$ has graded pieces $\underline\Omega_Z^p=\operatorname{gr}_F^p\underline\Omega_Z^\bullet[p]$. The canonical maps $\Omega_Z^p\to\underline\Omega_Z^p$ are isomorphisms on $Z_{\mathrm{sm}}$. If $Z$ is proper, $$E_1^{p,q}=\mathbb H^q(Z,\underline\Omega_Z^p)\Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(Z,\mathbb C)$$ degenerates at $E_1$.
fields.Topics: [[ren-steenbrink|Steenbrink’s log-resolution description]] · [[ren-saito-db|Theorem 3.20 (Saito)]] · [[ren-db-criterion|Theorem 3.21]]

fields.setting: $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ embeds a reduced variety in smooth $X/\mathbb C$. Let $\pi:Y\to X$ be a log resolution, isomorphic over $X\setminus Z$, with $E=(\pi^{-1}Z)_{\mathrm{red}}$ SNC.
fields.statement: The [[ren-du-bois|Du Bois complex]] fits into the exact triangle $$R\pi_*\Omega_Y^p(\log E)(-E)\longrightarrow\Omega_X^p\longrightarrow i_*\underline\Omega_Z^p\xrightarrow{+1}.$$
fields.proof: Combine the abstract blow-up triangle with the quotient sequence for differential forms on $E$, then apply the octahedral axiom.

fields.setting: $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a reduced closed subvariety of smooth $X/\mathbb C$ of dimension $n$.
fields.statement: The [[ren-du-bois|Du Bois complex]] satisfies $$i_*\underline\Omega_Z^p\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}\!\left(\operatorname{gr}_{p-n}^{F}\operatorname{DR}_X(i_*i^!\mathbb Q_X^H[n]),\omega_X\right)[p].$$
fields.proof: Apply graded de Rham and duality to the localization triangle. Proper pushforward identifies the complement term with logarithmic forms on a resolution; [[ren-steenbrink|Steenbrink’s triangle]] identifies the remaining term.

fields.setting: $Z$ is a reduced hypersurface in a smooth complex variety, and $p\ge0$ is an integer.
fields.statement: $$\widetilde\alpha(Z)\ge p+1\iff\Omega_Z^i\longrightarrow\underline\Omega_Z^i\text{ is a quasi-isomorphism for all }0\le i\le p.$$ The right side defines $p$-Du Bois singularities. For $p=0$, it identifies Du Bois hypersurfaces with log canonical ambient pairs.
fields.proof: For the forward implication, the minimal-exponent bound makes the Hodge filtration agree with pole order through degree $p$. [[ren-saito-db|Theorem 3.20 (Saito)]] then yields a truncated Koszul complex. [[ren-codimension|Lemma 3.22]] forces its negative-degree cohomology to vanish, leaving $\Omega_Z^i$.

fields.setting: $Z$ is a reduced hypersurface in a smooth complex variety, with [[ren-minimal-exponent|minimal exponent]] $\widetilde\alpha(Z)$, and $p\ge0$ is an integer.
fields.statement: $$\widetilde\alpha(Z)\ge p+1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{codim}_Z Z_{\mathrm{sing}}\ge2p+1.$$
fields.proof: A general transverse slice preserves the minimal-exponent bound and reduces to an isolated hypersurface singularity. In ambient dimension $m$, the bound $\widetilde\alpha\le m/2$ gives $m\ge2p+2$, hence the claimed codimension.

fields.setting: $Z$ is a reduced hypersurface in a smooth complex variety, with [[ren-minimal-exponent|minimal exponent]] $\widetilde\alpha(Z)$, and $p\ge0$ is an integer.
fields.statement: $Z$ has {{ren-higher-rational|$p$-rational singularities}} iff $$\widetilde\alpha(Z)>p+1.$$ Consequently, for $p\ge1$, $$p\text{-rational}\ \Longrightarrow\ \card{ren-db-criterion}{p\text{-Du Bois}}\ \Longrightarrow\ (p-1)\text{-rational}.$$

notations.ren-higher-rational: Rationality strengthened to control differential forms through degree $p$.
